The zero axis is a line of 2 drawn over the bars, so a bar stands on it and a negative
one hangs from it.

### Axes and grid

`hasGrid`, `hasXAxis`, `hasYAxis`, `tickCount`, `xLabelCount`, `formatX`, `formatY` and
`hasZeroBaseline` are the chart family's shared props, as on the `LineChart`.

## Sizes

```tsx
<BarChart size="sm" data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['units']} />
<BarChart size="md" data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['units']} />
<BarChart size="lg" data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['units']} />
```

`size` is the plot's height — 140, 200 or 280 — never its width, which is the parent's.

## Colour

The palette is walked out of one colour, a shade per series. `accent` picks one of the
twenty named Metro accents — the intents are `green`, `amber` and `red` — and `color`
takes a raw tint and wins when both are set. Inside a `Chart`, the frame's appearance is
the default.

```tsx
<Chart seriesCount={2} accent="violet">
  <Chart.Header>
    <Chart.Legend labels={['wi-fi', 'mobile']} />
  </Chart.Header>
  <BarChart data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['wifi', 'mobile']} />
</Chart>
```

`isDisabled` dims the plot.

## Accessibility

- The plot is a plain `View` with no role. Its `View` props are passed through: give it
  `accessible` and an `accessibilityLabel` that says what the figure shows.
- A `Chart.Title` in the frame is a `header` to a screen reader.

## Differences from Native

- **`radius`** defaults to 0 and is held at 2; Native's default is a third of the bar, a
  capsule.
- **`accent`** replaces `variant`: the palette's seed is one of the twenty named accents,
  the intents being `green`, `amber` and `red`.

# BottomSheet — @xaui/tram

A surface that comes up from the bottom edge and can be thrown back down, drawn as the
Metro sheet: a band the full width of the screen in the theme's contrast — white on the
dark theme, black on the light one — over the page dimmed, with no line, no shadow and no
corner.

The band has one height, its content's. It rises on the Metro curve and is dragged back
down. What is put on it reads the theme's other mode, so a field or an `outline` `Button`
on the band draws in the band's ink with nothing said.

## Import

```tsx
import { BottomSheet } from '@xaui/tram/bottom-sheet'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet.Trigger />
  <BottomSheet.Overlay />
  <BottomSheet.Content>
    <BottomSheet.Title />
    <BottomSheet.Close />
    <BottomSheet.Description />
  </BottomSheet.Content>
</BottomSheet>
```

- **`BottomSheet`** — the root. It renders no node: it holds whether the band is up, its
  motion and the styles the slots read.
- **`BottomSheet.Trigger`** — what brings the band up. It paints nothing of its own:
  `asChild` makes it a `Button`; a string is set in `body`.
- **`BottomSheet.Overlay`** — the dimmed page behind the band. A touch on it closes the
  sheet unless `isDismissable` is off.
- **`BottomSheet.Content`** — the band. It measures its own height and slides that far,
  and its bottom padding takes the safe area handed to `TramProvider`.
- **`BottomSheet.Title`** — the heading.
- **`BottomSheet.Description`** — the text under it.
- **`BottomSheet.Close`** — anything that sends the band down. Left empty, it is the
  `CloseButton`'s cross without its circle, pinned in the band's top-end corner.
  `asChild` makes it one of your buttons: the caller's `onPress` runs, then the band goes.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<BottomSheet>
  <BottomSheet.Trigger asChild>
    <Button>share</Button>
  </BottomSheet.Trigger>
  <BottomSheet.Overlay />
  <BottomSheet.Content>
    <BottomSheet.Title>share</BottomSheet.Title>
    <BottomSheet.Close accessibilityLabel="close" />
    <BottomSheet.Description>a read-only link.</BottomSheet.Description>
  </BottomSheet.Content>
</BottomSheet>
```

### Answers on the band

```tsx
<BottomSheet.Close asChild>
  <Button>add to cart</Button>
</BottomSheet.Close>
<BottomSheet.Close asChild>
  <Button variant="outline">later</Button>
</BottomSheet.Close>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<BottomSheet isOpen={isOpen} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <BottomSheet.Overlay />
  <BottomSheet.Content>…</BottomSheet.Content>
</BottomSheet>
```

### One that has to be answered

```tsx
<BottomSheet.Overlay isDismissable={false} />
<BottomSheet.Content isSwipeable={false}>…</BottomSheet.Content>
```

`isDismissable={false}` stops a touch on the dimmed page and the system's back from
closing it; `isSwipeable={false}` stops the drag.

### The drag

A decisive drag down sends the band away; anything else springs it back.
`dismissThreshold` is how far down it has to be dragged before letting go closes it, as a
fraction of its height — `0.35` by default. The pan is `react-native-gesture-handler`'s,
an optional peer.

`isDisabled` greys the trigger, which then opens nothing.

## Accessibility

- The band is a modal dialog (`accessibilityViewIsModal`, `role="dialog"`), named by its
  title and described by its description. A screen reader stops at it, and the focus
  moves to it as it opens and back to the trigger once it has gone.
- The trigger carries `expanded` and `aria-haspopup="dialog"`; the title is a `header`.
- An empty `BottomSheet.Close` needs an `accessibilityLabel` — the cross is not text.
- The band is a `Modal`, so the system's back closes it unless the overlay is not
  dismissable.
- It rises in 250 ms on the Metro curve and sinks on the exit curve; with motion reduced
  it fades.

## Differences from Native

- **One height, the content's**: no `Handle`, no `Summary`, no `collapsedHeight` or
  `isExpanded` — the head is the title and an empty `Close`.
- **`BottomSheet.Close`** left empty draws the cross in the top-end corner, where
  Native's draws nothing.
- **The band** is the theme's contrast, edge to edge, with no corner and no shadow; what
  is put on it reads the theme's other mode.
- **`radius`** is kept so the two roots take the same props, and draws nothing.
- **It is a `Modal`**, as the Tram `Dialog`, where Native's is drawn in a portal: it keeps
  the theme it was written under and covers the navigation.

# Button — @xaui/tram

A control that runs an action when it is pressed, drawn the Metro way: a flat rectangle in
one accent colour, square corners, and a press that tilts the button toward the finger
instead of changing its colour.

## Import

```tsx
import { Button } from '@xaui/tram/button'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Button>
  <Button.Spinner />
  <Button.Icon />
  <Button.Label />
</Button>
```

- **`Button`** — the root. It resolves the recipe once and hands the resolved styles to its
  slots. String children are wrapped in a `Button.Label` for you.
- **`Button.Label`** — the text, on one line. A Tram label keeps the case you write: the
  lower-case Metro look is the app's choice, not the component's.
- **`Button.Icon`** — an icon in the variant's colour, at the size's scale. It takes
  `Icon`'s three forms: `as`, a raw SVG child, or `source`.
- **`Button.Spinner`** — the busy indicator. `isLoading` inserts one when none is composed.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Button onPress={save}>save</Button>
```

### Composed

JSX order is screen order. No slot carries a margin: the gap belongs to the root.

```tsx
<Button variant="outline">
  <Button.Icon as={TrashIcon} />
  <Button.Label>delete</Button.Label>
</Button>
```

### Icon only

```tsx
<Button isIconOnly accessibilityLabel="Delete">
  <Button.Icon as={TrashIcon} />
</Button>
```

`isIconOnly` drops the horizontal padding and squares the button on its fixed height.

### Loading

```tsx
<Button isLoading>sending…</Button>
```

A loading button is not pressable, and announces as busy rather than as disabled.

## Variants

Four ways to draw one rectangle, all in the accent:

| Variant     | Drawn as                         |
| ----------- | -------------------------------- |
| `contained` | filled with the true colour      |
| `flat`      | filled with its soft slice       |
| `outline`   | a line and a label in the colour |
| `text`      | the label alone                  |

```tsx
<Button variant="contained">contained</Button>
<Button variant="flat">flat</Button>
<Button variant="outline">outline</Button>
<Button variant="text">text</Button>
```

None changes colour under the finger: the press is the tilt.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Button size="sm">sm</Button>
<Button size="md">md</Button>
<Button size="lg">lg</Button>
```

`size` drives height, padding, gap and type — never width. Every size keeps a 48-point
touch target.

## Colour

The colour is the theme's accent. `accent` picks another one of the twenty named Metro
accents; `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins when both are set. The label on a filled
button is black or white, whichever reads (`onAccent`); a colour drawn as a line or as text
is darkened or lightened until it reads on the page (`accentInk`).

```tsx
<Button accent="magenta">magenta</Button>
<Button variant="outline" color={theme.colors.danger}>delete</Button>
```

## Accessibility

- The root has the `button` role; a disabled or loading button announces its state.
- An icon-only button needs an `accessibilityLabel` — there is no text to read.
- The press tilt follows reduced motion: with motion reduced it is a short 150 ms timing
  instead of the `press` spring.

## Differences from Native

- **`variant`** is `contained`, `flat`, `outline` or `text` — how the box is drawn. Native's
  ladder (`primary`, `default`, `danger`…) mixes emphasis and intention; Tram has one colour
  to spend, so a destructive button is `color={theme.colors.danger}`.
- **`accent`** is added: one of the twenty named accents.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **The press** tilts the button toward the finger and leaves its colours alone; Native
  dims or scales it.
- **The corner** stays within 2, the Tram radius scale.

# Calendar — @xaui/tram

A month, and the day chosen in it, drawn as the Windows calendar: a light title at the
start, two bare chevrons at the end pointing up and down, and a grid of flat squares — the
chosen one in the accent, today lined in the ink.

The months page up and down: the next month rises from below and the one before drops in
from above. The month on screen, the chosen day and the panel are three pieces of state,
each controllable without the others.

## Import

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@xaui/tram/calendar'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Calendar>
  <Calendar.Header>
    <Calendar.Title />
    <Calendar.PreviousButton />
    <Calendar.NextButton />
  </Calendar.Header>
  <Calendar.Weekdays />
  <Calendar.Grid>
    <Calendar.Day />
  </Calendar.Grid>
  <Calendar.MonthPicker />
  <Calendar.YearPicker />
</Calendar>
```

- **`Calendar`** — the root. It holds the chosen day, the month on screen and the panel.
- **`Calendar.Header`** — the row over the grid.
- **`Calendar.Title`** — the month on screen, named through the locale, on `title`
  SemiLight. On the year and month panels it is the year alone. Children replace it.
- **`Calendar.PreviousButton`** / **`Calendar.NextButton`** — the chevrons, up and down.
  `step` is how many months a press moves; on the year and month panels they step a year.
  Children replace the chevron.
- **`Calendar.Weekdays`** — seven two-letter headings in the ink.
- **`Calendar.Grid`** — six weeks of the month on screen, always six, so nothing under it
  moves between months. A function child renders each day.
- **`Calendar.Day`** — one square. A day of another month is grey and still choosable;
  one out of bounds is the faint grey and inert.
- **`Calendar.MonthPicker`** — the twelve months, three to a row, rendered instead of the
  weekdays and the grid while `view` is `'month'`. `format` is `'short'` or `'long'`.
- **`Calendar.YearPicker`** — the years, three to a row in a scroll, rendered while `view`
  is `'year'`. `firstYear` and `lastYear` bound the list.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Calendar value={date} onValueChange={setDate}>
  <Calendar.Header>
    <Calendar.Title />
    <View style={{ flexDirection: 'row' }}>
      <Calendar.PreviousButton accessibilityLabel="previous month" />
      <Calendar.NextButton accessibilityLabel="next month" />
    </View>
  </Calendar.Header>
  <Calendar.Weekdays />
  <Calendar.Grid />
</Calendar>
```

`onValueChange` fires with the pressed day at midnight local time.

### Bounds and locale

```tsx
<Calendar minValue={today} maxValue={nextYear} locale="fr-FR">
  …
</Calendar>
```

Days outside the bounds are inert. `locale` names the months and the weekdays and, unless
`firstDayOfWeek` is set, decides which day a week starts on.

### Months and years

```tsx
<Calendar view={view} onViewChange={setView}>
  <Calendar.Header>
    <Calendar.Title
      onPress={() => setView(v => (v === 'grid' ? 'month' : 'year'))}
    />
    …
  </Calendar.Header>
  {view === 'grid' ? (
    <>
      <Calendar.Weekdays />
      <Calendar.Grid />
    </>
  ) : view === 'month' ? (
    <Calendar.MonthPicker />
  ) : (
    <Calendar.YearPicker style={{ maxHeight: 290 }} />
  )}
</Calendar>
```

Pressing a year goes on to its months; pressing a month lays the calendar on it and goes
back to the days. `month`, `defaultMonth` and `onMonthChange` control the month on screen.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Calendar size="sm">…</Calendar>
<Calendar size="md">…</Calendar>
<Calendar size="lg">…</Calendar>
```

Cells 36, 42 or 48 tall, and the type in them. The grid spans its parent; the squares
touch across and stand 2 apart down.

## Colour

The chosen day is the accent's flat square with its number in the ink that reads on it.
`accent` picks one of the twenty named accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins.

```tsx
<Calendar accent="lime" defaultValue={today}>
  …
</Calendar>
```

`isDisabled` greys the calendar and stops every day.

## Accessibility

- A day is a `button` labelled with its full date, carrying `selected` and `disabled`.
  The weekday headings are hidden from screen readers.
- The title is a `header`. The chevrons are `button`s; their `accessibilityLabel` is the
  caller's.
- A month or a year on the panels is a `button` carrying `selected` and `disabled`.
- A press shrinks the cell and a choice is felt as a `selection` haptic.
- The months move 32 points on the Metro curve while they fade in; with motion reduced
  they only fade.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`**, **no `radius`**: the chosen day is the accent's flat square, and a
  Tram cell has no corner.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **No `asChild`** on the root.
- **No today dot**: today is a square lined at 2 in the ink.
- **The months page up and down**, and the chevrons point up and down.
- **The arithmetic** is Native's, public from its root: `monthGrid`, `isSameDay`,
  `isSameMonth`, `isWithinBounds`, `startOfDay`, `firstDayOfWeekFor`, `weekdayNames`,
  `monthLabel`, `monthNames`.

# Card — @xaui/tram

A surface that groups related content, drawn as Tram asks: the discreet surface with no
line and no shadow, the content separated by space and type — a title on the Tram scale
over a detail faded under it, the actions in a row.

With `isPressable` it is the control that opens what it shows, and it leans toward the
finger as the Tram `Button` does, with no highlight.

## Import

```tsx
import { Card } from '@xaui/tram/card'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Card>
  <Card.Background />
  <Card.Header>
    <Card.Title />
    <Card.Description />
  </Card.Header>
  <Card.Body />
  <Card.Footer />
</Card>
```

- **`Card`** — the surface. It resolves the recipe once and hands the styles to its
  slots. A stringifiable child is wrapped in a `Card.Description`.
- **`Card.Background`** — a photo (`source`) or anything already positioned, across the
  whole card under its text. The root paints it first wherever it is written, clipped to
  the card's corner.
- **`Card.Header`** — the top of the card: its title and what describes it, in a column.
- **`Card.Body`** — the content.
- **`Card.Footer`** — the actions, in a row: the space between them is their only frame.
- **`Card.Title`** — the heading, on `body`, `subtitle` or `title` with the size. It wraps.
- **`Card.Description`** — the detail, in the title's ink faded to `muted`.

No slot carries a margin: the gap belongs to the root, so JSX order is screen order.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Card>
  <Card.Header>
    <Card.Title>night market</Card.Title>
    <Card.Description>tonight, 9 pm</Card.Description>
  </Card.Header>
  <Card.Footer>
    <Button variant="outline" size="sm">
      going
    </Button>
  </Card.Footer>
</Card>
```

### Pressable

```tsx
<Card isPressable onPress={open}>
  <Card.Title>invoice #1024</Card.Title>
</Card>
```

`isPressable` is a prop, not read off `onPress`: the two are different elements. A press
handler without it warns in development. `asChild` makes the caller's element the card.

### Background

```tsx
<Card variant="ghost" style={{ minHeight: 180, justifyContent: 'flex-end' }}>
  <Card.Background source={{ uri: cover }} />
  <Card.Title>marrakech</Card.Title>
</Card>
```

## Variants

Native's names, each saying how much ground the card has:

| Variant     | Drawn as                                          |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`   | the discreet surface, no line, no shadow          |
| `secondary` | the next grey, for a card inside a card           |
| `tertiary`  | the page inside the theme's line                  |
| `ghost`     | nothing: the content on the page, Metro's own way |

```tsx
<Card variant="secondary">…</Card>
```

## Sizes

```tsx
<Card size="sm">…</Card>
<Card size="md">…</Card>
<Card size="lg">…</Card>
```

`size` drives the padding, the gaps, and the type of the title and description — never a
height.

## Colour

`accent` picks one of the twenty named accents. It fills a `default` or a `secondary`
card with its true colour, the title in the ink that reads on it; on a `tertiary` it is
the line, and on a `ghost` the title, both as the mode's ink. `color` takes a raw tint,
lands where `accent` does, and wins.

```tsx
<Card accent="cobalt">…</Card>
```

`isDisabled` dims the card and, on a pressable one, stops the touch.

## Accessibility

- A static card has no role: the text inside it is what a screen reader reads.
- A pressable card is a `button` by default, its `disabled` state merged with any you pass.
- A pressable card is one target: put the actions in the footer of a static card rather
  than nesting buttons in a pressable one.
- The press is felt through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`. The tilt runs on the `press`
  spring, or fades with motion reduced; under `disable-all` the card does not move.

## Differences from Native

- **No line and no shadow**: `default` is the discreet surface, and `ghost` is the
  content on the page.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **The press** leans the card toward the finger and changes no colour; Native scales it
  and lays a wash over it.
- **The corner** stays within 2, the Tram radius scale.
- **`Card.Background`** is marked with Native's symbol (`Symbol.for`), shared by the two
  packages.

# Carousel — @xaui/tram

A series of slides, one or a few at a time, drawn in Metro: the slides are the caller's
and nothing paints them; the arrows are squares of the page's ground; the indicator is a
row of squares whose current one stretches into a bar of the accent.

Every move goes through the index — an arrow, a square, a thumbnail, autoplay or a
controlled parent — and the track glides to it on the Metro curve.

## Import

```tsx
import { Carousel } from '@xaui/tram/carousel'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Carousel>
  <Carousel.Content>
    <Carousel.Item />
  </Carousel.Content>
  <Carousel.Previous />
  <Carousel.Next />
  <Carousel.Indicator>
    <Carousel.Dot />
  </Carousel.Indicator>
  <Carousel.Counter />
  <Carousel.Thumbnails>
    <Carousel.Thumbnail />
  </Carousel.Thumbnails>
</Carousel>
```

- **`Carousel`** — the root. It holds the index and measures the track.
- **`Carousel.Content`** — the track, a `ScrollView` that snaps a slide at a time. It
  counts its children; your `onScroll` and `contentContainerStyle` are composed with its own.
- **`Carousel.Item`** — one slide. Its width is the track's, divided by `itemsPerView`
  less the gaps and the peeks; its height is what is inside it. It clips.
- **`Carousel.Previous`** / **`Carousel.Next`** — the arrows: squares the size of a key,
  8 in from the track's edge and centred on its height, a chevron of 2 in the ink.
  Children replace the chevron.
- **`Carousel.Indicator`** — the row of squares, held to the start. With no children it
  draws one `Carousel.Dot` per slide.
- **`Carousel.Dot`** — one square, which stretches into a bar of the accent as its slide
  comes into view. `index` is the slide it stands for.
- **`Carousel.Counter`** — `3 / 12` in tabular `body`, the total muted. Children replace it.
- **`Carousel.Thumbnails`** — a strip of thumbnails, a horizontal `ScrollView`.
- **`Carousel.Thumbnail`** — a square the size of a key, ringed; the current one's ring
  is a line of 2 in the ink. `index` is the slide it goes to.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Carousel autoPlayInterval={3200}>
  <Carousel.Content>
    {photos.map(photo => (
      <Carousel.Item key={photo.id}>
        <Image source={photo.source} style={{ width: '100%', height: 176 }} />
      </Carousel.Item>
    ))}
  </Carousel.Content>
  <Carousel.Previous accessibilityLabel="previous photo" />
  <Carousel.Next accessibilityLabel="next photo" />
  <Carousel.Indicator />
</Carousel>
```

### Peek, counter and thumbnails

```tsx
<Carousel peek={32}>
  <Carousel.Content>…</Carousel.Content>
  <Carousel.Counter />
  <Carousel.Thumbnails>
    {photos.map((photo, at) => (
      <Carousel.Thumbnail key={photo.id} index={at}>
        <Image source={photo.source} style={{ width: '100%', height: '100%' }} />
      </Carousel.Thumbnail>
    ))}
  </Carousel.Thumbnails>
</Carousel>
```

### Several in view, looping

```tsx
<Carousel itemsPerView={2} hasLoop>
  …
</Carousel>
```

Without `hasLoop`, the arrow at an end of the series stays in place, its chevron in the
faint grey, disabled.

### Controlled

```tsx
<Carousel index={index} onIndexChange={setIndex}>
  …
</Carousel>
```

`defaultIndex` places the track without animation. `autoPlayInterval` advances every so
many milliseconds; it always wraps and stops at the first interaction for good.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Carousel size="sm">…</Carousel>
<Carousel size="md">…</Carousel>
<Carousel size="lg">…</Carousel>
```

`size` sets the arrows' and thumbnails' key (32, 40, 48), the indicator's squares (6, 8
or 10) and the gap between slides (8, 12, 16) — never a slide. `gap` overrides the last.

## Colour

The indicator's bar is the one thing in a colour. `accent` picks one of the twenty named
accents for it; `color` takes a raw tint, wins, and reaches only the bar.

```tsx
<Carousel accent="lime">…</Carousel>
```

`radius` rounds the slides and thumbnails, within 2; unset, they are square.

## Accessibility

- The arrows are `button`s and need an `accessibilityLabel` — a development warning says
  so. At an end of a non-looping series they carry `disabled`.
- A square and a thumbnail are `button`s carrying `selected`, and read `3/5` through
  `accessibilityValue`. What is in a slide or thumbnail is yours to label.
- Arrows reach 48 all round; squares and thumbnails reach 48 above and below.
- Arrows and thumbnails tilt; a `press` haptic is felt on an arrow and a `selection` on a
  square or a thumbnail.
- The glide runs on the Metro curve; with motion reduced the track jumps.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`**: Native's four only paint the arrows' ground; Tram keeps one, the page's.
- **`accent`** is added for the bar; `color` wins over it and reaches only the bar.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **`radius`** stays within 2, slides and thumbnails square when unset; Native's is `2xl`.
- **The indicator**: Native's round dots and pill are squares and a bar.

# Charts — @xaui/tram

The words around a figure — a title, a description, a value and a legend — and the plot
the cartesian charts share. Tram draws the frame with **no shell**: no ground, no padding,
no line and no corner, so the figure sits on the page as Metro's figures did.

A caller who wants a card puts the frame in a Tram `Card`. The figures themselves are
their own pages: `LineChart`, `AreaChart`, `BarChart`, `PieChart`, `RadarChart` and
`RadialChart`.

## Import

```tsx
import { Chart, ChartPlot } from '@xaui/tram/chart'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Chart>
  <Chart.Header>
    <Chart.Heading>
      <Chart.Title />
      <Chart.Description />
      <Chart.Value />
    </Chart.Heading>
    <Chart.Legend>
      <Chart.LegendItem />
    </Chart.Legend>
  </Chart.Header>
  {/* a figure */}
  <Chart.Footer />
</Chart>
```

- **`Chart`** — the frame, and the palette everything in it shares. `accent`, `size` and
  `color` are handed down to the legend and the figure.
- **`Chart.Header`** — the row above the figure, pushed apart and wrapping: a long title
  keeps the row and the legend drops under it.
- **`Chart.Heading`** — the title, its description and a value, as one block.
- **`Chart.Title`** — what the figure is, on `title` Light.
- **`Chart.Description`** — what it measures, on `caption` in the muted ink.
- **`Chart.Value`** — the one number it is about, on `section` Light in tabular figures.
- **`Chart.Legend`** — which colour is which series. `labels` is the short form; children
  are the long one.
- **`Chart.LegendItem`** — one entry: a square of 10 in the series' colour, and its name
  on `caption`. `index` picks the series; `color` gives an entry its own.
- **`Chart.Footer`** — the row under the figure. It wraps.

## Usage

### A frame around a figure

```tsx
<Chart seriesCount={2} accent="cobalt">
  <Chart.Header>
    <Chart.Heading>
      <Chart.Title>data</Chart.Title>
      <Chart.Description>GB per month</Chart.Description>
      <Chart.Value>26 GB</Chart.Value>
    </Chart.Heading>
    <Chart.Legend labels={['wi-fi', 'mobile']} />
  </Chart.Header>
  <LineChart data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['wifi', 'mobile']} />
  <Chart.Footer>
    <Chart.Description>last twelve months</Chart.Description>
  </Chart.Footer>
</Chart>
```

`seriesCount` is the one number the frame asks for: it cannot count the figure's series,
and the legend needs the palette walked to the right length. Unset, the legend walks its
own length. A figure that names its own `accent`, `size` or `color` still wins.

### A legend with values

```tsx
<Chart.Legend>
  <Chart.LegendItem index={0}>wi-fi (18 GB)</Chart.LegendItem>
  <Chart.LegendItem index={1}>mobile (8 GB)</Chart.LegendItem>
</Chart.Legend>
```

Outside a `<Chart>`, a legend takes its own `accent`, `size`, `color` and `count`, which
have to be the figure's.

### A frame with no figure

Both halves are optional: a figure on its own draws no ground, and a frame with a
`Skeleton` in it is what a chart looks like while its data loads.

### A mark of your own

`ChartPlot` is the plot every cartesian chart is drawn in: the grid, the zero axis, the
labels, both scales and the palette. It takes the figures' shared props and a render
function handed the scaled series, the frame, the scales and the ticks.

```tsx
<ChartPlot data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['revenue']}>
  {({ series }) => <Path d={linePath(series[0].points)} stroke={series[0].color} />}
</ChartPlot>
```

`spacing` is `point` (the first and last readings on the plot's edges, for a line) or
`band` (each centred in a slot, for a bar). The grid lines are 1 in the faint grey; the
zero axis is a line of 2 in the muted ink, drawn over the marks when `hasXAxis` is on. The
labels are `caption`, tabular and muted. `react-native-svg` is an optional peer.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Chart size="sm">…</Chart>
<Chart size="md">…</Chart>
<Chart size="lg">…</Chart>
```

`size` is the plot's height — 140, 200, 280 — never its width, which is the parent's. The
words around the figure keep their roles at every size.

## Colour

The palette is shades of one colour, walked from the seed: `color`, the named `accent`'s
true colour, or the theme's accent. The three intents are accent names: `green`, `amber`,
`red`.

```tsx
<Chart accent="green" seriesCount={1}>
  …
</Chart>
```

## Accessibility

- `Chart.Title` has the `header` role.
- The axis labels are React Native `Text`, so they follow the theme's font and the
  platform's text size.
- A disabled frame greys the palette and dims itself; a figure dims for its own
  `isDisabled` alone.

## Differences from Native

- **No shell**: Native's frame is a card; Tram's has no ground, padding, line or corner.
- **`variant`** is replaced by `accent`, the palette's seed; `ChartVariant` is gone and
  `color` still wins. The intents are the accents `green`, `amber` and `red`.
- **`size`** moves only the plot. The square figures take the frame's size as well as its
  palette, where Native's take the palette alone.
- **The plot** is Tram's own on Native's maths: grid lines in the faint grey, the zero
  axis a line of 2 over the marks, a legend entry a square rather than a dot.

# Checkbox — @xaui/tram

A box that is ticked or not, drawn in Metro: a square with a line around it, and a square
of the accent inside once it is ticked, arriving on a spring.

The root is the row, so a tap on the label ticks the box too.

## Import

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from '@xaui/tram/checkbox'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Checkbox>
  <Checkbox.Indicator />
  <Checkbox.Label />
</Checkbox>
```

- **`Checkbox`** — the row and the control. A text child is the label, and the root
  supplies the box; with no children it is the box alone.
- **`Checkbox.Indicator`** — the box and the mark inside it. Children replace the square
  and keep its motion and its place.
- **`Checkbox.Label`** — the text beside the box. It keeps the case you write.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Checkbox defaultSelected>remember me</Checkbox>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<Checkbox isSelected={accepted} onSelectedChange={setAccepted}>
  i accept the terms
</Checkbox>
```

`onSelectedChange` fires with the new value on every tick, controlled or not.

### Composed

```tsx
<Checkbox size="lg" accent="lime" defaultSelected>
  <Checkbox.Indicator />
  <Checkbox.Label>get the newsletter</Checkbox.Label>
</Checkbox>
```

### A mark of your own

```tsx
<Checkbox.Indicator>
  <Icon as={CheckIcon} size={14} />
</Checkbox.Indicator>
```

### Indeterminate

```tsx
<Checkbox isIndeterminate={someSelected} isSelected={allSelected}>
  select all
</Checkbox>
```

Neither ticked nor empty: the mark is a bar, and a press resolves it to selected. It is a
display state and does not touch `isSelected`.

### Box alone

```tsx
<Checkbox accessibilityLabel="select row" />
```

### Invalid and disabled

`isInvalid` draws the box's line and the mark in `danger`; the label keeps its ink.
`isDisabled` greys the box, the mark and the label, and stops the press.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Checkbox size="sm">sm</Checkbox>
<Checkbox size="md">md</Checkbox>
<Checkbox size="lg">lg</Checkbox>
```

`size` drives the box, the mark, the gap and the label's type — never width. The touch
reaches past a small box.

## Colour

The mark is the theme's accent. `accent` picks one of the twenty named accents; `color`
takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins when both are set. The box's line stays the page's ink.
Both are ignored while `isInvalid`: an error outranks a brand colour.

```tsx
<Checkbox accent="magenta">magenta</Checkbox>
```

## Accessibility

- The root has the `checkbox` role and carries `checked` — `mixed` when indeterminate —
  and `disabled`.
- A box with no label needs an `accessibilityLabel`.
- A tick is felt through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`, as a `selection`.
- The mark grows from the centre on a spring; with motion reduced it fades in and out at
  its full size. `animation={false}` keeps the row its full size under the finger;
  `'disable-all'` also places the mark with no spring.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`**: Native's three are fills of the box at rest, and the Metro box has no
  fill — a line on the ground.
- **`accent`** is added: one of the twenty named accents, for the mark.
- **The mark** is a square of the accent, not a tick.
- **`isInvalid`** leaves the label its ink.
- **The press** shrinks the row; Native's scale, highlight and ripple are off.
- **The corner** stays within 2, the Tram radius scale.

# Chip — @xaui/tram

A compact token — a status, a tag, a filter, a person — drawn as the `Button`'s sharp
rectangle made small: 24, 32 or 40 tall, square corners, in the `Button`'s four drawings.

A static chip is a `View`. `isPressable` makes it a control that tilts toward the finger,
as the `Button` does, and changes no colour.

## Import

```tsx
import { Chip } from '@xaui/tram/chip'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Chip>
  <Chip.Dot />
  <Chip.Avatar />
  <Chip.Icon />
  <Chip.Label />
  <Chip.Close />
</Chip>
```

- **`Chip`** — the root. It resolves the recipe once and hands the resolved styles to its
  slots. A string child is wrapped in a `Chip.Label` for you.
- **`Chip.Label`** — the text, on one line.
- **`Chip.Dot`** — a small square before the label, in the ink — on `flat`, the true colour
  the soft fill stands for.
- **`Chip.Icon`** — a glyph at the chip's size and in its ink. It takes `Icon`'s three
  forms: `as`, a raw SVG child, or `source`.
- **`Chip.Avatar`** — a square, chip-sized frame. `source` lays a photo over it; without
  one, the children are its content.
- **`Chip.Close`** — the cross at the end: two bars of the `Button`'s line, no circle. It
  is a control of its own, so a static chip can still be dismissed.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Chip>new</Chip>
```

### Composed

JSX order is screen order. No slot carries a margin: the gap belongs to the root.

```tsx
<Chip variant="flat" accent="green">
  <Chip.Dot />
  <Chip.Label>delivered</Chip.Label>
</Chip>
```

### Dismissible

```tsx
<Chip variant="outline">
  <Chip.Avatar source={{ uri: photo }} />
  <Chip.Label>inès</Chip.Label>
  <Chip.Close accessibilityLabel="Remove Inès" onPress={remove} />
</Chip>
```

The cross is smaller than a finger: its touch reaches past it to 48.

### Filter

```tsx
<Chip isPressable variant={isOn ? 'contained' : 'outline'} onPress={toggle}>
  unread
</Chip>
```

A press handler needs `isPressable`; without it the chip is a `View` that never receives
the touch, and a development warning says so.

## Variants

The `Button`'s four drawings, in the accent or in `color`. `contained` is the default.

| Variant     | Drawn as                          |
| ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| `contained` | filled with the true colour       |
| `flat`      | filled with its soft slice        |
| `outline`   | the `Button`'s line and the label |
| `text`      | the label alone                   |

```tsx
<Chip variant="contained">contained</Chip>
<Chip variant="flat">flat</Chip>
<Chip variant="outline">outline</Chip>
<Chip variant="text">text</Chip>
```

## Sizes

```tsx
<Chip size="sm">sm</Chip>
<Chip size="md">md</Chip>
<Chip size="lg">lg</Chip>
```

24, 32 and 40 tall; `md` is the default. A pressable chip reaches 48 through `hitSlop`.

## Colour

A status is a colour, not a variant: `accent="green"` for a success, `amber` for a
warning, `red` for a danger. `accent` takes one of the twenty named Metro accents; `color`
takes a raw tint, is never corrected, and wins when both are set.

```tsx
<Chip variant="flat" accent="amber">pending</Chip>
<Chip variant="outline" color="#7c3aed">raw</Chip>
```

`radius` overrides the Tram corner of 2, on the theme's scale, so it stays within 2.

## Accessibility

- A pressable chip has the `button` role and announces `disabled`; a static chip has no
  role of its own.
- `Chip.Close` needs an `accessibilityLabel` — the cross has no text to read.
- The press tilt is dropped when animations are disabled.

## Differences from Native

- **`variant`** is `contained`, `flat`, `outline` or `text` — the `Button`'s four drawings
  for Native's eleven names. A status is an `accent`.
- **`accent`** is added: one of the twenty named accents.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **The shape** is a sharp rectangle with a corner of 2, not a capsule; the dot and the
  avatar are squares, not circles.
- **The cross** is two bars of the `Button`'s line with no circle.
- **The press** of `isPressable` tilts the chip and changes no colour (no `pressed` state).

# CloseButton — @xaui/tram

The way out of a page or a panel of the app, drawn as the round button of the Metro App
Bar with a cross in it — a thin circle in the page's ink, the cross built from two bars so
no icon set is needed.

It is drawn in the page's ink, not the accent: closing is not the action a screen puts
forward. `accent` or `color` paints it on demand.

## Import

```tsx
import { CloseButton } from '@xaui/tram/close-button'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<CloseButton />
```

- **`CloseButton`** — one node, no slots: the circle and the cross. `children` replace the
  cross — an `Icon` takes its size and ink without being told.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<CloseButton accessibilityLabel="Close draft" onPress={close} />
```

### Another glyph

```tsx
<CloseButton accessibilityLabel="Back" onPress={back}>
  <Icon as={BackIcon} />
</CloseButton>
```

### In a panel's corner

```tsx
<CloseButton variant="text" size="sm" accessibilityLabel="Hide" onPress={hide} />
```

`Dialog.Close` and `Toast.Close` draw nothing: a message box and a toast are closed by
their buttons. This one is for what the app owns.

## Variants

| Variant     | Drawn as                                                  |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `outline`   | the App Bar's button: a thin circle and a cross (default) |
| `contained` | a flat disc, the cross cut out in the ground              |
| `text`      | the cross alone, for the corner of a panel                |

```tsx
<CloseButton variant="outline" accessibilityLabel="Close" />
<CloseButton variant="contained" accessibilityLabel="Close" />
<CloseButton variant="text" accessibilityLabel="Close" />
```

All three take the same room: `text` keeps the line, clear, so its cross sits where the
others' does.

## Sizes

```tsx
<CloseButton size="sm" accessibilityLabel="Close" />
<CloseButton size="md" accessibilityLabel="Close" />
<CloseButton size="lg" accessibilityLabel="Close" />
```

The circle is 32, 40 or 48 across — the `Fab`'s — around a glyph of 16, 20 or 24. Every
size is pressed as 48: `hitSlop` makes up the rest.

## Colour

Unset, the button is the page's ink. `accent` takes one of the twenty named accents: a
`contained` disc is filled with its true colour, an `outline` or `text` cross is drawn in
its ink, moved until it reads on the ground. `color` takes a raw tint, is never
corrected, and wins when both are set.

```tsx
<CloseButton variant="contained" accent="red" accessibilityLabel="Discard" />
```

## Accessibility

- The root has the `button` role and announces `disabled`. Disabled is a grey line and
  cross, or a grey disc, not an opacity.
- A cross is not text: the button needs an `accessibilityLabel`, and warns in development
  without one.
- A press leans the circle toward the finger and is felt as `press` through
  `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`. With motion reduced, or animations off, it does not lean.
- On the web the browser's focus ring is kept, for keyboard focus only.

## Differences from Native

- **`radius`** is dropped: a Tram close button is a circle.
- **`variant`** is `outline`, `contained` or `text` — Tram's three drawings, not Native's
  four emphasis levels.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **`accent`** is added; `color` wins and is never corrected.
- **Disabled** is drawn in grey rather than dimmed.
- **The press** tilts the circle; Native scales or highlights it.

# ColorPicker — @xaui/tram

A colour chosen off a palette, drawn as the Windows Phone accents page: a field that shows
the chosen colour as a square and its name, and a full-screen page of swatches that
swivels in on its top edge.

The field is the Tram `DummyField`. The palette is the twenty Tram accents
(`TRAM_PALETTE`), named, with no shades; `colors` replaces it. A grid can also stand on
the screen with no field and no page.

## Import

```tsx
import { ColorPicker, TRAM_PALETTE } from '@xaui/tram/color-picker'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ColorPicker>
  <ColorPicker.Label />
  <ColorPicker.Field>
    <ColorPicker.Preview />
  </ColorPicker.Field>
  <ColorPicker.Description />
  <ColorPicker.Error />
  <ColorPicker.Overlay />
  <ColorPicker.Content>
    <ColorPicker.Title />
    <ColorPicker.Close />
    <ColorPicker.Grid>
      <ColorPicker.Group>
        <ColorPicker.Swatch />
      </ColorPicker.Group>
    </ColorPicker.Grid>
  </ColorPicker.Content>
</ColorPicker>
```

- **`ColorPicker`** — the root, the `DummyField`'s column. It holds the value and the open
  state.
- **`ColorPicker.Label`**, **`Description`**, **`Error`** — the `DummyField`'s own slots.
- **`ColorPicker.Field`** — the box that opens the page. Left empty, it draws the chip,
  the colour's name and the `Select`'s chevron; `value` replaces the name.
- **`ColorPicker.Preview`** — the flat square of the chosen colour, the box height less 20;
  an empty square lined in grey while nothing is chosen. `color` shows another one.
- **`ColorPicker.Overlay`** — draws nothing: the page takes the screen. It carries only
  `isDismissable`, whether the system's back closes the page.
- **`ColorPicker.Content`** — the page, a `Modal`.
- **`ColorPicker.Title`** — a light page title; the page is labelled by it.
- **`ColorPicker.Close`** — the Tram `CloseButton`, `text` by default, in the top-end
  corner.
- **`ColorPicker.Grid`** — a `ScrollView` of swatches; with no children it draws `colors`.
- **`ColorPicker.Group`** — a group of swatches under an optional `name`, a `caption`.
- **`ColorPicker.Swatch`** — one colour, with an optional `name`.

## Usage

### Field and page

```tsx
<ColorPicker value={accent} onValueChange={setAccent}>
  <ColorPicker.Label>accent colour</ColorPicker.Label>
  <ColorPicker.Field placeholder="choose a colour" />
  <ColorPicker.Overlay />
  <ColorPicker.Content>
    <ColorPicker.Title>accents</ColorPicker.Title>
    <ColorPicker.Close accessibilityLabel="Close" />
    <ColorPicker.Grid />
  </ColorPicker.Content>
</ColorPicker>
```

The page closes on a choice; `closeOnSelect={false}` keeps it open.

### Grid on the page

```tsx
<ColorPicker layout="mosaic" value={tile} onValueChange={setTile}>
  <ColorPicker.Grid scrollEnabled={false} />
</ColorPicker>
```

### A palette by hand

```tsx
<ColorPicker closeOnSelect={false} value={recent} onValueChange={setRecent}>
  <ColorPicker.Grid scrollEnabled={false}>
    <ColorPicker.Group name="recent">
      <ColorPicker.Swatch color="#A20025" name="crimson" />
      <ColorPicker.Swatch color="#00ABA9" name="teal" />
    </ColorPicker.Group>
  </ColorPicker.Grid>
</ColorPicker>
```

A `ColorGroup`'s `name` heads the group and prefixes every swatch's name ("violet 600");
unset, each swatch is named by its `shade` alone.

## Layout

| Layout   | Drawn as                                                                |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ramps`  | the Windows Phone 7 list: a square of 48 and the name, rows of 56       |
| `mosaic` | the Windows Phone 8 grid: squares five to a row, 2 apart, with no names |

`ramps` is the default; the chosen colour's name is written in its own colour, read as
ink. In `mosaic` the chosen square wears a ring: 3 of the ground, then 2 of ink.

## Sizes

`size` is the `DummyField`'s — `sm`, `md` or `lg` — and sizes the field. The page does not
change with it.

## Colour

`accent` and `color` are the field's line under the finger, as on the `DummyField`; the
palette is not tinted by them.

## Accessibility

- The page is a `dialog`, modal, labelled by `ColorPicker.Title` when one is mounted. The
  system's back and a screen reader's escape close it, unless `Overlay` sets
  `isDismissable={false}`.
- The grid is a `radiogroup` and each swatch a `radio` with its `selected` and `checked`
  state; a swatch reads its `name`, else the colour's hex.
- A choice is felt as `selection` through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`.
- With motion reduced the page fades in instead of swivelling; with animations off it is
  there or not, and the swatches do not lean.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`**, no `labelPlacement`, no `xs`; **`accent`** is added.
- **`Content`** is a full-screen page, not a `Dialog`, so `Overlay` draws nothing and
  takes only `isDismissable`.
- **`TRAM_PALETTE`** replaces `TAILWIND_PALETTE`.
- **`ColorGroup.name`** is optional, and `Swatch` gains `name`.
- **The chip** sits inside the box, not in a `FieldGroup.Prefix`, and the field shows the
  colour's name (its hex off the palette) where Native shows the upper-case hex.
- **A group's name** is a `caption` above its swatches.

# Combobox — @xaui/tram

A field you type in, over a list you must choose from — drawn as the Tram `Select`'s box
with the value replaced by the field being typed into, and the list unfolding under the
row, inside the same line.

The list is closed: what is typed narrows the rows and never becomes the value. It is
always unfolded in place, never a page — a page would cover the field being typed into.

## Import

```tsx
import { Combobox } from '@xaui/tram/combobox'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Combobox>
  <Combobox.Label />
  <Combobox.Trigger>
    <Combobox.Input />
    <Combobox.Indicator />
  </Combobox.Trigger>
  <Combobox.Overlay />
  <Combobox.Content>
    <Combobox.Item>
      <Combobox.ItemLabel />
    </Combobox.Item>
    <Combobox.Empty />
  </Combobox.Content>
  <Combobox.Description />
  <Combobox.Error />
</Combobox>
```

- **`Combobox`** — the root: the `Autocomplete`'s props — the value, the open state and the
  query.
- **`Combobox.Trigger`** — the `Select`'s box around the row, which also holds the list
  once it unfolds. A `View`, not a pressable: the input takes the touch.
- **`Combobox.Input`** — the text input, where the value stands in the `Select`: the query
  while open, the chosen label while not. Typing and focus open the list
  (`opensOnChange`, `opensOnFocus`, both on by default).
- **`Combobox.Indicator`** — the `Select`'s chevron as a key of 48: the way into the list
  without typing.
- **`Combobox.Overlay`** — a touch outside the unfolded list closes it; `isDismissable`
  set to false leaves only a choice to close it.
- **`Combobox.Content`**, **`Item`**, **`ItemLabel`**, **`Empty`** — the `Autocomplete`'s
  list, rows and the line shown when nothing matches.
- **`Combobox.Label`**, **`Description`**, **`Error`** — the `Select`'s own.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Combobox value={city} onValueChange={setCity}>
  <Combobox.Label>city</Combobox.Label>
  <Combobox.Trigger>
    <Combobox.Input placeholder="search a city" />
    <Combobox.Indicator accessibilityLabel="Open the list" />
  </Combobox.Trigger>
  <Combobox.Overlay />
  <Combobox.Content>
    <Combobox.Item value="bko">Bamako</Combobox.Item>
    <Combobox.Item value="dkr">Dakar</Combobox.Item>
    <Combobox.Empty>no city matches</Combobox.Empty>
  </Combobox.Content>
</Combobox>
```

The list pushes what is under the field and scrolls past five rows. The letters each row
matched are in the accent, read as ink. Closing without a choice puts the chosen row's
label back in the field.

### Controlled query

```tsx
<Combobox
  query={query}
  onQueryChange={setQuery}
  value={city}
  onValueChange={setCity}
>
  …
</Combobox>
```

Left uncontrolled, the query is cleared every time the list closes.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Combobox size="sm">…</Combobox>
<Combobox size="md">…</Combobox>
<Combobox size="lg">…</Combobox>
```

`size` drives the field's height, padding, gaps and type — never width.

## Colour

`accent` takes one of the twenty named accents: the colour of the line while the list is
open and of the current choice in it, read as ink. `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins
when both are set.

## Accessibility

- `Combobox.Trigger` has the `combobox` role. `Combobox.Input` is labelled by the label,
  described by the description and the error, and carries `aria-controls`,
  `aria-expanded` and `aria-autocomplete="list"`.
- `Combobox.Indicator` is a `button`; give it an `accessibilityLabel`.
- Each row is an `option` with its selected state.
- The list unfolds on the `navigation` spring; with motion reduced it fades in instead.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`**; **`accent`** is added.
- **Always in place**, never a page — a page would cover the field being typed into.
- **The input** carries `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-autocomplete`.

# DatePicker — @xaui/tram

A field that opens a page of wheels to choose a day, drawn as the Metro date picker: the
`TextField`'s box with the day in it, and a page that swivels in with three columns of
squares — the day, the month and the year — and the App Bar's ✓ and ✕ along the bottom.

Nothing is chosen while the wheels turn: ✓ takes the day and fires `onValueChange`; ✕ and
the system's back leave the value as it was.

## Import

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from '@xaui/tram/date-picker'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<DatePicker>
  <DatePicker.Label />
  <DatePicker.Field />
  {/* or */}
  <DatePicker.Trigger>
    <DatePicker.Value />
    <DatePicker.Indicator />
  </DatePicker.Trigger>
  <DatePicker.Overlay />
  <DatePicker.Content>
    <DatePicker.Wheel />
  </DatePicker.Content>
  <DatePicker.Description />
  <DatePicker.Error />
</DatePicker>
```

- **`DatePicker`** — the root is the column: the label, the field, the description or the
  error. `ref`, `style` and the style props dress that column.
- **`DatePicker.Label`** — what the field is for. Its text also titles the page.
- **`DatePicker.Field`** — the trigger and its value in one tag; `placeholder` is the line
  shown while nothing is chosen.
- **`DatePicker.Trigger`** — the box and its row, the control a screen reader stops on.
- **`DatePicker.Value`** — the day as the root reads it; children replace it.
- **`DatePicker.Indicator`** — a glyph at the end of the field. It draws nothing unless
  given one with `as`.
- **`DatePicker.Overlay`** — draws nothing: the page takes the screen. It carries only
  `isDismissable`, whether the system's back closes the page.
- **`DatePicker.Content`** — the page: the label as its title, the wheels, and the ✓ and ✕
  bar. `confirmLabel` and `cancelLabel` name the two buttons (`done` and `cancel`).
- **`DatePicker.Wheel`** — the wheel on the page: the `WheelPicker`'s props, less its
  columns, colour and disabled state. Unwritten, the page draws it for you.
- **`DatePicker.Description`**, **`DatePicker.Error`** — the help lines under the field.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<DatePicker value={date} onValueChange={setDate}>
  <DatePicker.Label>birthday</DatePicker.Label>
  <DatePicker.Field placeholder="choose a date" />
  <DatePicker.Content confirmLabel="ok" cancelLabel="cancel" />
</DatePicker>
```

The field reads the day through `Intl` (`dateStyle: 'medium'`); `formatOptions` takes
anything `Intl.DateTimeFormat` takes. `value` is a day at midnight.

### Locale

```tsx
<DatePicker locale="ja-JP">…</DatePicker>
```

The columns are in the locale's order — the day first in French, the month first in
American English, the year first in Japanese. A month square carries its number and its
short name, a day square its number and its weekday.

### Bounds

```tsx
<DatePicker minValue={new Date(2026, 0, 1)} maxValue={new Date(2026, 11, 31)}>
  …
</DatePicker>
```

The day and the month turn without end; the year runs a century each way, or between the
bounds. A day outside them turns back to the nearest one; 31 January turned to February
lands on its last day.

### The wheel

```tsx
<DatePicker.Content>
  <DatePicker.Wheel variant="light" isAwake visibleCount={3} />
</DatePicker.Content>
```

## Sizes

```tsx
<DatePicker size="sm">…</DatePicker>
<DatePicker size="md">…</DatePicker>
<DatePicker size="lg">…</DatePicker>
```

`size` sets the field's height and type, and the side of the squares on the page.

## Colour

`accent` takes one of the twenty named accents: the field's line while the page is open,
read as ink, and the fill of the current squares. `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins
when both are set.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a `button`, labelled by the label and described by the help lines, with
  `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the page.
- The page is a modal `dialog` labelled by the label; its title is a `header`.
- ✓ and ✕ are buttons named by `confirmLabel` and `cancelLabel`; a press is felt through
  `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`.
- A column is named for a screen reader in the locale (`Intl.DisplayNames`).
- With motion reduced the page fades in instead of swivelling.

## Differences from Native

- **`Calendar`** is replaced by **`Wheel`**: the `WheelPicker`'s props less its columns,
  colour and disabled state; `size` defaults to the picker's.
- **No `variant`** (one box), no `calendarVariant` (written on `Wheel`), no
  `firstDayOfWeek` (no grid), no `closeOnSelect` (✓ confirms); **`accent`** is added.
- **`Overlay`** draws nothing and only carries `isDismissable` — the page takes the screen.
- **`Content`** is a page, not an anchored panel: its placement props are dropped and
  `confirmLabel` / `cancelLabel` are added.
- **`Indicator`** draws nothing unless given a glyph; Native draws a calendar.

# DateTimePicker — @xaui/tram

A field that opens a page of wheels to choose a moment — a day and a time — drawn as the
Tram `DatePicker`'s field and page, its two halves taking turns under a pair of tabs.

Six columns do not fit across a phone, so the page shows the date or the time: two titles
along the top each read their half of the moment being chosen, and a press on one brings
its wheels in from its side. Nothing is chosen until ✓.

## Import

```tsx
import { DateTimePicker } from '@xaui/tram/date-time-picker'
import { Tabs } from '@xaui/tram/tabs' // only to write the panels out
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<DateTimePicker>
  <DateTimePicker.Label />
  <DateTimePicker.Field />
  {/* or */}
  <DateTimePicker.Trigger>
    <DateTimePicker.Value />
    <DateTimePicker.Indicator />
  </DateTimePicker.Trigger>
  <DateTimePicker.Overlay />
  <DateTimePicker.Content>
    <DateTimePicker.Steps>
      <Tabs.Content value="date">
        <DateTimePicker.DateWheel />
      </Tabs.Content>
      <Tabs.Content value="time">
        <DateTimePicker.TimeWheel />
      </Tabs.Content>
    </DateTimePicker.Steps>
  </DateTimePicker.Content>
  <DateTimePicker.Description />
  <DateTimePicker.Error />
</DateTimePicker>
```

- **`DateTimePicker`** — the root is the column: the label, the field, the description or
  the error.
- **`Label`**, **`Field`**, **`Trigger`**, **`Value`**, **`Indicator`**, **`Overlay`**,
  **`Content`**, **`Description`**, **`Error`** — the `DatePicker`'s slots, with a moment
  in them. `Indicator` draws nothing unless given a glyph; `Overlay` draws nothing and
  carries only `isDismissable`.
- **`DateTimePicker.Steps`** — the two halves as the Tram `Tabs`. Unwritten, `Content`
  draws it; with no children, its panels hold the two wheels. Written out, each panel is a
  `Tabs.Content` whose `value` is the step's name, `date` or `time`.
- **`DateTimePicker.DateWheel`** — the `DatePicker`'s wheel: a day turned keeps the time.
- **`DateTimePicker.TimeWheel`** — the `TimePicker`'s wheel, on the picker's clock: a time
  turned keeps the day.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<DateTimePicker value={moment} onValueChange={setMoment}>
  <DateTimePicker.Label>appointment</DateTimePicker.Label>
  <DateTimePicker.Field placeholder="choose a moment" />
  <DateTimePicker.Content confirmLabel="ok" cancelLabel="cancel" />
</DateTimePicker>
```

The field reads the moment as `{ dateStyle: 'medium', timeStyle: 'short' }` on the
picker's clock; `formatOptions` replaces it. ✓ confirms the moment from either half; ✕ and
the system's back drop it. The page opens on the date.

### Clock and step

```tsx
<DateTimePicker locale="fr-FR" hourCycle={12} minuteStep={15}>
  …
</DateTimePicker>
```

The clock is the locale's unless `hourCycle` (`12` or `24`) says otherwise. `minuteStep`
is how far apart two minute squares are.

### Controlled step

```tsx
<DateTimePicker step={step} onStepChange={setStep}>
  <DateTimePicker.Label>departure</DateTimePicker.Label>
  <DateTimePicker.Field />
  <DateTimePicker.Content>
    <DateTimePicker.Steps labels={{ date: 'date', time: 'time' }} />
  </DateTimePicker.Content>
</DateTimePicker>
```

### Bounds

`minValue` and `maxValue` are compared to the minute: a moment before the first turns to
the first square after it, one past the last to the last square before it.

## Sizes

```tsx
<DateTimePicker size="sm">…</DateTimePicker>
<DateTimePicker size="md">…</DateTimePicker>
<DateTimePicker size="lg">…</DateTimePicker>
```

`size` sets the field's height and type, and the side of the squares on the page.
`Steps` has its own `size`, `md` by default.

## Colour

`accent` takes one of the twenty named accents: the field's line while the page is open,
read as ink, and the fill of the current squares. `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins
when both are set.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a `button`, labelled by the label and described by the help lines, with
  `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the page.
- The page is a modal `dialog` labelled by the label.
- The step titles show the halves of the moment, not words: `labels` name them for a
  screen reader, announced as "date, 18 Nov 2026".
- ✓ and ✕ are buttons named by `confirmLabel` and `cancelLabel`.
- With motion reduced the page fades in instead of swivelling.

## Differences from Native

- **The root is the column**, with `Label`, `Field`, `Description` and `Error`; Native's
  root renders no node.
- **`Sheet`** is replaced by **`Content`** (a page), and **`Overlay`** is added.
- **`Calendar`** and **`Clock`** are replaced by **`DateWheel`** and **`TimeWheel`**.
- **`Steps`** takes `labels` for a screen reader, and its children are the panels
  (`Tabs.Content` per step).
- **No `variant`**, no `closeOnSelect`; **`accent`** is added.
- **`Indicator`** draws nothing unless given a glyph.

# Dialog — @xaui/tram

A message that interrupts the screen and asks for an answer, drawn as the Metro
`MessageBox`: a banner of the discreet surface across the top of the screen, edge to edge,
over the page dimmed at the theme's `backdrop`, swivelling in on its top edge.

Its children arrive in cascade as soon as it reads as flat. A swipe upward turns it under
the finger and lightens the ground; past a threshold of distance or of speed, it leaves.

## Import

```tsx
import { Dialog } from '@xaui/tram/dialog'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Dialog>
  <Dialog.Trigger />
  <Dialog.Overlay />
  <Dialog.Content>
    <Dialog.Title />
    <Dialog.Description />
    <Dialog.Close />
  </Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

- **`Dialog`** — the root. It renders no node: `ref` and `style` live on the parts that
  draw. It holds the open state.
- **`Dialog.Trigger`** — what opens the banner. It paints nothing of its own: `asChild`
  makes it a `Button`, and a string is set in `body`.
- **`Dialog.Overlay`** — the dimmed ground. `isDismissable={false}` makes a banner that
  must be answered.
- **`Dialog.Content`** — the banner. Each child is one step of the cascade, in the order
  written: the title, the description, then a row of actions.
- **`Dialog.Title`**, **`Dialog.Description`** — the question and its detail.
- **`Dialog.Close`** — what closes the banner. It draws no cross: a `MessageBox` is closed
  by its buttons. `asChild` makes it one; a string is set in `body`.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Dialog>
  <Dialog.Trigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outline">delete</Button>
  </Dialog.Trigger>
  <Dialog.Overlay />
  <Dialog.Content paddingTop={insets.top + 24}>
    <Dialog.Title>delete this document?</Dialog.Title>
    <Dialog.Description>it will not go to the bin.</Dialog.Description>
    <View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', gap: 12 }}>
      <Dialog.Close asChild>
        <Button flex={1}>delete</Button>
      </Dialog.Close>
      <Dialog.Close asChild>
        <Button flex={1} variant="outline">
          cancel
        </Button>
      </Dialog.Close>
    </View>
  </Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

The banner reads no safe area: it starts at the very top of the screen, under the notch.
Pad `Dialog.Content` with the app's own inset.

### At the bottom

```tsx
<Dialog placement="bottom">
  <Dialog.Trigger asChild>…</Dialog.Trigger>
  <Dialog.Overlay />
  <Dialog.Content paddingBottom={insets.bottom + 24}>…</Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

`placement="bottom"` lays the same banner against the foot of the screen, within reach of
the thumb: it turns on its bottom edge and is swiped back down.

### Must be answered

```tsx
<Dialog.Overlay isDismissable={false} />
```

Neither a touch on the ground, nor a swipe, nor the system's back closes it, and it
resists the finger.

### Controlled

```tsx
<Dialog isOpen={isOpen} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  …
</Dialog>
```

## Accessibility

- `Dialog.Content` is a `dialog` (`alertdialog` on the web when not dismissable), labelled
  by `Dialog.Title` and described by `Dialog.Description`.
- It takes the focus as it opens and gives it back to the trigger as it closes.
- A screen reader's escape and the system's back close it, unless `isDismissable` is off.
- A disabled dialog's trigger is grey and opens nothing; a `Button` under `asChild` is
  handed `isDisabled`.
- With motion reduced the banner fades in and out instead of swivelling, and does not
  follow the finger.

## Differences from Native

- **`placement`** (`top` / `bottom`) is added.
- **`radius`** is accepted and draws nothing: the banner runs edge to edge.
- **No `accent`**: the banner has none; its buttons carry their own.
- **`Close`** draws no cross — a string or `asChild`.
- **`Trigger`** and **`Close`** set a string in `body`; a disabled trigger is grey.
- **A `Modal`**, not the portal, with `Overlay` drawn inside it.
- **`Content`** is a `dialog` (`alertdialog` on the web when not dismissable); Native's is
  an `alert`.
- **`isDismissable={false}`** also holds the swipe, the system's back and the screen
  reader's escape.
- **Each child of `Content`** is wrapped in a view of its own for the cascade.
- **The banner reads no safe area**: `Content` is padded by the app.

# Divider — @xaui/tram

The line between two things, drawn in the Tram grey: one point of `muted`, faded so the
space around it still does most of the separating — Metro's way.

It is one node with no slots. It takes the axis it does not run along from its parent, so
it needs no width.

## Import

```tsx
import { Divider } from '@xaui/tram/divider'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Divider />
```

- **`Divider`** — the rule. Under `asChild` the child element becomes the rule and keeps
  its thickness and ink.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Row />
<Divider />
<Row />
```

### Vertical

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', gap: 12 }}>
  <Typography>pivot</Typography>
  <Divider orientation="vertical" size="md" />
  <Typography>panorama</Typography>
</View>
```

`orientation` is `horizontal` (the default) or `vertical`.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Divider size="sm" />
<Divider size="md" />
<Divider size="lg" />
```

| Size | Thickness              |
| ---- | ---------------------- |
| `sm` | 1 (default)            |
| `md` | 2, the `Button`'s line |
| `lg` | 3, the theme's border  |

## Colour

The rule is `muted`, faded to half on a dark theme and to three quarters on a light one.
`color` takes a raw tint, never a token, and is drawn whole, not faded. There is no
`accent`: a line in the accent is a `color`.

```tsx
<Divider size="md" color={theme.colors.accent} />
```

## Accessibility

- The rule is furniture: `accessibilityElementsHidden` and
  `importantForAccessibility="no"` are set, so a screen reader reads the two groups it sits
  between, not the line. Both stay overridable.

## Differences from Native

- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg` — 1, 2 or 3 points — with `sm` the default; Native's
  default is the `xs` hairline, and Tram has no `xs`.
- **The grey** is faded to half on black and to three quarters on white; a raw `color` is
  drawn whole.
- **No `accent`**: a line in the accent is a `color`.

# DummyField — @xaui/tram

A field that is pressed rather than typed into, drawn as the Tram `TextField`'s box: a line
of 2 round a value it only shows. A press opens what sets the value — a sheet, a picker, a
page.

It is a `TextField`: the root is the Tram `TextField`'s, and `Description` and `Error` are
its slots. Under the finger the line takes the accent and gives it back on release; the
box does not move.

## Import

```tsx
import { DummyField } from '@xaui/tram/dummy-field'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<DummyField>
  <DummyField.Label />
  <DummyField.Field>
    <DummyField.Value />
    <DummyField.Indicator />
  </DummyField.Field>
  <DummyField.Description />
  <DummyField.Error />
</DummyField>
```

- **`DummyField`** — the root, the `TextField`'s column. `onPress` is what a press on the
  field — or on its label — does.
- **`DummyField.Label`** — the `TextField`'s label, which presses the field instead of
  focusing an input. A disabled field's label is plain text again.
- **`DummyField.Field`** — the box, and the control a screen reader stops on. Text
  children become a `DummyField.Value`; with no children it shows `value`, or
  `placeholder` in grey.
- **`DummyField.Value`** — what the field shows, on one line, or its `placeholder` until
  there is something to show.
- **`DummyField.Indicator`** — a glyph at the end of the field, a chevron unless given
  `as`, at the `Select`'s sizes. Left out, the row holds the value alone.
- **`DummyField.Description`**, **`DummyField.Error`** — the `TextField`'s help lines.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<DummyField onPress={openSlots}>
  <DummyField.Label>delivery</DummyField.Label>
  <DummyField.Field placeholder="choose a slot">{slot}</DummyField.Field>
  <DummyField.Description>tap to change the slot.</DummyField.Description>
</DummyField>
```

### Composed

```tsx
<DummyField onPress={openCountries}>
  <DummyField.Label>country</DummyField.Label>
  <DummyField.Field>
    <DummyField.Value placeholder="choose a country">{country}</DummyField.Value>
    <DummyField.Indicator />
  </DummyField.Field>
</DummyField>
```

### Invalid

```tsx
<DummyField onPress={openCalendar} isInvalid={!day}>
  <DummyField.Label>date</DummyField.Label>
  <DummyField.Field placeholder="choose a date" value={day} />
  <DummyField.Error>a date, please.</DummyField.Error>
</DummyField>
```

`isInvalid` draws the line in `danger`; the label keeps its ink. It does not mount the
error: that stays the caller's.

## Sizes

```tsx
<DummyField size="sm">…</DummyField>
<DummyField size="md">…</DummyField>
<DummyField size="lg">…</DummyField>
```

`size` drives the box's height, padding, gaps and type — never width.

## Colour

`accent` takes one of the twenty named accents: the colour of the line under the finger,
read as ink. `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins when both are set; it is ignored while
`isInvalid`.

## Accessibility

- `DummyField.Field` has the `button` role, is labelled by the label and described by the
  description and the error, and announces `disabled` and `aria-invalid`.
- `isRequired` tells a screen reader the field has to be filled; it draws nothing.
- The line moves on the `navigation` spring; with motion reduced it is a short timing.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`**, no `labelPlacement`, no `xs`: the Metro box has one drawing, its label
  above it.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **The label** keeps its ink when invalid.
- **The root** does not bridge the `TextField` context for a `FieldGroup`.

# EmptyState — @xaui/tram

What is on the screen when there is nothing on it, said as a Metro page says it: aligned
to the start, a title on the Tram scale, the detail faded under it, then what to do about
it.

The header and the content are two parts, as in Native: the gap inside the words is not
the gap between them and the buttons. The words are never tinted — `accent` and `color`
land on the media's square only.

## Import

```tsx
import { EmptyState } from '@xaui/tram/empty-state'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<EmptyState>
  <EmptyState.Header>
    <EmptyState.Media />
    <EmptyState.Title />
    <EmptyState.Description />
  </EmptyState.Header>
  <EmptyState.Content />
</EmptyState>
```

- **`EmptyState`** — the root, the ground the whole state sits on.
- **`EmptyState.Header`** — the media and the words.
- **`EmptyState.Media`** — an illustration, a photo, or a glyph on a square of the accent
  (`variant="icon"`).
- **`EmptyState.Title`** — what is missing, on `subtitle`, `title` or `section` as the
  size chooses.
- **`EmptyState.Description`** — the detail, faded as the `Card`'s.
- **`EmptyState.Content`** — what to do about it: a button, a row of them.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<EmptyState>
  <EmptyState.Header>
    <EmptyState.Media variant="icon">
      <Icon as={FolderIcon} />
    </EmptyState.Media>
    <EmptyState.Title>no files</EmptyState.Title>
    <EmptyState.Description>
      Files you import or receive by mail show up here.
    </EmptyState.Description>
  </EmptyState.Header>
  <EmptyState.Content>
    <Button variant="outline">import</Button>
  </EmptyState.Content>
</EmptyState>
```

### Media

`EmptyState.Media` has two drawings:

| Variant | Drawn as                                                           |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `plain` | the media as it is; a glyph stays on the page in `muted` (default) |
| `icon`  | a square of the accent, the glyph in the ink that reads on it      |

## Variants

Three grounds, kept from Native by name:

| Variant    | Ground                                                 |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `plain`    | the page (default)                                     |
| `surface`  | the discreet surface, the `Card`'s                     |
| `outlined` | the page inside a solid line of 2 in `muted` — no dash |

```tsx
<EmptyState variant="surface">…</EmptyState>
```

## Sizes

```tsx
<EmptyState size="sm">…</EmptyState>
<EmptyState size="md">…</EmptyState>
<EmptyState size="lg">…</EmptyState>
```

`size` drives the media's square — 40, 56 or 72, the `Avatar`'s — the gaps and the type.
Never a height.

## Colour

`accent` takes one of the twenty named accents and repaints the media's square only.
`color` takes a raw tint, wins over `accent`, and also lands on the square alone.
`radius` overrides the Tram corner of 2 and stays within 2.

```tsx
<EmptyState accent="teal">…</EmptyState>
```

## Accessibility

- `EmptyState.Title` has the `header` role, which is what a screen reader jumps between —
  so a screen whose only content is an empty state is still navigable.

## Differences from Native

- **Aligned to the start**, as a Metro page, not centred.
- **`outlined`** is a solid line of 2 in `muted`, not Native's dashes.
- **`Media variant="icon"`** is a square of the accent 40 / 56 / 72, the glyph in the ink
  that reads on it, where Native draws a muted circle; `plain` leaves a glyph in `muted`.
- **`accent`** is added, repainting the square only.
- **`color`** tints the square alone, unlike Native.
- **`radius`** caps at 2.

# Fab — @xaui/tram

The one thing to do on a screen, drawn as the round button of the Metro App Bar: a circle
in a band of the discreet `surface`, docked edge to edge on the bottom of the nearest
positioned ancestor — a flat circle of the accent, or the App Bar's thin circle.

It never sits in the flow. The band comes up from the bottom edge on the `navigation`
spring and leaves the same way; a press leans the circle toward the finger.

## Import

```tsx
import { Fab } from '@xaui/tram/fab'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Fab>
  <Fab.Icon />
  <Fab.Label />
  <Fab.Spinner />
</Fab>
```

- **`Fab`** — the root: the band and the circle in it.
- **`Fab.Icon`** — the glyph, at the size's scale and in the ink that reads on the circle.
  It takes `Icon`'s three forms: `as`, a raw SVG child, or `source`.
- **`Fab.Label`** — a caption laid under the circle, drawn only while `isExtended`. A bare
  string child is a label too.
- **`Fab.Spinner`** — the busy ring. `isLoading` puts one in the glyph's place when none
  is composed; `animation={false}` stops its rotation.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Fab accessibilityLabel="New message" onPress={compose}>
  <Fab.Icon as={PlusIcon} />
</Fab>
```

### Extended

```tsx
<Fab isExtended placement="bottom-end" onPress={compose}>
  <Fab.Icon as={PlusIcon} />
  <Fab.Label>new</Fab.Label>
</Fab>
```

The circle does not stretch: the label is laid under it in the band's ink, centred, on one
line no wider than the circle plus the band's side padding, and the band rises by its
height. A visible label names the button.

### Showing and hiding

```tsx
<Fab isVisible={!isScrolling} accessibilityLabel="New">
  <Fab.Icon as={PlusIcon} />
</Fab>
```

`isVisible={false}` sends the band under the bottom edge, where it can be neither seen,
pressed nor read. A change of `placement` is a way out, then a way in.

### Safe area

`offset` is the band's padding under the circle (8 by default). The bottom safe area is
added under it, from the hook the app handed `TramProvider`
(`safeArea={{ useSafeAreaInsets }}`). `hasSafeArea={false}` leaves it out, for a band
docked in a box that does not reach the screen's bottom edge.

### Placement

`placement` is `bottom-start`, `bottom-center` (default) or `bottom-end`: where the
circle sits across its band.

## Variants

| Variant     | Drawn as                                                    |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `contained` | a flat fill of the true colour, the glyph in the ink on it  |
| `outline`   | the App Bar's button: a line of 2 and a glyph in the colour |

Both are the same size: the filled circle draws its line in its fill. `contained` is the
default.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Fab size="sm" accessibilityLabel="New"><Fab.Icon as={PlusIcon} /></Fab>
<Fab size="md" accessibilityLabel="New"><Fab.Icon as={PlusIcon} /></Fab>
<Fab size="lg" accessibilityLabel="New"><Fab.Icon as={PlusIcon} /></Fab>
```

The circle is 32, 40 or 48 across, around a glyph of 16, 20 or 24. Every size is pressed
as 48: `hitSlop` makes up the rest.

## Colour

`accent` takes one of the twenty named accents: a `contained` circle is filled with its
true colour, the glyph black or white, whichever reads; an `outline` is drawn in its ink,
moved until it reads on the band. `color` takes a raw tint, is never corrected, and wins
when both are set.

## Accessibility

- The circle has the `button` role and announces `disabled` and `busy`.
- A `Fab` with no visible label needs an `accessibilityLabel`, and warns in development
  without one. A visible label names the button without being read twice.
- Hidden by `isVisible={false}`, the band is out of the accessibility tree.
- A press is felt as `press` through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`. With motion reduced the
  circle does not lean; the spinner still turns, and is a fixed ring under `disable-all`.
- No focus ring is drawn on the web.

## Differences from Native

- **`radius`** is dropped: a Tram `Fab` is a circle.
- **`variant`** is `contained` or `outline`, Tram's two drawings.
- **`placement`** is never unset and only along the bottom.
- **`accent`** is added; `color` wins and is never corrected.
- **No shadow**; Native carries one at rest.
- **The extended label goes under the circle**, a caption in the band's ink; Native writes
  it beside the glyph in a pill.
- **`isVisible`** is added.
- **`isLoading`** keeps the colours; Native dims.
- **Disabled** is a flat grey circle, or a grey line and glyph, not an opacity.
- **Smaller**: 32 / 40 / 48 across, where Native's are 40 / 56 / 72.

# FieldGroup — @xaui/tram

A field with something beside it — a glyph, a unit, a country, a reveal toggle — drawn in
Metro as one box around a cell, the text and a cell, inside the `TextField`'s line of 2,
which takes the accent while the field has the focus.

It goes inside a `TextField` and replaces nothing but the field. The label, the help, the
error, `size`, the accent, `isInvalid` and `isDisabled` are the `TextField`'s, and so is
the box: its line, corner, ground and height are read off the field's style, so a group
and a plain field on one form are the same box.

## Import

```tsx
import { FieldGroup } from '@xaui/tram/field-group'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<TextField>
  <TextField.Label />
  <FieldGroup>
    <FieldGroup.Prefix>
      <FieldGroup.Icon />
    </FieldGroup.Prefix>
    <FieldGroup.Field />
    <FieldGroup.Suffix />
  </FieldGroup>
  <TextField.Description />
</TextField>
```

- **`FieldGroup`** — the box: one row, a cell, the field and a cell.
- **`FieldGroup.Field`** — `TextField.Field` itself, inside the box, with no line of its
  own.
- **`FieldGroup.Prefix`**, **`FieldGroup.Suffix`** — a cell at the start or the end.
  `isDecorative` decides what it is: a mark leaning on the text, or a key of its own.
- **`FieldGroup.Icon`** — a glyph at the box's size (16, 20 or 24, the `CloseButton`'s)
  in the placeholder's grey. `size` and `color` passed to it win.

## Usage

### A decorative mark

```tsx
<TextField>
  <TextField.Label>email</TextField.Label>
  <FieldGroup>
    <FieldGroup.Prefix isDecorative>
      <FieldGroup.Icon as={MailIcon} />
    </FieldGroup.Prefix>
    <FieldGroup.Field keyboardType="email-address" />
  </FieldGroup>
</TextField>
```

A decorative cell stands off the box's end by the field's padding, takes no touch — a tap
on it focuses the field — and leaves the accessibility tree.

### A unit

```tsx
<FieldGroup>
  <FieldGroup.Field keyboardType="decimal-pad" />
  <FieldGroup.Suffix isDecorative>
    <Text>kg</Text>
  </FieldGroup.Suffix>
</FieldGroup>
```

### A control

```tsx
<FieldGroup>
  <FieldGroup.Field secureTextEntry={!isShown} />
  <FieldGroup.Suffix>
    <Pressable
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityLabel={isShown ? 'Hide' : 'Show'}
      onPress={toggle}
    >
      <FieldGroup.Icon as={EyeIcon} />
    </Pressable>
  </FieldGroup.Suffix>
</FieldGroup>
```

A control cell is a key: padded on both sides and ruled off from the text by the
`NumberField`'s rule in `muted`. It keeps its touches and its place for a screen reader.

### Under `asChild`

`asChild` merges the box into the single child: the caller's element draws the box, and
its line stays at rest.

The group has no `size` of its own: the `TextField`'s sets the box — 40, 48 or 56 tall.

## Accessibility

- The box has no role: the control is the field inside it.
- A decorative cell is hidden from screen readers on both platforms; a control cell is
  not, and names itself with its own `accessibilityRole` and `accessibilityLabel`.
- A prefix is not a label: write a `TextField.Label` as well.
- A disabled group takes the touches of both cells.
