## Differences from Native

- **One row**, where Native lays its decorators over the field and pads it by their
  measured width. The context carries the box's focus and geometry instead of
  `prefixWidth` / `suffixWidth` and their setters, and `decoratorPadding` is not exported.
- **`isDecorative`** also decides how the cell is drawn.
- **`FieldGroup.Icon`** reads its size and the placeholder's grey from the group.
- **Under `asChild`** the caller's element draws the box and its line stays at rest.

# InputOTP — @xaui/tram

A one-time code, one character to a box, drawn as a row of Tram fields one character wide:
a faint line while a box is empty, the ink once it holds a character, the accent on the
box being typed in.

There is one input, and it is hidden: it covers the row, holds the whole code as one
string, and the boxes are a drawing of it.

## Import

```tsx
import { InputOTP, OTP_ALPHANUMERIC } from '@xaui/tram/input-otp'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<InputOTP maxLength={6}>
  <InputOTP.Group>
    {({ slots }) => slots.map(s => <InputOTP.Box key={s.index} index={s.index} />)}
  </InputOTP.Group>
</InputOTP>
```

- **`InputOTP`** — the root. It owns the code as one string, renders the hidden
  `TextInput` over the row, and hands the resolved styles and each box's state to its
  slots. Its `ref` is `focus`, `blur` and `clear`.
- **`InputOTP.Group`** — a row of boxes. It takes a render function as well as elements:
  the number of boxes is data.
- **`InputOTP.Box`** — one character's box, read by its `index`. With no children it draws
  the value, the placeholder and the caret.
- **`InputOTP.Value`** — the character, or nothing while the box is empty.
- **`InputOTP.Placeholder`** — what stands in for it before anything is typed.
- **`InputOTP.Caret`** — a bar 2 wide that blinks in the box the next character lands in.
  `animation={false}` stops the blink.
- **`InputOTP.Separator`** — a 10 × 2 dash in `muted` between two groups.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<InputOTP maxLength={6} onComplete={verify}>
  <InputOTP.Group>
    {({ slots }) => slots.map(s => <InputOTP.Box key={s.index} index={s.index} />)}
  </InputOTP.Group>
</InputOTP>
```

`onComplete` fires once the last box is filled. Leave `value` out and the component keeps
the code itself; `defaultValue` seeds it.

### Two groups

```tsx
<InputOTP maxLength={6}>
  <InputOTP.Group>{({ slots }) => boxes(slots.slice(0, 3))}</InputOTP.Group>
  <InputOTP.Separator />
  <InputOTP.Group>{({ slots }) => boxes(slots.slice(3))}</InputOTP.Group>
</InputOTP>
```

### Letters and digits

```tsx
<InputOTP maxLength={4} pattern={OTP_ALPHANUMERIC} inputMode="text">
  …
</InputOTP>
```

`pattern` is tested against the whole value; `OTP_DIGITS`, `OTP_LETTERS` and
`OTP_ALPHANUMERIC` are the three usual answers. `inputMode` is `numeric` by default.
`textInputProps` carries anything else the hidden input should have.

### Your own box

```tsx
<InputOTP.Box index={slot.index}>
  <InputOTP.Value />
  <MyOwnCaret />
</InputOTP.Box>
```

## Variants

| Variant     | Drawn as                                                        |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `primary`   | the ground inside a line of 2 (default)                         |
| `secondary` | the discreet surface, no line until the box is the one typed in |
| `tertiary`  | drawn as `primary`                                              |

## Sizes

```tsx
<InputOTP size="sm" maxLength={6}>…</InputOTP>
<InputOTP size="md" maxLength={6}>…</InputOTP>
<InputOTP size="lg" maxLength={6}>…</InputOTP>
```

The box is 36 × 44, 44 × 52 or 52 × 60, narrowing to fit the row and never growing; the
character is on `subtitle`, `title` or `section` in tabular figures.

## Colour

`accent` takes one of the twenty named accents for the line and the caret of the box
being typed in, read as ink. `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins when both are set.
`isInvalid` puts every line in `danger`, with no active line, and outranks both.

## Accessibility

- The hidden input is the control. It carries a label ("6-character code"), the disabled
  state and an `accessibilityValue` reading "n of m entered", so a screen reader never
  walks the boxes one by one.
- `autoComplete="one-time-code"` and `textContentType="oneTimeCode"` are set, which puts
  the code in the keyboard's suggestion strip.
- `InputOTP.Separator` is hidden from the accessibility tree: the dash is not in the
  value.
- The caret stands still with motion reduced or animations off.

## Differences from Native

- **`variant`** defaults to `primary`, the ground inside the line; Native's default is
  `secondary`. `tertiary` draws as `primary`.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **The box** is sharp, 36 × 44 / 44 × 52 / 52 × 60, in the `TextField`'s line of 2: 60 %
  of `muted` while empty, the ink once filled, the accent on the box being typed in.
- **`isInvalid`** puts every line in `danger`.
- **The separator** is a 10 × 2 dash in `muted`.

# JumpList — @xaui/tram

The Metro grouped list — a contact list, a song list — where every group opens on a square
of the accent: press one and a grid of keys comes up over the page; press a key and the
grid turns away, and the list lands on that group.

It is Tram's own, with no Native equivalent. It is a `SectionList` and takes its props, so
it is virtualised: a list of two thousand names jumps as fast as one of twenty.

## Import

```tsx
import { JumpList, groupByInitial } from '@xaui/tram/jump-list'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<JumpList sections={sections} renderItem={renderRow}>
  <JumpList.Header />
  <JumpList.Overlay>
    <JumpList.Key />
  </JumpList.Overlay>
</JumpList>
```

- **`JumpList`** — the root, a `SectionList`. Its `ref` is that list. Every group with rows
  opens on a header; a group with none has no header, and its key is grey.
- **`JumpList.Header`** — written once, the drawing of every header: a flat square of the
  accent with its letter in the bottom-start corner, or a bar as wide as its word for a
  group that is not a letter. Pressed, it puts the grid up.
- **`JumpList.Overlay`** — the grid, over the whole screen: the page's own ground, opaque,
  with the keys on it. A `Modal`, so it covers the navigation and hears the system's back.
- **`JumpList.Key`** — written once inside the overlay, the drawing of every key. Pressed,
  the grid leaves and the list lands on its group.

All three are optional: left out, they are drawn as they are. Their text is the section's
`title`, or its key; a function child is handed the group (`key`, `title`, `isEmpty`).

## Usage

### A list of names

```tsx
const sections = groupByInitial(contacts, contact => contact.name, { locale: 'fr' })

<JumpList
  sections={sections}
  keyExtractor={contact => contact.id}
  renderItem={({ item }) => <ContactRow contact={item} />}
  onJump={key => track('jump', key)}
/>
```

`groupByInitial` files every row under the key of its initial — accents folded, sorted by
locale within a group — and gives every key its section, empty ones included. A row whose
initial is no key goes under `#`. The keys default to `JUMP_LIST_ALPHABET`: `#`, then a–z.

### Groups that are not letters

```tsx
const sections = [
  { key: 'today', title: 'today', data: today },
  { key: 'yesterday', title: 'yesterday', data: yesterday },
]

<JumpList sections={sections} renderItem={renderMessage} />
```

Keys of one character are a grid of squares four across; any longer key makes a column of
bars. `layout` (`grid` or `list`) forces one. `keys` lists the grid's keys in order when
they are not the sections' own.

### Hints

```tsx
<JumpList sections={sections} renderItem={renderContact}>
  <JumpList.Header accessibilityHint="Opens the alphabet" />
  <JumpList.Overlay>
    <JumpList.Key accessibilityHint="Goes to this letter" />
  </JumpList.Overlay>
</JumpList>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<JumpList
  sections={sections}
  renderItem={renderContact}
  isOpen={isOpen}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
/>
```

## Sizes

```tsx
<JumpList size="sm" sections={sections} renderItem={renderContact} />
<JumpList size="md" sections={sections} renderItem={renderContact} />
<JumpList size="lg" sections={sections} renderItem={renderContact} />
```

A header is a square of 40, 48 or 56, its letter scaled with it; `md` is the default. A
40-point square is pressed as 48.

## Colour

`accent` takes one of the twenty named accents for the headers and the keys. `color` takes
a raw `#RRGGBB` fill, is never corrected, and wins when both are set. A key with no row is
the soft grey `default`, its letter muted, and does not respond.

## Accessibility

- Headers and keys are `button`s named by their text; an empty key announces `disabled`.
  Add an `accessibilityHint` to say what they do.
- The grid is modal. The system's back closes it.
- The header the list lands on takes the focus — the keyboard's on the web, the screen
  reader's on a phone — so the reader goes on from the group chosen.
- A header is felt as `press`, a key as `selection`, through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`.
- The grid arrives a row at a time and leaves in a turnstile on the screen's start edge.
  With motion reduced it fades; under an ancestor's `disable-all` it is there or not.
- `isDisabled` dims the headers, which then open nothing.

Headers do not stick to the top: a Metro list has none. There is no `asChild`, since the
root is a virtualised list.

# LineChart — @xaui/tram

A line per series over a shared scale, drawn the Metro way: a stroke of 2 with sharp
corners and square-cut ends, straight from one reading to the next, and squares for points.

The series are props, not children: each line is a column of your data, named in `yKeys`.
The axes, the grid and the palette come from the shared plot of the chart family; the
words around the figure come from the `Chart` frame.

## Import

```tsx
import { LineChart } from '@xaui/tram/line-chart'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Chart>
  <Chart.Header>
    <Chart.Heading>
      <Chart.Title />
      <Chart.Description />
      <Chart.Value />
    </Chart.Heading>
    <Chart.Legend />
  </Chart.Header>
  <LineChart />
  <Chart.Footer />
</Chart>
```

- **`LineChart`** — the plot. It has no slots of its own: it draws the grid, the lines,
  the points and the axis labels from its props. Its ref is the plot's view.
- **`Chart`** (from `@xaui/tram/chart`) — the optional frame. It has no ground, line or
  corner; it hands its `accent`, `size` and `color` down to the figure inside and lays
  out the title, the value and the legend.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<LineChart data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['wifi', 'mobile']} />
```

`xKey` runs along the bottom; each key in `yKeys` is a line, in the order the palette
walks them. An empty `data` draws the axes and nothing else.

### In a frame

```tsx
<Chart seriesCount={2}>
  <Chart.Header>
    <Chart.Heading>
      <Chart.Title>data</Chart.Title>
      <Chart.Description>GB per month, on this phone</Chart.Description>
    </Chart.Heading>
    <Chart.Legend labels={['wi-fi', 'mobile']} />
  </Chart.Header>
  <LineChart data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['wifi', 'mobile']} />
</Chart>
```

The frame cannot count the series: `seriesCount` walks the legend's palette to the same
length as the figure's.

### Curve and points

```tsx
<LineChart data={rows} xKey="day" yKeys={['value']} curve="monotone" hasPoints />
```

`curve` is `linear` by default. `monotone` (Fritsch–Carlson) smooths the line without
leaving the data — it never dips below a valley. `hasPoints` draws a square of 6 on every
reading; it reads best on a short series. `strokeWidth` sets the line's thickness.

### Axes and grid

```tsx
<LineChart
  data={rows}
  xKey="month"
  yKeys={['wifi']}
  hasGrid={false}
  hasXAxis={false}
  hasYAxis={false}
  size="sm"
/>
```

`formatX` and `formatY` write the labels, `tickCount` aims the y axis at a number of
labels, `xLabelCount` thins the x labels, and `hasZeroBaseline={false}` starts the y axis
at the lowest value instead of zero.

## Sizes

```tsx
<LineChart size="sm" data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['wifi']} />
<LineChart size="md" data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['wifi']} />
<LineChart size="lg" data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['wifi']} />
```

`size` is the plot's height — 140, 200 or 280 — never its width, which is the parent's.

## Colour

The palette is walked out of one colour, a shade per series. `accent` picks one of the
twenty named Metro accents — the intents are `green`, `amber` and `red` — and `color`
takes a raw tint and wins when both are set. Inside a `Chart`, the frame's appearance is
the default.

```tsx
<LineChart accent="teal" data={rows} xKey="month" yKeys={['wifi', 'mobile']} />
```

`isDisabled` dims the plot.

## Accessibility

- The plot is a plain `View` with no role. Its `View` props are passed through: give it
  `accessible` and an `accessibilityLabel` that says what the figure shows.
- A `Chart.Title` in the frame is a `header` to a screen reader.

## Differences from Native

- **`curve`** defaults to `linear` — Metro's figures were angular. Native defaults to
  `monotone`, which stays one prop away.
- **The stroke** has mitred corners and square-cut ends; Native's cap and join are round.
- **`hasPoints`** draws squares of 6; Native draws dots.
- **`accent`** replaces `variant`: the palette's seed is one of the twenty named accents,
  the intents being `green`, `amber` and `red`.

# List — @xaui/tram

A virtualised list of content rows, drawn as the Metro content list: a square thumbnail at
the start, a large title in the page's ink, a line in the accent, a detail in Metro's subtle
grey, and no card and no line between the rows.

`List` is a `FlatList`: it takes the vertical `FlatList` props, and its `renderItem`
composes each row from slots. The rows carry the page's 24-point margin, so the list runs
edge to edge, and 12 points of space separate two rows.

## Import

```tsx
import { List } from '@xaui/tram/list'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<List>
  <List.Item>
    <List.Leading />
    <List.Content>
      <List.Title />
      <List.Subtitle />
      <List.Description />
    </List.Content>
    <List.Action />
    <List.Swipe>
      <List.SwipeAction />
    </List.Swipe>
  </List.Item>
</List>
```

- **`List`** — the root, a `FlatList`. `ItemSeparatorComponent`, `horizontal`, `inverted`
  and `numColumns` are locked: the list is one column, read from the top.
- **`List.Item`** — one row. With `onPress` or `onLongPress` it becomes a button that leans
  toward the finger; without them it does not move.
- **`List.Leading`** — a square of 52 in the accent, with a glyph in it. With `asChild` its
  one child — an `Image` — fills the square.
- **`List.Content`** — takes the remaining width and stacks the three lines of text.
- **`List.Title`** — the title, in the page's ink on the `title` role.
- **`List.Subtitle`** — a line in the accent, read as ink, on `body`.
- **`List.Description`** — a detail of up to two lines on `caption`, in the subtle grey.
- **`List.Action`** — level with the title at the row's end: the time of a mail, or a
  control. A string is written in the grey.
- **`List.Swipe`** — the actions lying under the row at its end, out of sight until the row
  is swiped.
- **`List.SwipeAction`** — one action: a flat fill at least 72 wide holding a label and an
  `Icon`.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<List
  data={stories}
  keyExtractor={story => story.id}
  renderItem={({ item }) => (
    <List.Item onPress={() => open(item)}>
      <List.Leading>
        <Icon as={SunIcon} />
      </List.Leading>
      <List.Content>
        <List.Title>{item.title}</List.Title>
        <List.Subtitle>{item.category}</List.Subtitle>
        <List.Description>{item.lede}</List.Description>
      </List.Content>
    </List.Item>
  )}
/>
```

### A mail list

No square, and the time level with the title:

```tsx
<List.Item onPress={() => read(mail)}>
  <List.Content>
    <List.Title>{mail.from}</List.Title>
    <List.Subtitle>{mail.subject}</List.Subtitle>
    <List.Description>{mail.body}</List.Description>
  </List.Content>
  <List.Action>{mail.time}</List.Action>
</List.Item>
```

A row without `onPress` does not move: a control such as a `Switch` in `List.Action` keeps
its own role and press.

### Swipe actions

```tsx
<List.Item onPress={() => open(item)}>
  <List.Content>
    <List.Title>{item.title}</List.Title>
  </List.Content>
  <List.Swipe>
    <List.SwipeAction onPress={() => archive(item)}>
      <Icon as={ArchiveIcon} />
      archive
    </List.SwipeAction>
    <List.SwipeAction accent="red" onPress={() => remove(item)}>
      <Icon as={TrashIcon} />
      delete
    </List.SwipeAction>
  </List.Swipe>
</List.Item>
```

The row follows the finger toward its start, a third as fast past its actions, and settles
open past half of them or when flung. One row is open at a time: opening another, touching
the row, pressing an action or scrolling the list closes it.

### Disabled

`isDisabled` on `List.Item` greys the text and the square and stops the press and the
swipe.

## Colour

The square, the subtitle and the swipe actions take the theme's accent. `accent` on the root
picks one of the twenty named Metro accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins when both
are set. A swipe action's own `accent` or `color` wins over the list's; its label and glyph
are black or white, whichever reads on the fill.

The subtitle's accent ink is moved, by the smallest step, until it stands apart from both
the title's ink and the description's grey. A raw `color` is never moved.

## Accessibility

- The root has the `list` role.
- A row with `onPress` or `onLongPress` has the `button` role; a disabled row announces its
  state.
- The swipe actions are hidden from a screen reader while the row is closed, and offered as
  the row's accessibility actions instead.
- The first rows arrive in a cascade when the list first shows some; rows drawn later by
  scrolling are placed. With motion reduced they fade in together; `hasEntrance={false}`
  places them.
- The swipe is mirrored in right-to-left layouts.

## Differences from Native

- **`List.Subtitle`** is added: Metro's three levels of text.
- **`onPress` / `onLongPress`** on `List.Item` make the row a button that leans toward the
  finger; Native's row has no press of its own.
- **`isDisabled`** is added on `List.Item`.
- **`List.Swipe` and `List.SwipeAction`** are added.
- **`accent`** and **`color`** are added on the root, and **`hasEntrance`**.
- **The `separator` slot** is dropped: rows are separated by space, never a line.
- **`List.Leading`** takes `asChild` for a picture that fills the square.

# ListBox — @xaui/tram

Rows on a ground, drawn as the rows of the Metro settings page: no fill, no line, no shadow
and no corner — a title in the page's ink, a description in the muted grey, and the space
between the rows to tell them apart.

`ListBoxGroup` stacks several lists into sections under headers. A row you can press leans
toward the finger; a row can also be chosen or ticked, as in the Metro mail list.

## Import

```tsx
import { ListBox, ListBoxGroup } from '@xaui/tram/list-box'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ListBoxGroup>
  <ListBoxGroup.Section>
    <ListBoxGroup.Header />
    <ListBox>
      <ListBox.Item>
        <ListBox.ItemPrefix />
        <ListBox.ItemContent>
          <ListBox.ItemTitle />
          <ListBox.ItemDescription />
        </ListBox.ItemContent>
        <ListBox.ItemSuffix />
      </ListBox.Item>
      <ListBox.ItemButton />
    </ListBox>
    <ListBoxGroup.Footer />
  </ListBoxGroup.Section>
</ListBoxGroup>
```

- **`ListBox`** — the root, a `list`. It resolves the rows' styles once and holds the
  selection.
- **`ListBox.Item`** — a plain row: no press, no movement, a `listitem`. A control inside it
  keeps its own role and press.
- **`ListBox.ItemButton`** — a row you can press, used in place of `ListBox.Item`. Its `id`
  is what the selection reads.
- **`ListBox.ItemPrefix`** — what leads the row. `variant="bare"` draws it as given;
  `variant="square"` puts it on a square of the accent, its glyph in the ink that reads on
  it.
- **`ListBox.ItemContent`** — the text column, which pushes the suffix to the end.
- **`ListBox.ItemTitle`** — what the row is, in the page's ink.
- **`ListBox.ItemDescription`** — what it is set to, in the muted grey.
- **`ListBox.ItemSuffix`** — a value or a control at the end, in the muted grey. It draws
  nothing of its own.
- **`ListBoxGroup`** — the sections, with the defaults every list inside takes.
- **`ListBoxGroup.Section`** — one section, a `group` named by its header.
- **`ListBoxGroup.Header`** / **`ListBoxGroup.Footer`** — the text above and below a list.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<ListBox>
  <ListBox.ItemButton onPress={openWifi}>
    <ListBox.ItemPrefix variant="square">
      <Icon as={WifiIcon} />
    </ListBox.ItemPrefix>
    <ListBox.ItemContent>
      <ListBox.ItemTitle>Wi-Fi</ListBox.ItemTitle>
      <ListBox.ItemDescription>home</ListBox.ItemDescription>
    </ListBox.ItemContent>
  </ListBox.ItemButton>
</ListBox>
```

A row holding a `Switch` in its suffix is a plain `ListBox.Item`: the switch is the
control.

### Sections

```tsx
<ListBoxGroup>
  <ListBoxGroup.Section>
    <ListBoxGroup.Header>network</ListBoxGroup.Header>
    <ListBox>{/* rows */}</ListBox>
    <ListBoxGroup.Footer>Turns off when the screen sleeps.</ListBoxGroup.Footer>
  </ListBoxGroup.Section>
</ListBoxGroup>
```

The group's `size`, `accent`, `color` and `isDisabled` are the defaults of every list in it.

### Single selection

```tsx
<ListBox selectionMode="single" selectedKeys={tone} onSelectionChange={setTone}>
  {tones.map(item => (
    <ListBox.ItemButton key={item.id} id={item.id}>
      <ListBox.ItemContent>
        <ListBox.ItemTitle>{item.id}</ListBox.ItemTitle>
      </ListBox.ItemContent>
    </ListBox.ItemButton>
  ))}
</ListBox>
```

A press chooses the row and its title turns to the accent, read as ink; `onPress` still
runs. A row without an `id` is never chosen.

### Multiple selection

```tsx
<ListBox
  selectionMode="multiple"
  selectedKeys={picked}
  onSelectionChange={setPicked}
  isSelecting={isPicking}
  onSelectingChange={setIsPicking}
>
  {/* ItemButtons, each with an id and an onPress */}
</ListBox>
```

A press on the row's first 48 points puts the boxes out and ticks it. While the list is
selecting, every press ticks or unticks and `onPress` does not run; leaving empties the
selection. `isSelecting` / `defaultSelecting` hold whether the boxes are out.

## Sizes

`size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the rows' height — 52, 64 or 80 at least — the type of the
title and the description, and the prefix's square. Never the width.

## Colour

The squares of `ItemPrefix variant="square"` and the chosen title take the theme's accent.
`accent` picks one of the twenty named Metro accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins when
both are set. Nothing else on a row is the accent.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `list`; `ListBox.Item` a `listitem`; `ListBoxGroup.Section` a `group`, and
  `ListBoxGroup.Header` a `header`.
- `ListBox.ItemButton` is a `button`, announced as `selected` when chosen in `single`; while
  a `multiple` list is selecting it is a `checkbox`, announced as `checked`.
- `isDisabled` greys the rows and stops their press, on one row or the whole list.
- The rows, headers and footers arrive in one cascade through every section; a row added or
  removed later opens or closes its height. With motion reduced the list only fades in, and
  the boxes' column is open or shut. `hasEntrance={false}` places the rows.
- The start edge of a row is mirrored in right-to-left layouts.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`** — Native's four are card fills — and **no `radius`**: there is no card.
- **`hasSeparator`** is dropped on the list and the group: a Metro list reads by the space
  between its rows, never a line.
- **Selection** is added — `selectionMode`, the selected keys, `isSelecting`, and an `id`
  on `ItemButton`. Native's `ListBox` has none.
- **`accent`** is added, and **`hasEntrance`** on both roots.
- **`ItemPrefix`** gains `variant="square"`.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **The press** on `ItemButton` leans the row toward the finger; Native washes it.

# MaskField — @xaui/tram

A value typed into a shape — a date, a time, a card number, or a pattern of your own — in
the Tram `TextField`'s box: the ground inside a line, with what is left of the shape waiting
in grey behind the typed text.

It is a `TextField`. `MaskField.Label`, `.Description` and `.Error` are the Tram
`TextField`'s own slots, re-exported; only `MaskField.Field` differs, by masking what is
typed into it. The mask itself is Native's, so both packages accept, clamp and put back the
same characters.

## Import

```tsx
import { MaskField } from '@xaui/tram/mask-field'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<MaskField>
  <MaskField.Label />
  <MaskField.Field />
  <MaskField.Description />
  <MaskField.Error />
</MaskField>
```

- **`MaskField`** — the root, the Tram `TextField`'s. It holds the masked text and decides
  the keyboard and the placeholder once.
- **`MaskField.Label`** — the label above the box. A touch on it gives the field the focus.
- **`MaskField.Field`** — the box, masked. It takes the number pad for a digit shape and
  the default keyboard for one with letters, and stops at the shape's length.
- **`MaskField.Description`** — a line of help under the box.
- **`MaskField.Error`** — the error, drawn with `isInvalid`. Mounting it stays yours.

## Usage

### Presets

```tsx
<MaskField mask="credit-card" onValueChange={setCard}>
  <MaskField.Label>card number</MaskField.Label>
  <MaskField.Field />
</MaskField>
```

`mask` takes one of four presets: `date`, `time` (24-hour), `datetime` and `credit-card`.
A date part is clamped as it is typed — the 31st of February becomes the 28th.

### A pattern

```tsx
<MaskField mask="AA-###-AA">
  <MaskField.Label>plate</MaskField.Label>
  <MaskField.Field autoCapitalize="characters" />
</MaskField>
```

Any other string is a pattern: `#` a digit, `A` a letter, `*` either, and every other
character a literal, put back as the parts fill. A pattern does not clamp.

### Dates and locales

```tsx
<MaskField
  mask="date"
  locale="fr-FR"
  segmentLabels={{ day: 'JJ', month: 'MM', year: 'AAAA' }}
  convert={text => parseMaskedDate(text, 'fr-FR')}
  onValueChange={(text, value) => setDay(value as Date | null)}
>
  <MaskField.Label>delivery date</MaskField.Label>
  <MaskField.Field />
</MaskField>
```

The order and the separator of the date parts are read from `locale` (`en-US` by default).
`order` sets the order when it is a decision — an ISO field is `YMD` — and `separator` and
`segmentLabels` override the rest. `parseMaskedDate` and `parseMaskedTime` come from
`@xaui/native/mask-field`.

### The value

`value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` work on the masked text; a raw string given to
`value` or `defaultValue` is masked on the way in. `convert` turns the text into a value of
your own — a `Date`, `{ hours, minutes }` — and returns `null` while the text is not one
yet; `onValueChange` receives it as its second argument.

### The rest of the shape

```tsx
<MaskField mask="date" defaultValue="0412" showMask={false}>
  <MaskField.Label>date</MaskField.Label>
  <MaskField.Field />
</MaskField>
```

With `showMask` (true by default), what is left of the shape stays in the placeholder's grey
behind the typed text — `04/12/` then a grey `YYYY`. It steps aside on its own when it
cannot sit exactly under the text: labels not as wide as their parts, or text not aligned to
the start. With `showMask={false}` the shape is only the placeholder, gone at the first key.

## Sizes

```tsx
<MaskField size="sm" mask="time">…</MaskField>
<MaskField size="md" mask="time">…</MaskField>
<MaskField size="lg" mask="time">…</MaskField>
```

`size` is the box's height — 40, 48 or 56 — with its padding and type. Never its width.

## Colour

The line turns to the theme's accent, read as ink, once the field has the focus. `accent`
picks one of the twenty named Metro accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins when both are
set. `isInvalid` draws the line in the danger colour and outranks both.

## Accessibility

- The field is described by `MaskField.Error` when it is shown.
- `isRequired` tells a screen reader the field has to be filled; it draws nothing.
- `isDisabled` greys the line, the text and the label, and makes the field uneditable.
- The grey rest of the shape is hidden from screen readers and takes no touches.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`** and **no `labelPlacement`**: the Metro box has one drawing, and its label
  stands above it.
- **`accent`** and **`isRequired`** are added — the Tram `TextField`'s.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **`showMask`** is added, true by default. Native shows the shape only while the box is
  empty.

# Menu — @xaui/tram

A list of actions anchored to whatever opened it, drawn as the Metro context menu: a band in
the theme's contrast colour, the width of the screen, set against its trigger, with large
light rows and no line, shadow or corner.

The band swivels in on the edge it shares with the trigger and its rows arrive in a cascade.
With `Menu.Overlay`, the ground is dimmed everywhere but over the trigger, and a focused
`Page` recedes behind it while the trigger stays in front, in place and at its size.

## Import

```tsx
import { Menu } from '@xaui/tram/menu'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger />
  <Menu.Overlay />
  <Menu.Content>
    <Menu.Label />
    <Menu.Group>
      <Menu.Item>
        <Menu.ItemIndicator />
        <Menu.ItemTitle />
        <Menu.ItemDescription />
      </Menu.Item>
    </Menu.Group>
    <Menu.Separator />
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

- **`Menu`** — the open state and the resolved styles. It renders no node.
- **`Menu.Trigger`** — what opens it. It paints nothing of its own: with `asChild` it is your
  element, and a string is set in `body`. It is wrapped in one view, the one that stays in
  front while the page recedes.
- **`Menu.Overlay`** — the dimmed ground, and what closes the menu on a touch outside.
  Optional: without it nothing is dimmed, nothing recedes and a touch outside closes
  nothing.
- **`Menu.Content`** — the band, in a `Modal`. Each child is one step of the cascade, in the
  order written.
- **`Menu.Label`** — a heading over a run of rows, in the band's quieter ink.
- **`Menu.Group`** — that run, announced as a group.
- **`Menu.Separator`** — a gap of 12 between two runs. It draws no line.
- **`Menu.Item`** — one action.
- **`Menu.ItemTitle`** — its title. It takes the row's intent and wraps rather than cutting.
- **`Menu.ItemDescription`** — a second line, in the band's quieter ink.
- **`Menu.ItemIndicator`** — a fixed box of 24 at either end of a row, for a check or a
  glyph, so titles line up whatever it holds.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outline">actions</Button>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Overlay />
  <Menu.Content>
    <Menu.Item onPress={rename}>
      <Menu.ItemTitle>rename</Menu.ItemTitle>
    </Menu.Item>
    <Menu.Separator />
    <Menu.Item variant="danger" onPress={remove}>
      <Menu.ItemTitle>delete</Menu.ItemTitle>
    </Menu.Item>
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

Choosing a row closes the menu after its `onPress` has run. `closesOnPress={false}` keeps it
open, for a row the reader will want to press again.

### The context menu

```tsx
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger asChild opensOn="longPress">
    <ListBox.ItemButton onPress={() => open(mail)}>{/* … */}</ListBox.ItemButton>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Overlay />
  <Menu.Content>
    <Menu.Item onPress={() => reply(mail)}>
      <Menu.ItemTitle>reply</Menu.ItemTitle>
    </Menu.Item>
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

With `opensOn="longPress"`, the element keeps its own press — the row still opens the mail —
and the menu opens on a hold.

### Headings and indicators

```tsx
<Menu.Content>
  <Menu.Label>sort by</Menu.Label>
  <Menu.Group>
    {sorts.map(item => (
      <Menu.Item
        key={item.id}
        accessibilityRole="radio"
        accessibilityState={{ checked: item.id === sort }}
        onPress={() => setSort(item.id)}
      >
        <Menu.ItemTitle>{item.label}</Menu.ItemTitle>
        <Menu.ItemIndicator>
          {item.id === sort ? <Icon as={CheckIcon} /> : null}
        </Menu.ItemIndicator>
      </Menu.Item>
    ))}
  </Menu.Group>
</Menu.Content>
```

### Placement

`placement` on `Menu.Content` is `bottom` (the default) or `top`. The band takes the other
side when it only fits there, and the roomier side, scrolled, when it fits on neither. It
always keeps clear of the screen's edges and of the safe area handed to `TramProvider`.

For a menu that must be answered, `isDismissable={false}` on `Menu.Overlay`: neither a
touch outside nor the system's back closes it.

## Variants

`variant` on `Menu.Item` is the row's intent: `default` writes the title in the band's ink,
`danger` in the danger ink, on the band. Nothing else changes. A disabled row has a grey
title and does not move.

## Accessibility

- `Menu.Content` is a `menu` and a modal view; the focus moves to it when it opens and back
  to the trigger when it closes.
- `Menu.Item` is a `menuitem`, `Menu.Group` a `menu`, `Menu.Label` a `header`; the role
  stays overridable, as in the radio rows above. The separator is hidden.
- The trigger is a `button`. With `opensOn="longPress"` the hold is offered to a screen
  reader as an action.
- A row presses with a tilt and a `press` haptic; the hold that opens a context menu is felt
  as a `longPress`.
- With motion reduced, the ground fades, the page stays where it is and the rows do not
  lean.

## Differences from Native

- **`opensOn`** is added on `Menu.Trigger`: `press` by default, or `longPress`.
- **The trigger** is wrapped in one view, the one that stays in front.
- **`placement`** is `top` or `bottom` only.
- **`align`, `width`, `offset`, `alignOffset`, `avoidCollisions` and `insets`** are dropped:
  the band runs the width of the screen, touches its trigger and always avoids the edges.
- **`radius`** is kept so the two roots take the same props, and draws nothing.
- **`Menu.ItemTitle`** wraps instead of staying on one line.
- **The band** is drawn in a `Modal`, not a portal.

# MorphButton — @xaui/tram

A button that changes shape: closed, it is the Tram `Button` exactly — a flat rectangle in
one accent colour; open, the same box grows to the width it is given and keeps its fill,
with a light title and a description inside it.

One face is mounted at a time and nothing is measured: a layout transition carries the box
between the two sizes on the `navigation` spring, and the new face rises and fades in just
after.

## Import

```tsx
import { MorphButton, useMorphButton } from '@xaui/tram/morph-button'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<MorphButton>
  <MorphButton.Collapsed>
    <MorphButton.Icon />
    <MorphButton.Label />
  </MorphButton.Collapsed>
  <MorphButton.Expanded>
    <MorphButton.Title />
    <MorphButton.Description />
  </MorphButton.Expanded>
</MorphButton>
```

- **`MorphButton`** — the root, the pressable box that travels. A press toggles the shape,
  and `onPress` still runs.
- **`MorphButton.Collapsed`** — the closed face, mounted while the button is closed.
- **`MorphButton.Expanded`** — the open face, mounted while it is open.
- **`MorphButton.Label`** — the closed face's text, the `Button`'s label.
- **`MorphButton.Title`** — the open face's title, Light.
- **`MorphButton.Description`** — the sentence under it, a step smaller, in the same ink.
- **`MorphButton.Icon`** — an icon in the variant's colour, at the size's scale.

A bare string is not wrapped for you: it could belong to either face.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<MorphButton alignSelf="flex-start">
  <MorphButton.Collapsed>
    <MorphButton.Label>new theme</MorphButton.Label>
  </MorphButton.Collapsed>
  <MorphButton.Expanded>
    <MorphButton.Title>new theme</MorphButton.Title>
    <MorphButton.Description>
      Start from the current accent, then adjust it page by page.
    </MorphButton.Description>
  </MorphButton.Expanded>
</MorphButton>
```

Without an `alignSelf`, the box fills its column in both shapes.

### Controlled

```tsx
<MorphButton isExpanded={isOpen} onExpandedChange={setOpen}>
  {/* faces */}
</MorphButton>
```

`defaultExpanded` opens it on the card at first mount, with no entrance of its own.

### A control inside a face

```tsx
function Close() {
  const { toggle } = useMorphButton()

  return <Button onPress={toggle}>close</Button>
}
```

`useMorphButton().toggle` changes the shape and costs no state.

### Animation

`animation={false}` puts it in the other shape with no travel: the box jumps, the faces
swap without a fade, and the press does not tilt. An object — `{ stiffness, damping, mass }`
— retunes the spring the box travels on.

## Variants

The `Button`'s four drawings. Open, the box keeps the one it was drawn with.

| Variant     | Drawn as                         |
| ----------- | -------------------------------- |
| `contained` | filled with the true colour      |
| `flat`      | filled with its soft slice       |
| `outline`   | a line and a label in the colour |
| `text`      | the label alone                  |

## Sizes

```tsx
<MorphButton size="sm">…</MorphButton>
<MorphButton size="md">…</MorphButton>
<MorphButton size="lg">…</MorphButton>
```

`size` sets the closed height — 40, 48 or 56 — the insets, the gaps and the type of both
faces. Never the width. `radius` overrides the corner both shapes share, capped at the Tram 2.

## Colour

The colour is the theme's accent. `accent` picks another one of the twenty named Metro
accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins when both are set. A destructive button is
`color={theme.colors.danger}`.

## Accessibility

- The root is a `button` whose `accessibilityState.expanded` says which shape it is in; your
  own `accessibilityState` is merged over it rather than replacing it.
- The press tilts the box and leaves its colours alone, felt as a `press`.
- With motion reduced the box jumps to its new size and the face takes a 150 ms fade.

## Differences from Native

- **`variant`** is the `Button`'s four drawings — `contained`, `flat`, `outline`, `text` —
  for Native's seven and its inverted surface.
- **Open**, the box keeps its fill; it never turns into a card surface.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **`radius`** stays under the Tram ceiling of 2, `full` included: no pill and no
  half-height corner.
- **`animation={false}`** also stops the tilt.
- **The press** tilts the box; Native darkens it with the variant's pressed colour.

# NumberField — @xaui/tram

A number, typed, with the two ends of its range and a pair of keys that walk it — the Tram
`TextField`'s box drawn around the field, with a square key at each end and the value
centred between them in tabular figures.

It is a `TextField`. `NumberField.Label`, `.Description` and `.Error` are the Tram
`TextField`'s own slots, re-exported; parsing, clamping and stepping are Native's.

## Import

```tsx
import { NumberField } from '@xaui/tram/number-field'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<NumberField>
  <NumberField.Label />
  <NumberField.Group>
    <NumberField.Decrement />
    <NumberField.Field />
    <NumberField.Increment />
  </NumberField.Group>
  <NumberField.Description />
  <NumberField.Error />
</NumberField>
```

- **`NumberField`** — the root, the Tram `TextField`'s, plus the value, the bounds and the
  step.
- **`NumberField.Label`** — the label above the box.
- **`NumberField.Group`** — the box: one line around the field and its two keys.
- **`NumberField.Field`** — the input, the value centred in tabular figures.
- **`NumberField.Decrement`** / **`NumberField.Increment`** — the square keys at the start
  and the end, each ruled off from the value in `muted`. With no children they draw a minus
  or a plus in bars of 2; pass an `Icon` to replace the mark.
- **`NumberField.Description`** — a line of help under the box.
- **`NumberField.Error`** — the error, drawn with `isInvalid`. Mounting it stays yours.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<NumberField min={1} max={99} defaultValue={1} onValueChange={setQuantity}>
  <NumberField.Label>quantity</NumberField.Label>
  <NumberField.Group>
    <NumberField.Decrement accessibilityLabel="One fewer" />
    <NumberField.Field />
    <NumberField.Increment accessibilityLabel="One more" />
  </NumberField.Group>
</NumberField>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<NumberField value={copies} onValueChange={setCopies} min={1} max={5}>
  {/* … */}
</NumberField>
```

The value is a number, or `null` while the box holds no number yet — never `NaN`.

### Format and locale

```tsx
<NumberField
  locale="fr-FR"
  formatOptions={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }}
  defaultValue={34}
  min={0}
  step={0.5}
>
  {/* … */}
</NumberField>
```

Out of the field, the value is written with `Intl.NumberFormat` and `formatOptions`; with
the caret in it, the same number is written plainly so it can be edited. `locale` (`en-US`
by default) decides which characters group and separate the number, in and out.

### Bounds and step

`min` and `max` land when the reader leaves the field and on every press of a key — not while
they type, so a reader on their way to `15` with `min={10}` can type the `1`. `step` is how
far one press moves the value (1 by default); from an empty field, a step starts at zero. A
key with nowhere left to go turns grey and stops taking presses.

### Keyboard

A fractional `step`, or `formatOptions` asking for decimals, opens the decimal pad; anything
else opens the number pad. `keyboardType` on `NumberField.Field` overrides it — for a field
that has to take a minus sign.

## Sizes

```tsx
<NumberField size="sm">…</NumberField>
<NumberField size="md">…</NumberField>
<NumberField size="lg">…</NumberField>
```

`size` sets the box's height — 40, 48 or 56 — and the keys' square, 36, 44 or 52 across.

## Colour

The line turns to the theme's accent, read as ink, once the field has the focus. `accent`
picks one of the twenty named Metro accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins when both are
set. `isInvalid` draws the line in the danger colour and outranks both.

## Accessibility

- Each key is a `button`, announced as disabled when it has nowhere left to go. It needs an
  `accessibilityLabel` — a plus is not text — and warns in development without one.
- A key smaller than 48 points reaches past its cell for the touch.
- A press shrinks the key, changes no colour, and every step is felt as a `selection`.
- The field is described by `NumberField.Error` when it is shown; `isRequired` tells a
  screen reader the field has to be filled.

## Differences from Native

- **`NumberField.Group`** is added: Tram has no `FieldGroup`, so the box around the field
  and its keys is the number field's own.
- **No `variant`** and **no `labelPlacement`**, as on the Tram `TextField`.
- **`accent`** and **`isRequired`** are added — the Tram `TextField`'s.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **A spent key** turns grey and out; Native's goes flat.

# NumberPad — @xaui/tram

The keypad a PIN, a code or an amount is typed on, drawn as the Metro dialer: three columns
of digits alone on the ground — light, centred, in the page's ink — with no fill, no line
and no corner around them.

The digits `1` to `9`, the `0` and the backspace are drawn by the root. The one cell you
compose is the free corner of the bottom row, beside the `0` and opposite the backspace. The
pad draws no display: what the value looks like is the screen's.

## Import

```tsx
import { NumberPad } from '@xaui/tram/number-pad'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<NumberPad>
  <NumberPad.Action>
    <NumberPad.Icon />
    <NumberPad.Label />
  </NumberPad.Action>
</NumberPad>
```

- **`NumberPad`** — the root. It draws the grid of digits and the backspace, holds the
  value and applies the edits.
- **`NumberPad.Key`** — a key that inserts its `value`, and shows it when nothing is
  composed inside it. Placed in the free corner, it adds a key of your own — a decimal
  comma, a `00`.
- **`NumberPad.Backspace`** — deletes the last character; a long press empties the value.
  The root draws it for you.
- **`NumberPad.Action`** — a cell that runs its own `onPress`, for the free corner.
- **`NumberPad.Label`** — the text in a cell. Its type follows the cell it is in.
- **`NumberPad.Icon`** — an icon in a cell, in the cell's ink.

Left out, the free corner is an empty cell that keeps the `0` in the middle column.

## Usage

### A code

```tsx
<NumberPad maxLength={4} onChangeText={setCode} onComplete={unlock} />
```

`onComplete` fires once the value reaches `maxLength`. A press past it changes nothing at
all, so `onChangeText` does not fire and a full code cannot be completed twice.

### An amount

```tsx
<Typography variant="section">{`${amount || '0'} €`}</Typography>
<NumberPad value={amount} onChangeText={setAmount}>
  <NumberPad.Key value="," />
</NumberPad>
```

Without `maxLength` the value is unbounded.

### An action in the corner

```tsx
<NumberPad value={code} onChangeText={setCode} maxLength={4}>
  <NumberPad.Action onPress={() => setCode('')} accessibilityLabel="Clear all">
    <NumberPad.Label>clear</NumberPad.Label>
  </NumberPad.Action>
</NumberPad>
```

### Disabled

`isDisabled` on the root greys every key and stops them all. `isDisabled` on one cell
overrides the pad's, so a single key can be out while the rest are live.

### The edits

`appendPadKey`, `removePadKey` and `isPadComplete` — the same edits the pad applies — are
exported from `@xaui/native/number-pad`, for a display or a pad of your own.

## Sizes

```tsx
<NumberPad size="sm" />
<NumberPad size="md" />
<NumberPad size="lg" />
```

`size` sets the keys' height — 48, 56 or 64 — the gaps, and the digits' type (`title`,
`section` or `pivot`). Never a width.

## Accessibility

- Every cell is a `button`, announced as disabled when it is out. A digit key is labelled by
  its value, the backspace "Backspace".
- A `NumberPad.Action` holding an icon or a word needs an `accessibilityLabel` that says what
  it does.
- A press shrinks the key a little and springs back, felt as a `press`; it changes no colour.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`, no `radius`, no `color`**: the keys have no box to fill, round or tint.
- **Disabled** is grey, not dimmed.
- **The press** shrinks the key and changes no colour.

# NumberStepper — @xaui/tram

A quantity and the two presses that move it, drawn the Metro way: two square keys in the
`Button`'s drawing, and the value between them in tabular figures, on the ground.

Nothing is typed, so there is no parse and no late clamp: a value that can only be pressed
into existence is inside its range at every moment. Stepping, clamping and formatting are
Native's.

## Import

```tsx
import { NumberStepper } from '@xaui/tram/number-stepper'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<NumberStepper>
  <NumberStepper.Track />
  <NumberStepper.Decrement />
  <NumberStepper.Value />
  <NumberStepper.Increment />
</NumberStepper>
```

- **`NumberStepper`** — the root, a row holding the value, the bounds and the step.
- **`NumberStepper.Track`** — kept for Native's markup. It draws nothing unless you style it,
  takes no touches and is hidden from screen readers.
- **`NumberStepper.Decrement`** / **`NumberStepper.Increment`** — the two square keys. With
  no children they draw a minus or a plus in bars of 2; pass an `Icon` to replace the mark.
- **`NumberStepper.Value`** — the value formatted, or an em dash while there is none. A
  function child is given the number to write it your own way.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<NumberStepper min={0} max={5} defaultValue={1} onValueChange={setQuantity}>
  <NumberStepper.Decrement accessibilityLabel="One fewer" />
  <NumberStepper.Value />
  <NumberStepper.Increment accessibilityLabel="One more" />
</NumberStepper>
```

A key with nowhere left to go is drawn as a disabled key and stops taking presses.

### Writing the value

```tsx
<NumberStepper.Value>
  {value => `${value ?? 0} ${value === 1 ? 'guest' : 'guests'}`}
</NumberStepper.Value>
```

`formatOptions` (`Intl.NumberFormat`'s options) and `locale` (`en-US` by default) write the
value when `Value` has no children.

### A bin at the floor

```tsx
<NumberStepper.Decrement
  accessibilityLabel={quantity === 1 ? 'Remove from basket' : 'One fewer'}
  onPress={quantity === 1 ? remove : undefined}
>
  {quantity === 1 ? <Icon as={TrashIcon} /> : undefined}
</NumberStepper.Decrement>
```

A key's own `onPress` replaces the step rather than running beside it.

## Variants

The `Button`'s four drawings, on the keys:

| Variant     | Drawn as                             |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `outline`   | a line in the accent's ink (default) |
| `contained` | filled with the accent               |
| `flat`      | filled with its soft slice           |
| `text`      | the bare mark                        |

```tsx
<NumberStepper variant="contained">…</NumberStepper>
```

## Sizes

```tsx
<NumberStepper size="sm">…</NumberStepper>
<NumberStepper size="md">…</NumberStepper>
<NumberStepper size="lg">…</NumberStepper>
```

`size` sets the keys' side — 32, 40 or 48 — the gaps, and the value's type (`body`,
`subtitle` or `title`). Never the width. `radius` overrides the keys' corner, within 2.

## Colour

The keys take the theme's accent. `accent` picks another one of the twenty named Metro
accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins when both are set. The value keeps the page's ink.

## Accessibility

- Each key is a `button`, announced as disabled when it has nowhere left to go. It needs an
  `accessibilityLabel` — a plus is not text — and warns in development without one.
- A key smaller than 48 points reaches past its box for the touch.
- The root row has no role: the controls are the two keys.
- A key tilts toward the finger and leaves its colours alone; every move is felt as a
  `selection`.

## Differences from Native

- **`variant`** is the `Button`'s four drawings — `outline` by default, `contained`, `flat`,
  `text` — for Native's `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary` and `ghost`.
- **No pill**: `Track` is kept for Native's markup and draws nothing unless styled.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **A `selection` haptic** is felt on every move.

# Page — @xaui/tram

A screen that arrives and leaves the Metro way: by default the whole page turns around the
screen's start edge like a door — out on the exit curve, in on the `navigation` spring —
and comes back the same way when it is focused again.

`Page` is Tram's own, with no Native equivalent. It depends on no navigation library: the
app hands its navigator's focus hook to `TramProvider`, and `usePageLeave` plays the way out
before the app navigates. While it is focused, a `Page` is also what a context menu makes
recede.

## Import

```tsx
import { Page, pageScreenOptions, usePageLeave } from '@xaui/tram/page'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Page>{/* the screen */}</Page>
```

- **`Page`** — the root, an animated view that fills the screen with the theme's background,
  edge to edge. It takes `View`'s props and the style props. It has no `asChild`: the root
  is the view that moves.

## Setup

Two things, once, in the layout that holds the navigator.

**The focus hook.** Hand `TramProvider` your navigator's `useIsFocused` — Expo Router's or
React Navigation's. That is how a page learns it was covered or uncovered:

```tsx
import { Stack, useIsFocused } from 'expo-router' // or '@react-navigation/native'
import { pageScreenOptions } from '@xaui/tram/page'
import { TramProvider } from '@xaui/tram/theme'

const PAGES = { useIsFocused }

export default function Layout() {
  return (
    <TramProvider pages={PAGES}>
      <Stack>
        <Stack.Screen name="index" />
        <Stack.Screen name="mail" options={{ ...pageScreenOptions }} />
      </Stack>
    </TramProvider>
  )
}
```

Pass the hook itself, always the same one. Without it a page still arrives, but has no way
out and no way back to play.

**The navigator's animation, per screen.** `pageScreenOptions` (`{ animation: 'none' }`)
turns the navigator's own push and pop off, so the `Page` is the only thing that moves.
Spread it on the screens that render a `Page`, not on the whole `Stack`: a screen that is
not a `Page` would then appear with no animation at all.

## Usage

### A page

```tsx
// app/mail.tsx
export default function Mail() {
  return <Page>{/* … */}</Page>
}
```

Arriving needs nothing else.

### Leaving

```tsx
const leave = usePageLeave()
const router = useRouter()

<Button onPress={() => leave(() => router.push('/mail'))}>mail</Button>
<Button onPress={() => leave(() => router.back(), 'backward')}>back</Button>
```

The focused page turns away, then the function runs. The direction is `forward` by default,
or `backward`. With no `Page` on screen, or no focus hook on the provider, the function runs
at once. A page left without `usePageLeave` — by the system's back or a header button —
still comes back on its own when it is focused again.

### Transitions

```tsx
<TramProvider pages={{ useIsFocused, transition: 'slide' }}>…</TramProvider>

<Page transition="fade">…</Page>
```

| Transition  | Drawn as                                       |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `turnstile` | the page turns around the screen's start edge  |
| `slide`     | the page comes in from the end side, and fades |
| `fade`      | the page fades                                 |
| `none`      | the page is there or it is not                 |

`turnstile` is the default. The provider's `transition` applies to every page; a page's own
`transition` wins.

### The context menu recede

While a `Page` is focused, a `Menu` with a `Menu.Overlay` opened anywhere on it makes it
recede to 95 % around its centre, and the menu's trigger stays in front, in place and at its
size. Nothing needs wiring beyond the setup above.

## Accessibility

- With motion reduced, every transition but `none` becomes a fade, and the page does not
  recede behind a context menu.
- Under an ancestor's `disable-all`, a page is there or it is not, and `leave` navigates at
  once.
- The turnstile's hinge is mirrored in right-to-left layouts.

# Panorama — @xaui/tram

The Metro hub: one wide page slid across section by section under a giant title, the title
and the backdrop travelling slower than the sections so the page reads as one surface seen
through the screen.

`Panorama` is Tram's own, with no Native equivalent. A `Pivot` filters; a `Panorama` shows.
Each section is the screen's width less 48 points, so the start of the next one always
shows at the end. The track does not loop: the last section rests against the screen's end.

## Import

```tsx
import { Panorama } from '@xaui/tram/panorama'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Panorama>
  <Panorama.Background />
  <Panorama.Title />
  <Panorama.Section>
    <Panorama.Header />
  </Panorama.Section>
</Panorama>
```

- **`Panorama`** — the root. It fills what holds it, draws the theme's ground and holds the
  section on screen.
- **`Panorama.Background`** — what lies behind everything, wider than the screen: a picture,
  flat blocks of colour. It travels exactly a quarter as far as the sections.
- **`Panorama.Title`** — the giant title, `hero`, on one line at its natural width and
  clipped by the root. It travels a shorter way than the sections.
- **`Panorama.Section`** — one section, named by its `value`.
- **`Panorama.Header`** — a section's header, on `pivot`, Light, in the page's ink.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Panorama>
  <Panorama.Background>
    <Image source={cover} style={{ flex: 1 }} />
  </Panorama.Background>
  <Panorama.Title>music + videos</Panorama.Title>
  <Panorama.Section value="collection">
    <Panorama.Header>collection</Panorama.Header>
    {/* … */}
  </Panorama.Section>
  <Panorama.Section value="new">
    <Panorama.Header>new</Panorama.Header>
    {/* … */}
  </Panorama.Section>
</Panorama>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<Panorama value={section} onValueChange={setSection}>
  {/* … */}
</Panorama>
```

`value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` work by the sections' `value`, as on `Tabs`.
Without `defaultValue` the first section is shown first. Setting `value` from outside moves
the track.

### The swipe

The sections follow the finger, a third as fast past either end. A release moves on a
section when flung past 500 points per second or dragged a quarter of a section, and
settles on the `navigation` spring, felt as a `selection`. While the track rubber-bands, the
title and the backdrop hold at their ends.

A drag that is mostly vertical stays the section's: a `ScrollView` inside a section scrolls.

### `asChild`

With `asChild`, your one element is the panorama's frame: the slots are written inside it,
and its props and ref merge with the root's.

## Accessibility

- Only the current section is read by a screen reader; the others and the background are
  hidden. `Panorama.Header` is a `header`.
- `Panorama.Title` — or, without one, the current section's header — is `adjustable`, its
  value the section on screen. Its `increment` and `decrement` actions move to the next or
  the previous section.
- With motion reduced, the title and the backdrop stay put and the track fades to its
  section. Under an ancestor's `disable-all` it is placed.
- The track is mirrored in right-to-left layouts.

# PhoneNumberField — @xaui/tram

A national phone number beside its country, with a searchable list of countries — drawn in
Metro as the Tram `TextField`'s box with the country as a key at its start (its ISO code,
its calling code and a small chevron, ruled off from the number), and the countries in the
Tram `BottomSheet`, a band in the theme's contrast.

It is a `TextField`: the root is the Tram `TextField`'s, and `Label`, `Description` and
`Error` are its slots. The value, the pasting of an international number, the formatting on
blur and the E.164 read are Native's own helpers.

`libphonenumber-js` is an optional peer, and this component needs it. It is imported from
its subpath only, never from the package root.

## Import

```tsx
import { FieldGroup } from '@xaui/tram/field-group'
import { PhoneNumberField, usePhoneNumberField } from '@xaui/tram/phone-number-field'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<PhoneNumberField>
  <PhoneNumberField.Label />
  <FieldGroup>
    <FieldGroup.Prefix>
      <PhoneNumberField.Country />
    </FieldGroup.Prefix>
    <PhoneNumberField.Field />
  </FieldGroup>
  <PhoneNumberField.Description />
  <PhoneNumberField.Error />
  <PhoneNumberField.Overlay />
  <PhoneNumberField.Content>
    <PhoneNumberField.Title />
    <PhoneNumberField.Close />
    <PhoneNumberField.Search />
    <PhoneNumberField.CountryList />
  </PhoneNumberField.Content>
</PhoneNumberField>
```

- **`PhoneNumberField`** — the root, the Tram `TextField`'s, plus the number and its country.
- **`PhoneNumberField.Label`** / **`.Description`** / **`.Error`** — the `TextField`'s slots.
- **`PhoneNumberField.Country`** — the key that opens the list: the ISO code in `caption`,
  the calling code in the field's type in tabular figures, and a chevron. It is
  `BottomSheet.Trigger` and goes in `FieldGroup.Prefix`; children replace the drawing.
- **`PhoneNumberField.Field`** — the input for the national number.
- **`PhoneNumberField.Overlay`** — the dimmed ground behind the list, `BottomSheet.Overlay`.
- **`PhoneNumberField.Content`** — the band, `BottomSheet.Content` itself.
- **`PhoneNumberField.Title`** / **`.Close`** — the band's title and its cross.
- **`PhoneNumberField.Search`** — the Tram `SearchField`'s field. The query is the root's.
- **`PhoneNumberField.CountryList`** — a `FlatList` of rows of 48: the ISO code, the name and
  the calling code, the current one in the accent. `renderCountry` replaces a row's
  contents and keeps its selection.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<PhoneNumberField locale="fr" defaultValue={{ country: 'FR', nationalNumber: '' }}>
  <PhoneNumberField.Label>phone</PhoneNumberField.Label>
  <FieldGroup>
    <FieldGroup.Prefix>
      <PhoneNumberField.Country accessibilityLabel="Choose country" />
    </FieldGroup.Prefix>
    <PhoneNumberField.Field placeholder="06 12 34 56 78" />
  </FieldGroup>
  <PhoneNumberField.Overlay />
  <PhoneNumberField.Content>
    <PhoneNumberField.Title>choose a country</PhoneNumberField.Title>
    <PhoneNumberField.Close accessibilityLabel="Close" />
    <PhoneNumberField.Search
      accessibilityLabel="Search country"
      placeholder="country"
    />
    <PhoneNumberField.CountryList />
  </PhoneNumberField.Content>
</PhoneNumberField>
```

### The value

The value is `{ country: 'FR', nationalNumber: '0612345678' }`; `value` and `onValueChange`
make the field controlled. Changing country keeps the national text. Pasting a complete
international number selects its country, when `countries` allows it. Formatting runs on
blur, so deleting does not fight the inserted spaces.

```tsx
function E164() {
  const { phoneNumber } = usePhoneNumberField()
  return (
    <PhoneNumberField.Description>{phoneNumber ?? '—'}</PhoneNumberField.Description>
  )
}
```

`usePhoneNumberField().phoneNumber` is the number in E.164 when it is possible — a length
check, not proof that it is assigned — and `null` otherwise.

### Countries and locale

`countries` restricts the list; the initial country must belong to it. `locale` (`en` by
default) gives the countries' names and their alphabetical order. The search matches a
name, an ISO code or a calling code.

## Sizes

```tsx
<PhoneNumberField size="sm">…</PhoneNumberField>
<PhoneNumberField size="md">…</PhoneNumberField>
<PhoneNumberField size="lg">…</PhoneNumberField>
```

`size` is the `TextField`'s: the box's height — 40, 48 or 56 — its padding and its type.

## Colour

The line turns to the theme's accent, read as ink, once the field has the focus; the current
country in the list is drawn in the accent. `accent` picks one of the twenty named Metro
accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins when both are set. `isInvalid` draws the line in
the danger colour.

## Accessibility

- `PhoneNumberField.Country` is a `button` whose value is the country and its calling code.
  Give it an `accessibilityLabel` in your app's language.
- A country row is a `button` labelled with its name and calling code, and announced as
  `selected` when it is the current one. Choosing one is felt as a `selection`.
- `PhoneNumberField.Search` has no label above it: give it an `accessibilityLabel`.
- `isDisabled` stops both the typing and the choice of country.

## Differences from Native

- **No `Handle`**: the Tram `BottomSheet` has none.
- **The country** shows its ISO code where Native draws a flag.
- **No `variant`**; **`accent`** is added.
- **`Content`** is `BottomSheet.Content` itself; **`Search`** is the `SearchField`'s field.
- **The rows** are Tram rows, not `Button`s with a check mark.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.

# PieChart — @xaui/tram

The whole and its parts, drawn as a ring in Metro flat colour: one shade of an accent per
slice, the ground showing through a drawn gap between them, and what sits in the hole
written in React Native.

A ring is square rather than framed, so it draws its own geometry instead of sitting in the
shared plot of the other charts. It can still sit in a `Chart` frame, which hands it its
`accent`, `size` and `color`.

## Import

```tsx
import { PieChart } from '@xaui/tram/pie-chart'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<PieChart>{/* the middle */}</PieChart>
```

- **`PieChart`** — the root, a square view holding the ring. Its ref is that view.
- **children** — what sits in the hole: a `View` laid over the ring, centred, that takes no
  touches. It is drawn only when there are children.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<PieChart data={rows} labelKey="device" valueKey="sessions" />
```

Each row is a slice; `valueKey` is the quantity, and each slice is its share of the total.
`labelKey` names the slice — what a legend would print.

### The middle

```tsx
<PieChart data={rows} labelKey="device" valueKey="sessions">
  <Typography variant="section">4.5 k</Typography>
  <Typography variant="caption" color={theme.colors.muted}>
    sessions
  </Typography>
</PieChart>
```

The middle is React Native rather than SVG text, so it takes the theme's font and the
platform's text size like everything else on the screen.

### Pie, not ring

```tsx
<PieChart data={rows} labelKey="browser" valueKey="share" innerRadius={0} gap={0} />
```

`innerRadius` is a fraction of the radius, not points, so the hole stays in proportion at
every size: `0.62` by default, `0` for a pie. `gap` is in degrees between two slices,
`1.5` by default, `0` to leave them touching.

### With a legend

```tsx
<Chart seriesCount={rows.length}>
  <Chart.Header>
    <Chart.Heading>
      <Chart.Title>devices</Chart.Title>
    </Chart.Heading>
  </Chart.Header>
  <PieChart data={rows} labelKey="device" valueKey="sessions" />
  <Chart.Footer>
    <Chart.Legend labels={rows.map(row => row.device)} />
  </Chart.Footer>
</Chart>
```

## Sizes

```tsx
<PieChart size="sm" data={rows} labelKey="device" valueKey="sessions" />
<PieChart size="md" data={rows} labelKey="device" valueKey="sessions" />
<PieChart size="lg" data={rows} labelKey="device" valueKey="sessions" />
```

`size` is the ring's diameter: 140, 200 or 260.

## Colour

The palette is walked out of one colour, a shade per slice. `accent` picks one of the
twenty named Metro accents — the intents are `green`, `amber` and `red` — and `color` takes
a raw tint and wins when both are set. Inside a `Chart`, the frame's appearance is the
default.

```tsx
<PieChart accent="orange" data={rows} labelKey="device" valueKey="sessions" />
```

`isDisabled` dims the ring.

## Accessibility

- The ring is a plain `View` with no role. Its `View` props are passed through: give it
  `accessible` and an `accessibilityLabel` that says what the parts are.
- The middle is ordinary text and is read as such.

## Differences from Native

- **`accent`** replaces `variant`: the palette's seed is one of the twenty named accents,
  the intents being `green`, `amber` and `red`.
- **A single slice** takes no gap and draws a full ring.
- **A row at zero** draws nothing; Native keeps a hairline at the seam.

# Pivot — @xaui/tram

The Metro pivot: giant titles in a row that loops, over the section they name — the current
title on the margin in the page's ink, the others grey after it, and the whole row sliding
with the sections under the finger.

`Pivot` is Tram's own, with no Native equivalent. A `Pivot` filters one set of things
several ways; a `Panorama` shows several things. It is not `Tabs`: it has no size and no
rule, and past the last section the first one comes back.

## Import

```tsx
import { Pivot } from '@xaui/tram/pivot'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Pivot>
  <Pivot.Title />
  <Pivot.Header />
  <Pivot.Section />
</Pivot>
```

- **`Pivot`** — the root. It fills what holds it, draws the theme's ground and holds the
  section on screen.
- **`Pivot.Title`** — the app's name above the titles, on `caption` in the page's ink. It
  does not move. Its case is the app's.
- **`Pivot.Header`** — one title of the row, on `pivot`, Light, tied to its section by its
  `value`. It is written beside the sections and laid by the root in the loop's order.
- **`Pivot.Section`** — one section, named by its `value`. The order of the sections is the
  loop's.

`Pivot.Header` and `Pivot.Section` are direct children of the root: it sorts its children
and never reads a grandchild.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Pivot defaultValue="all">
  <Pivot.Title>MAIL</Pivot.Title>
  <Pivot.Header value="all">all</Pivot.Header>
  <Pivot.Header value="unread">unread</Pivot.Header>
  <Pivot.Header value="flagged">flagged</Pivot.Header>
  <Pivot.Section value="all">{/* … */}</Pivot.Section>
  <Pivot.Section value="unread">{/* … */}</Pivot.Section>
  <Pivot.Section value="flagged">{/* … */}</Pivot.Section>
</Pivot>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<Pivot value={filter} onValueChange={setFilter}>
  {/* … */}
</Pivot>
```

`value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` work by the sections' `value`. Without
`defaultValue` the first section is shown first.

### Moving through it

A swipe across the screen drags the loop a section per screen width: the titles slide by
their own advance and fade between grey and ink, the sections slide a screen apart and
fade. A release moves on a section either way, round the loop, when flung past 500 points
per second or dragged a quarter of the screen, and settles on the `navigation` spring, felt
as a `selection`.

A title pressed — or a `value` set from outside — is reached going forward, the way the row
slides. On the web, the arrow keys step either way and move the focus.

A drag that is mostly vertical stays the section's: a `ScrollView` inside a section
scrolls. Every section stays mounted.

### `asChild`

With `asChild`, your one element is the pivot's frame: the slots are written inside it, and
its props and ref merge with the root's.

## Accessibility

- The row is a `tablist`, the titles `tab`s and the sections `tabpanel`s; only the current
  section is read by a screen reader. `Pivot.Title` is a `header`.
- With motion reduced, the titles are laid for the nearest section and the sections fade
  where they stand. Under an ancestor's `disable-all` it is placed.
- The row is mirrored in right-to-left layouts.

# ProgressBar — @xaui/tram

How far along something is, drawn the Metro way: a bar of soft grey with nearly square
corners, filled with the accent — or, when the duration is unknown, five bubbles of the
accent that run across it.

## Import

```tsx
import { ProgressBar } from '@xaui/tram/progress-bar'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ProgressBar>
  <ProgressBar.Header>
    <ProgressBar.Label />
    <ProgressBar.Value />
  </ProgressBar.Header>
  <ProgressBar.Track>
    <ProgressBar.Fill />
  </ProgressBar.Track>
</ProgressBar>
```

- **`ProgressBar`** — the root. It holds the value within the range once and hands the
  result and the resolved styles to its slots.
- **`ProgressBar.Header`** — the line above the bar, the label and the value pushed apart.
- **`ProgressBar.Label`** — what is happening.
- **`ProgressBar.Value`** — how far along, as text. It formats itself; children replace
  it.
- **`ProgressBar.Track`** — the bar: the whole of the distance.
- **`ProgressBar.Fill`** — what is done of it, a child the track clips. On an
  indeterminate bar it draws the five bubbles instead.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<ProgressBar value={40}>download</ProgressBar>
```

A text child becomes the label, and the bar comes with it. With no children at all it is
the bar alone — give it an `accessibilityLabel`.

```tsx
<ProgressBar value={40} size="sm" accessibilityLabel="download" />
```

### The range and the number

```tsx
<ProgressBar value={7} minValue={5} maxValue={10} />
<ProgressBar
  value={1250}
  maxValue={2000}
  formatOptions={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR', maximumFractionDigits: 0 }}
>
  collected
</ProgressBar>
```

`0` to `100` by default; the value is held within the range. `formatOptions` is
`Intl.NumberFormat`'s and is what `ProgressBar.Value` reads — a percentage unless told
otherwise. The value is set in tabular figures, so it does not push the label as it ticks.

### Composed

```tsx
<ProgressBar value={7} minValue={5} maxValue={10}>
  <ProgressBar.Header>
    <ProgressBar.Label>step</ProgressBar.Label>
    <ProgressBar.Value>3 of 6</ProgressBar.Value>
  </ProgressBar.Header>
  <ProgressBar.Track>
    <ProgressBar.Fill />
  </ProgressBar.Track>
</ProgressBar>
```

### Indeterminate

```tsx
<ProgressBar isIndeterminate>connecting</ProgressBar>
```

The bar gives way to five bubbles that come in fast, close up in the middle without
overlapping, and leave fast. `value` is not read, and `ProgressBar.Value` writes only the
children it is handed.

### The motion

The fill reaches a new value on a spring with next to no bounce.
`<ProgressBar.Fill animation={false} />` puts it at its width at once — for a value the
caller already animates — and stands the bubbles still.

## Sizes

```tsx
<ProgressBar size="sm" value={30} />
<ProgressBar size="md" value={55} />
<ProgressBar size="lg" value={70} />
```

`size` sets the bar's thickness — 8, 12 or 16 — and the header's type, never the width.
`radius` overrides the corner of the bar and of its fill; every key stays within 2.

## Colour

The fill and the bubbles are the theme's accent. `accent` picks another of the twenty
named accents; `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins when both are set.

```tsx
<ProgressBar value={60} accent="lime">
  sync
</ProgressBar>
```

`isDisabled` greys the fill and the header and dims the bar.

## Accessibility

- The root has the `progressbar` role and reads the caller's own range,
  `{ min, max, now }`, not the clamped fraction. On the web it sets the matching
  `aria-value*` attributes.
- An indeterminate bar has no value to read: it announces as busy.
- The label is a `Text` inside the root, read with the value.
- Under reduced motion the fill moves on a 150 ms timing, and the five bubbles stand in a
  row in the middle of the bar.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`.** Native colours the fill by intention (`primary`, `success`,
  `danger`…); Tram has one colour to spend — the accent, another `accent`, or a raw
  `color`.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **`isIndeterminate`** is added: the Metro bar's five bubbles. Native leaves an unknown
  duration to its `Spinner`.
- **The bar** is 8 / 12 / 16 thick with nearly square corners; Native's is a thinner,
  rounded rail.
- **The fill** moves through Tram's motion (a spring, or 150 ms under reduced motion)
  rather than a fixed 240 ms sweep.

# RadarChart — @xaui/tram

Several quantities at once, each on its own axis, drawn the Metro way: rings and spokes
in lines of 1 of the faint grey, each series a polygon with sharp corners, a stroke of 2
and a flat fill, and the axis names in `caption` around the web.

## Import

```tsx
import { RadarChart } from '@xaui/tram/radar-chart'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<RadarChart data={rows} axisKey="skill" yKeys={['alice', 'bob']} />
```

- **`RadarChart`** — one element with no slots: the web, the series and the axis names
  are drawn from the props. It can stand alone, or sit in a `Chart` frame that gives it a
  title, a legend and its palette.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<RadarChart
  data={[
    { skill: 'speed', alice: 80, bob: 55 },
    { skill: 'stamina', alice: 65, bob: 90 },
    { skill: 'aim', alice: 92, bob: 70 },
  ]}
  axisKey="skill"
  yKeys={['alice', 'bob']}
  maxValue={100}
/>
```

### The data is transposed

A row is an **axis**, not a reading along one: `axisKey` names each axis and `yKeys` are
the series, in the order the palette walks them. The vertices are the axes, so the edges
are always straight. Fewer than three axes draws nothing.

### A common top

Unset, `maxValue` is the highest reading in this chart, so its shape compares the measures
within it and says nothing about any other radar. Give every radar on a screen the same
`maxValue` to compare them.

### In a frame

```tsx
<Chart seriesCount={2} accent="cobalt">
  <Chart.Header>
    <Chart.Heading>
      <Chart.Title>profile</Chart.Title>
      <Chart.Description>Out of 100, one scale for all</Chart.Description>
    </Chart.Heading>
    <Chart.Legend labels={['Alice', 'Bob']} />
  </Chart.Header>
  <RadarChart
    data={skills}
    axisKey="skill"
    yKeys={['alice', 'bob']}
    maxValue={100}
  />
</Chart>
```

The frame's `accent`, `color` and `size` are defaults; the radar's own props win.

### As a glyph

```tsx
<RadarChart
  data={skills}
  axisKey="skill"
  yKeys={['alice']}
  hasLabels={false}
  hasPoints
  levels={3}
  size="sm"
/>
```

`hasLabels={false}` hands the whole box to the web. `hasPoints` draws a square of 6 at
every vertex. `levels` sets the number of rings (4 by default), `fillOpacity` the share of
colour in a series' fill (0.18), and `strokeWidth` the outline (2).

## Sizes

```tsx
<RadarChart size="sm" {...props} />
<RadarChart size="md" {...props} />
<RadarChart size="lg" {...props} />
```

`size` is the web's square box — 180, 240 or 300 — before the labels are given room.

## Colour

The series wear shades of one colour, walked out of the theme's accent. `accent` seeds
the palette with another of the twenty named accents; `color` seeds it with a raw tint and
wins when both are set. `isDisabled` dims the figure.

```tsx
<RadarChart accent="magenta" {...props} />
```

## Accessibility

- The figure sets no role and reads nothing by itself: give it an `accessibilityLabel`
  that states what it shows, or put the numbers beside it in text.
- Nothing moves, so there is nothing for reduced motion to change.

## Differences from Native

- **`accent`** replaces `variant`, as across the chart family: it seeds the palette with
  a named accent's true colour. `color` still wins.
- **The drawing**: rings and spokes in lines of 1 of the faint grey, mitred polygons, and
  square points where Native draws dots. The API is otherwise Native's.

# RadialChart — @xaui/tram

Several quantities, each as far round its own ring as it has got, drawn the Metro way:
rings cut square at their ends, over a track of the faint grey.

A ring is not a slice. A `PieChart` splits one quantity into shares of a whole; a
`RadialChart` draws quantities that have nothing to do with each other — calories, steps,
minutes — each against a target of its own.

## Import

```tsx
import { RadialChart } from '@xaui/tram/radial-chart'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<RadialChart data={rows} labelKey="label" valueKey="value">
  {/* what sits in the middle */}
</RadialChart>
```

- **`RadialChart`** — one element with no slots: the rings and their tracks are drawn from
  the props. Its `children` are laid over the middle of the canvas, as React Native, and
  take no touches. It can stand alone or sit in a `Chart` frame.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<RadialChart
  data={[
    { label: 'calories', value: 1623, target: 2000 },
    { label: 'steps', value: 5400, target: 10000 },
    { label: 'exercise', value: 25, target: 120 },
  ]}
  labelKey="label"
  valueKey="value"
  maxKey="target"
/>
```

The first row is the outermost ring, and the palette walks the rows in that order.

### The targets

| What you have            | What you write                         |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| a goal per row           | `maxKey="target"`                      |
| one goal for all of them | `maxValue={2000}`                      |
| no goal at all           | neither — the largest value is the top |

A row's own target wins over `maxValue`. A reading of zero or below draws no arc; a
reading past its target closes its ring.

### The middle

```tsx
<RadialChart data={activity} labelKey="label" valueKey="value" maxKey="target">
  <Typography variant="section">81 %</Typography>
  <Typography variant="caption">calories</Typography>
</RadialChart>
```

### The rings

```tsx
<RadialChart
  data={activity}
  labelKey="label"
  valueKey="value"
  maxKey="target"
  hasTrack={false}
  thickness={20}
  gap={2}
  size="sm"
/>
```

`thickness` sets every ring's width in points and wins over `size`; `gap` is the bare
