ground between two rings, half the thickness by default. When the rings ask for more room
than the box has, they thin rather than drop. `hasTrack={false}` leaves out the grey
behind each ring — for a figure used as a glyph.

## Sizes

```tsx
<RadialChart size="sm" {...props} />
<RadialChart size="md" {...props} />
<RadialChart size="lg" {...props} />
```

`size` is the outermost ring's diameter — 140, 200 or 260 — and its thickness — 10, 14
or 18.

## Colour

The rings wear shades of one colour, walked out of the theme's accent. `accent` seeds the
palette with another of the twenty named accents; `color` seeds it with a raw tint and
wins when both are set. Inside a `Chart`, the frame's `accent`, `color` and `size` are the
defaults. `isDisabled` dims the figure.

```tsx
<RadialChart color="#1BA1E2" {...props} />
```

## Accessibility

- The figure sets no role and reads nothing by itself: give it an `accessibilityLabel`
  that states the readings, or write them in the middle or beside it.
- The middle takes no touches, so it never blocks a press meant for what is under it.
- Nothing moves, so there is nothing for reduced motion to change.

## Differences from Native

- **`accent`** replaces `variant`, as across the chart family: it seeds the palette with a
  named accent's true colour. `color` still wins.
- **The ends of a ring** are cut square (`butt`); Native rounds them.
- **An empty ring** draws no arc at all.
- The thinning, the per-row targets and the quarter turn of the canvas are Native's.

# Radio — @xaui/tram

One option out of a set, drawn the Metro way: a circle with a line around it on the page's
ground, and a dot of the accent inside once it is the chosen one.

## Import

```tsx
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from '@xaui/tram/radio'
```

`RadioGroup` is `Radio.Group` under another name, for a call site that reads better naming
the set.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Radio.Group>
  <Radio>
    <Radio.Indicator />
    <Radio.Label />
  </Radio>
</Radio.Group>
```

- **`Radio.Group`** — the set. It holds the chosen `value` and hands `size`, `accent` and
  `color` down as defaults.
- **`Radio`** — one option, and the whole row: a tap on the label chooses it too. A text
  child becomes the label and the root supplies the circle; with no children it is the
  circle alone.
- **`Radio.Indicator`** — the circle and its dot. Children replace the dot and keep its
  motion and its place.
- **`Radio.Label`** — the text beside the circle.

## Usage

### In a group

```tsx
<Radio.Group value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan}>
  <Radio value="monthly">monthly</Radio>
  <Radio value="yearly">yearly</Radio>
</Radio.Group>
```

An option joins the set by naming a `value`; nothing walks the children, so an option
nested in a row is in the set as much as a direct child. Leave `value` out of the group
and it holds its own, starting from `defaultValue`. A press selects and never clears:
`onValueChange` is never called with `undefined`.

### Composed

```tsx
<Radio value="yearly" accent="lime">
  <Radio.Indicator />
  <Radio.Label>yearly</Radio.Label>
</Radio>
```

### Alone

```tsx
<Radio isSelected={isMuted} onSelectedChange={() => setIsMuted(true)}>
  muted
</Radio>
```

Outside a group, a radio runs on its own `isSelected` / `defaultSelected`.
`onSelectedChange` fires with `true` only.

### Orientation

```tsx
<Radio.Group orientation="horizontal" defaultValue="m">
  <Radio value="s">small</Radio>
  <Radio value="m">medium</Radio>
  <Radio value="l">large</Radio>
</Radio.Group>
```

`vertical` is the default. `horizontal` wraps rather than overflowing.

### Disabled and invalid

```tsx
<Radio.Group defaultValue="card" isInvalid>
  <Radio value="card">card</Radio>
  <Radio value="transfer" isDisabled>
    transfer
  </Radio>
</Radio.Group>
```

`isDisabled` greys the circle, the dot and the label and stops the press; a disabled set
has no option that can opt back in. `isInvalid` draws the circle's line and the dot in
`danger`, and the label keeps its ink.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Radio size="sm">sm</Radio>
<Radio size="md">md</Radio>
<Radio size="lg">lg</Radio>
```

`size` sets the circle (20, 26 or 34 across), the dot, the gap and the label's type —
never the width. Every size is pressed as 48 points.

## Colour

The dot is the theme's accent. `accent` picks another of the twenty named accents; `color`
takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins when both are set. The circle's line stays the page's ink.
An option's own paint wins over its group's, and `isInvalid` overrides both.

```tsx
<Radio.Group accent="cobalt" defaultValue="a">
  <Radio value="a">cobalt</Radio>
  <Radio value="b" accent="magenta">
    magenta
  </Radio>
</Radio.Group>
```

## Accessibility

- An option has the `radio` role and announces `checked` and `disabled`; on the web it
  sets `aria-checked` and `aria-invalid`. The group has the `radiogroup` role.
- A choice is felt as a `selection` haptic through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`, only when
  the choice moves.
- The dot grows from the centre on a spring. Under reduced motion it fades in and out at
  its full size, and the row no longer shrinks under the finger.
- `animation={false}` keeps the row its full size under the finger; `'disable-all'` also
  places the dot with no spring.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`.** Native's three are three fills of the circle at rest; the Metro circle
  has no fill.
- **No `radius`.** A radio is a circle.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **The press** shrinks the row and fills nothing: no highlight, no ripple.
- **`isInvalid`** leaves the label its ink: the circle says which option is wrong.
- **The set** spaces its options on a pitch of 48.

# RangeCalendar — @xaui/tram

A month, and the period chosen in it, drawn as the Tram `Calendar`: the two ends are the
accent's flat squares and the days between them its soft slice, filling their cells edge
to edge so the period reads as one strip across the weeks.

It is the Tram `Calendar` — the same root, header, chevrons, weekday headings and paging.
Only the day differs.

## Import

```tsx
import { RangeCalendar } from '@xaui/tram/range-calendar'
```

`DateRange` and `RangePosition` are re-exported as types.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<RangeCalendar>
  <RangeCalendar.Header>
    <RangeCalendar.Title />
    <RangeCalendar.PreviousButton />
    <RangeCalendar.NextButton />
  </RangeCalendar.Header>
  <RangeCalendar.Weekdays />
  <RangeCalendar.Grid>
    {date => <RangeCalendar.Day date={date} />}
  </RangeCalendar.Grid>
</RangeCalendar>
```

- **`RangeCalendar`** — the root: the `Calendar`'s root holding a period instead of a day.
- **`RangeCalendar.Header`**, **`.Title`**, **`.PreviousButton`**, **`.NextButton`**,
  **`.Weekdays`** — the `Calendar`'s own slots, re-exported. The title names the month
  through the locale; the chevrons point up and down and step a month.
- **`RangeCalendar.Grid`** — six weeks of squares. With no children it draws a
  `RangeCalendar.Day` in every cell; a function child of your own wins.
- **`RangeCalendar.Day`** — one day and its place in the period: an end, a day between, or
  neither.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
const [stay, setStay] = useState<DateRange>({ start: null, end: null })

<RangeCalendar value={stay} onValueChange={setStay}>
  <RangeCalendar.Header>
    <RangeCalendar.Title />
    <View style={{ flexDirection: 'row' }}>
      <RangeCalendar.PreviousButton accessibilityLabel="previous month" />
      <RangeCalendar.NextButton accessibilityLabel="next month" />
    </View>
  </RangeCalendar.Header>
  <RangeCalendar.Weekdays />
  <RangeCalendar.Grid />
</RangeCalendar>
```

Leave `value` out and the calendar holds its own period, from `defaultValue`. The month on
screen opens on the period's start, and is its own state (`month`, `defaultMonth`,
`onMonthChange`).

### Three presses

| The state        | Pressing a day                       |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| nothing chosen   | it becomes the start                 |
| a start, no end  | on or after it → it becomes the end  |
| a start, no end  | before it → it becomes the new start |
| both ends chosen | a new period starts from it          |

A one-day period is allowed and draws as one square.

### Bounds and locale

```tsx
<RangeCalendar
  minValue={today}
  maxValue={inSixMonths}
  locale="en-GB"
  firstDayOfWeek={1}
/>
```

Days outside `minValue` / `maxValue` are the faint grey and inert. `locale` names the
months and the weekdays; `firstDayOfWeek` is read from it when unset.

## Sizes

```tsx
<RangeCalendar size="sm" />
<RangeCalendar size="md" />
<RangeCalendar size="lg" />
```

`size` sets the cell's height — 36, 42 or 48 — and the type in it. The grid spans its
parent.

## Colour

The ends are the theme's accent; the days between are its soft slice at 30 %. `accent`
picks another of the twenty named accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins when both
are set. `isDisabled` greys the calendar and stops every day.

```tsx
<RangeCalendar accent="magenta" size="sm" />
```

## Accessibility

- A day has the `button` role, is named by its full date in the locale, and announces
  `selected` while it is part of the period and `disabled` when out of bounds.
- The chevrons are `button`s with no text: give each an `accessibilityLabel`.
- A press shrinks the cell and is felt as a `selection` haptic.
- The next month rises from below as it fades in; under reduced motion it only fades.

## Differences from Native

- Those of the Tram `Calendar`: **no `variant`**, **no `radius`**, **no `xs`**, **no
  `asChild`**; **`accent`** is added; no today dot — today is a square lined in the ink.
- **The band**: no half band hidden under a disc. A Tram day is a square that fills its
  cell, so the period runs edge to edge.

# Rating — @xaui/tram

A row of marks, given or shown, drawn the Metro way: flat marks, the given ones in the
accent and the rest in a faint grey, an average filling the last mark to the tenth.

One component serves the input and the average: a mark's fill is a fraction, so `4.3`
shows three tenths of the fifth mark.

## Import

```tsx
import { Rating } from '@xaui/tram/rating'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Rating>
  <Rating.Icon />
</Rating>
```

- **`Rating`** — the root. It draws `max` marks in a row and holds the value.
- **`Rating.Icon`** — the glyph, written once and drawn once per mark, in both layers: the
  faint grey, and the given colour clipped to the fraction. Left out, the mark is a star.
  It takes `Icon`'s forms (`as`, a raw SVG child, or `source`).
- **`Rating.Item`** — one mark, pressable. The root draws `max` of them for you, each
  holding the glyph.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Rating value={score} onValueChange={setScore} />
```

Leave `value` out and the rating keeps its own, from `defaultValue` (0). `max` sets how
many marks: five by default.

### Read-only

```tsx
<Rating value={4.3} isReadOnly size="sm" />
```

A display rather than a control: the marks take no press and the row reads as one image,
"4.3 out of 5".

### Precision

```tsx
<Rating value={half} onValueChange={setHalf} precision={0.5} />
```

`precision` is the step a press lands on — `1` for whole marks, `0.5` for halves. It
governs input only: a value of any precision is shown as it is. A press is measured from
the start edge of the mark, mirrored in a row read right to left.

### Another glyph

```tsx
<Rating value={score} onValueChange={setScore} accent="teal">
  <Rating.Icon as={HeartIcon} />
</Rating>
```

An explicit `color` on `Rating.Icon` wins over both layers.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Rating size="sm" value={3} isReadOnly />
<Rating size="md" value={3.5} isReadOnly />
<Rating size="lg" value={4} isReadOnly />
```

`size` sets the mark's side — 16, 24 or 32 — and the gap between marks (4, 6 or 8). Every
mark is pressed as 48 points.

## Colour

The given marks are the theme's accent. `accent` picks another of the twenty named
accents; `color` takes a raw tint — the amber of a store, the page's ink — and wins when
both are set. The marks not given yet are always the faint grey.

```tsx
<Rating accent="amber" defaultValue={3} />
<Rating color={theme.colors.foreground} defaultValue={2} />
```

## Accessibility

- An input rating is a row of `button`s, each carrying its place as a value
  (`{ now, min: 1, max }`) and its `disabled` state.
- A read-only rating is one element labelled "value out of max"; its marks are `image`s.
- Each change is felt as a `selection` haptic through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`.
- A press shrinks the mark a little and springs back; the fill changes at once. Under
  reduced motion the mark does not move.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`.** Native has three fills for the given marks; Tram fills them with the
  accent, `accent` names another and `color` writes one as a raw tint.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **The marks** are flat: a mark not given yet is the faint grey of the `Skeleton`, and a
  given one does not grow, glow or bounce.

# Scaffold — @xaui/tram

The app's chrome in Tram: the ground under every screen, the status bar over it, and the
options the app's navigator is dressed with — drawn flat, with no shadow, and the title at
the start of its line.

`Scaffold` depends on no navigator. `Scaffold.Navigator` clones the app's own navigator
and merges the theme's options under its `screenOptions`, so a Stack, Tabs or a Drawer —
Expo Router or React Navigation — are dressed by the same component. Routing, the safe
area and the colour-mode toggle stay the app's.

## Import

```tsx
import { Scaffold } from '@xaui/tram/scaffold'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Scaffold>
  <Scaffold.StatusBar />
  <Scaffold.Navigator>{/* the app's navigator */}</Scaffold.Navigator>
</Scaffold>
```

- **`Scaffold`** — the ground: a view in the page's colour under every screen. It resolves
  the chrome once and hands it to its slots.
- **`Scaffold.StatusBar`** — React Native's own `StatusBar`, in the ink that reads on the
  header's ground. Every `StatusBarProps` is accepted, and what you write wins.
- **`Scaffold.Navigator`** — takes exactly one element, the app's navigator, and clones it
  with the theme's screen options. It has no `asChild` and no default element, and throws
  when handed anything else.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <TramProvider colorMode={colorMode}>
      <Scaffold>
        <Scaffold.StatusBar />
        <Scaffold.Navigator>
          <Stack screenOptions={{ headerRight: () => <ThemeToggle /> }}>
            <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: 'home' }} />
          </Stack>
        </Scaffold.Navigator>
      </Scaffold>
    </TramProvider>
  )
}
```

`Scaffold` sits under `TramProvider`, which resolves the theme it reads.

### The merge gives the app the last word

The theme's options go **under** the navigator's own, through Native's
`mergeScreenOptions`: the style keys blend, every other key is the app's, and a function
`screenOptions` stays a function.

```tsx
<Scaffold.Navigator>
  <Stack screenOptions={{ headerStyle: { height: 96 } }} />
</Scaffold.Navigator>
// → headerStyle: { backgroundColor: <theme>, height: 96 }
```

The options are Native's five — `headerStyle`, `headerTintColor`, `headerTitleStyle`,
`headerShadowVisible` (always `false`) and `contentStyle` — and a sixth,
`headerTitleAlign: 'left'`. iOS's native stack ignores the alignment and keeps its title
centred.

### With Tram pages

A screen that renders a Tram [`Page`](/docs/components/page?package=tram) carries its own transition. Turn
the navigator's animation off on those screens, one by one, with `pageScreenOptions` from
`@xaui/tram/page`.

### `useScaffold`

```tsx
const { screenOptions, statusBar } = useScaffold()
```

The resolved values, for a chrome the slots do not reach — a drawer's `drawerStyle`, a tab
bar, an Android navigation-bar module.

### `asChild`

```tsx
<Scaffold asChild>
  <GestureHandlerRootView />
</Scaffold>
```

Merges the ground into the view the app already has. The ground's `ViewStyle` keys are
props too, so `backgroundColor` lets a page painted from an image show through.

## Variants

How much the header separates from the page:

| Variant     | The header                                          |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `ghost`     | the page's ground, no edge — the default            |
| `tertiary`  | the page's ground, closed by a line of 2 in `muted` |
| `secondary` | the discreet surface                                |
| `primary`   | a flat fill of the accent, its ink `onAccent`       |

Metro had no bar at all — the app's name and the page's title sat on the ground — which
is why `ghost` stays the default. The title is on the Tram `title` role, SemiLight.

## Colour

`accent` picks one of the twenty named accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins. Either
fills the bar of a `primary` or a `secondary`, and is the title's ink — read on the page —
on a `tertiary` or a `ghost`.

```tsx
<Scaffold variant="primary" accent="lime">
  …
</Scaffold>
```

## Accessibility

- The status bar's ink is the one that reads on the header's own ground: a lime bar gets
  dark icons in the dark mode too. Under `primary` and `secondary`, its Android background
  is the bar's colour.
- The back arrow and the header's icons follow the title's ink (`headerTintColor`).
- Nothing here moves; transitions belong to the navigator.

## Differences from Native

- **`accent`** is added: it fills the bar of `primary` and `secondary`, and is the title's
  ink on `tertiary` and `ghost`.
- **The edge** of `tertiary` is a line of 2 in `muted`, not the theme's `border` hairline.
- **The title** is left-aligned (`headerTitleAlign: 'left'`), which iOS's native stack
  ignores.
- **The status bar** follows the bar's ground rather than the colour mode alone.
- **`mergeScreenOptions`** and its two types are not re-exported: import them from
  `@xaui/native/scaffold`.

# SearchField — @xaui/tram

A query, with the mark that says so and the cross that takes it back, drawn the Metro way:
one box holding the magnifier, the typed text and the cross, inside a line of 2 that takes
the accent with the focus.

It is a Tram `TextField`: the same root, `size`, `radius`, `accent`, `color`, `isInvalid`,
`isDisabled` and `isRequired`, and its `Label`, `Description` and `Error` are that
component's own slots.

## Import

```tsx
import { SearchField } from '@xaui/tram/search-field'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<SearchField>
  <SearchField.Label />
  <SearchField.Field>
    <SearchField.Icon />
    <SearchField.Clear />
  </SearchField.Field>
  <SearchField.Description />
  <SearchField.Error />
</SearchField>
```

- **`SearchField`** — the root, a `TextField` that holds the query.
- **`SearchField.Label`**, **`.Description`**, **`.Error`** — the `TextField`'s slots.
- **`SearchField.Field`** — the box and the text input in it. Its children are the marks:
  `SearchField.Icon` goes before the text, anything else after it. With none, the box
  draws the magnifier alone.
- **`SearchField.Icon`** — the magnifier, drawn from views in the box's line. `as`
  replaces it with an icon of your own; `size` and `color` override its side and ink.
- **`SearchField.Clear`** — the cross that empties the box: the Tram `CloseButton` drawn
  `text`, at the field's size. It renders nothing while the box is empty.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<SearchField onValueChange={setQuery} onSearch={run}>
  <SearchField.Label>artists</SearchField.Label>
  <SearchField.Field placeholder="search">
    <SearchField.Icon />
    <SearchField.Clear accessibilityLabel="clear the search" />
  </SearchField.Field>
  <SearchField.Description>by name or by album.</SearchField.Description>
</SearchField>
```

### Typing and searching

`onValueChange` fires on every keystroke and on the clear — what a list filtered in memory
reads. `onSearch` fires on the keyboard's search key — what a query that costs a request
waits for. Use `value` with `onValueChange` for a controlled query, or `defaultValue` and
let the field keep its own.

`SearchField.Field` takes what `TextField.Field` takes, less `value`, `defaultValue`,
`onChangeText` and `onSubmitEditing`, which are the root's. Its defaults are a search
box's: no autocorrect, no leading capital, a return key that says "search" — all yours to
override.

### The clear

A press on `SearchField.Clear` empties the query, reports it through `onValueChange`, and
hands the focus back to the text so the next query is typed straight away.

### The magnifier alone

```tsx
<SearchField>
  <SearchField.Field placeholder="search" />
</SearchField>
```

## Variants

| Variant     | Drawn as                                               |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `primary`   | the ground inside a line of 2 in `muted` — the default |
| `secondary` | the discreet surface with no line at rest              |

Under both, the line takes the accent with the focus, and the magnifier goes from `muted`
to the page's ink. `secondary` is for a search box on a sheet or a header.

```tsx
<SearchField variant="secondary" defaultValue="timbuktu">
  <SearchField.Field placeholder="search" />
</SearchField>
```

## Sizes

```tsx
<SearchField size="sm" />
<SearchField size="md" />
<SearchField size="lg" />
```

The box is 40, 48 or 56 tall. `sm` is pressed as 48 points.

## Colour

The line of the focus is the theme's accent, read as ink. `accent` picks another of the
twenty named accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins when both are set. `isInvalid`
draws the line in `danger`, focused or not, and outranks both; the label and the
description keep their ink. `radius` stays within 2.

## Accessibility

- The input has the `search` role and announces `disabled`. On the web it is labelled by
  `SearchField.Label` and described by `Description` and `Error`, with `aria-invalid` and
  `aria-required`.
- The magnifier is hidden from screen readers.
- `SearchField.Clear` is a cross, not text: it needs an `accessibilityLabel`.
- The line and the magnifier's ink move with the focus on the `navigation` spring, or a
  150 ms timing under reduced motion.

## Differences from Native

- **One box, no `FieldGroup`.** The marks are written inside `SearchField.Field`; Native
  composes a `FieldGroup` with a prefix and a suffix.
- **The magnifier** is drawn from views, so it needs no `react-native-svg`.
- **`variant`** keeps Native's two names, drawn flat: `primary` a line of 2 on the ground,
  `secondary` the discreet surface.
- **`accent`** is added. There is no `labelPlacement` (a Metro label stands above its box)
  and no `xs`.
- **`SearchField.Clear`** is the Tram `CloseButton` drawn `text`, pressed as 48.

# Select — @xaui/tram

A field that opens a list, drawn as the Metro list picker: the Tram `TextField`'s box,
which unfolds in place for up to five choices and pushes what is under it, or opens a page
of its own that swivels in for more.

Open, the border and the current choice are the accent read as ink; nothing else changes
colour.

## Import

```tsx
import { Select } from '@xaui/tram/select'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Select>
  <Select.Label />
  <Select.Trigger>
    <Select.Value />
    <Select.Indicator />
  </Select.Trigger>
  <Select.Overlay />
  <Select.Content>
    <Select.GroupLabel />
    <Select.Item>
      <Select.ItemLabel />
      <Select.ItemDescription />
      <Select.ItemIndicator />
    </Select.Item>
  </Select.Content>
  <Select.Description />
  <Select.Error />
</Select>
```

- **`Select`** — the root is the column — label, field, description, error — not the
  field. It holds the value and the open state.
- **`Select.Label`** — what the field is for. A touch on it opens the list; on a page it
  becomes the page's title.
- **`Select.Trigger`** — the field's row and the control a screen reader stops on.
- **`Select.Value`** — the chosen item's label, or `placeholder` until one is chosen.
  Children name the value when the root cannot read it off the items.
- **`Select.Indicator`** — the chevron at the end; it turns as the list opens. `as`,
  `size` and `color` override it.
- **`Select.Overlay`** — draws nothing. Around an unfolded list it closes the list on a
  touch above or below the box; `isDismissable={false}` leaves only a choice to close it.
  Omitted, a touch outside closes nothing.
- **`Select.Content`** — the list, inside the field or as a page.
- **`Select.GroupLabel`** — a heading over a run of choices.
- **`Select.Item`** — one choice, pressed like a control of 48. `label` is the string the
  field shows when the children are not one; `children` may be a function of
  `{ isSelected, isPressed, isDisabled }`.
- **`Select.ItemLabel`**, **`.ItemDescription`** — an item's line, and a second one in
  `muted`.
- **`Select.ItemIndicator`** — a mark beside the chosen item. It draws nothing unless
  given `as`: the current choice is read by its colour.
- **`Select.Description`**, **`.Error`** — the lines under the field.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Select defaultValue="fr" onValueChange={setLocale}>
  <Select.Label>language</Select.Label>
  <Select.Trigger>
    <Select.Value placeholder="choose a language" />
    <Select.Indicator />
  </Select.Trigger>
  <Select.Overlay />
  <Select.Content>
    <Select.Item value="fr">français</Select.Item>
    <Select.Item value="en">english</Select.Item>
  </Select.Content>
  <Select.Description>the interface's.</Select.Description>
</Select>
```

`value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange` and `isOpen` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange`
are each controlled or left to the root.

### In place or a page

Unset, the number of choices decides: five at most unfold inside the field, more open a
page. `mode` on `Select.Content` forces one or the other.

```tsx
<Select.Content mode="fullscreen" paddingTop={insets.top + 24}>
  {items}
</Select.Content>
```

A page starts at the very top of the screen and reads no safe area: pad it with the app's
own inset. On a page, the system's back closes the list unless `Select.Overlay` says
`isDismissable={false}`.

### Groups and a second line

```tsx
<Select.Content>
  <Select.GroupLabel>automatic</Select.GroupLabel>
  <Select.Item value="wifi" label="on wi-fi">
    <Select.ItemLabel>on wi-fi</Select.ItemLabel>
    <Select.ItemDescription>never on mobile data.</Select.ItemDescription>
  </Select.Item>
</Select.Content>
```

### Invalid and disabled

`isInvalid` draws the border in `danger`, open or not; the label and the description keep
their ink. `Select.Error` stays the caller's to mount. `isDisabled` greys the border, the
value and the label, and the select does not open. An item's own `isDisabled` greys it
and keeps it from being chosen.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Select size="sm" />
<Select size="md" />
<Select size="lg" />
```

The `TextField`'s heights — 40, 48 and 56 — so a select and a text field stacked in a form
read as one control. `size` never sets the width; `sm` is pressed as 48 points. `radius`
overrides the box's corner and stays within 2.

## Colour

The open border and the current choice are the theme's accent, read as ink. `accent`
picks another of the twenty named accents; `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins when
both are set.

```tsx
<Select accent="magenta">…</Select>
```

## Accessibility

- The trigger has the `combobox` role and announces `expanded` and `disabled`. On the web
  it carries `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-invalid`, and is labelled and
  described by the label, description and error.
- An item has the `option` role and announces `selected` and `disabled`.
- The list is a `listbox` on the web and a `list` on a phone, whose roles have no
  `listbox`.
- A choice is felt as a `selection` haptic through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`.
- The box unfolds and the border changes on the `navigation` spring; the page swivels in
  on its top edge and its choices arrive in cascade. Under reduced motion the height is
  set at once and the list fades.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`.** Native's four are four fills of the box; the Metro box has one — the
  ground inside a line.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **`mode`** (`inline` / `fullscreen`) is added on `Select.Content`, whose eight placement
  props — `placement`, `align`, `offset`, `alignOffset`, `avoidCollisions`, `insets`,
  `width`, `minWidth` — are dropped: the list is part of its field or the whole screen.
- **`Select.ItemIndicator`** draws nothing unless given `as`; Native draws a check.
- **Roles**: the trigger is a `combobox` and an item an `option`; Native uses `button`
  and `menuitem`.
- **Disabled** is grey, not dimmed, and does not open.
- **A touch on the label** opens the list.
- **`Select.Overlay`** closes on a touch above or below an unfolded list, not beside it;
  on a page, `isDismissable` is the system's back.
- **A page reads no safe area**: `Select.Content` is padded by the app.

# Skeleton — @xaui/tram

The shape of what has not arrived yet, drawn the Metro way: one flat, square block in a
fifth of the page's ink over its ground — `#333333` on black, `#CCCCCC` on white — that
breathes down to half and back.

## Import

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from '@xaui/tram/skeleton'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Skeleton />
```

- **`Skeleton`** — one node and no slots. A paragraph of placeholders is several of them
  in a column. There is no `size`: only the caller knows the shape of what is missing, so
  `width` and `height` are the whole sizing API.

## Usage

### A block

```tsx
<Skeleton width={140} height={20} />
<Skeleton width="70%" height={16} />
```

### A row it stands in for

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', gap: 12, alignItems: 'center' }}>
  <Skeleton width={52} height={52} />
  <View style={{ flex: 1, gap: 6 }}>
    <Skeleton height={12} width="50%" />
    <Skeleton height={12} width="80%" />
  </View>
</View>
```

### As a gate

```tsx
<Skeleton isLoading={!user} width={140} height={20}>
  <Typography>{user?.name}</Typography>
</Skeleton>
```

With `isLoading={false}` the block gives way to its `children`, rendered as they are: no
block style reaches them.

### The corner

```tsx
<Skeleton width={48} height={48} radius="full" />
```

Square by default, 2 at most, and `full` let through for a round avatar placeholder.

### The breath

The block breathes from full opacity down to half and back, 1100 ms each way, on one
clock shared by every block on the screen — a block mounted late joins in step.
`animation={false}` keeps it still and mounts no worklet.

## Colour

A placeholder carries no colour of the app: there is no `accent`. A block that has to
stand out on a particular ground takes a raw `color`, drawn as given.

```tsx
<Skeleton width={140} height={20} color="#2A2A2A" />
```

## Accessibility

- A block is hidden from screen readers (`accessibilityElementsHidden`,
  `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"`); announce loading as `busy` on the
  region that loads. Both stay overridable.
- Under reduced motion the block is still.

## Differences from Native

- **The drawing**: one flat, square block in a fifth of the page's ink; Native's is the
  theme's neutral fill with a rounded `md` corner.
- **`radius`** is square by default and stays within 2, with `full` let through.
- **The breath** runs 1 → 0.5 → 1 over 1100 ms each way on one shared clock, so blocks
  mounted at different times stay in step.
- **No `accent`**, as there is no `variant`. Native's props are otherwise unchanged.

# SlideButton — @xaui/tram

A button you drag rather than tap, drawn as the Metro lock screen: a rectangle in the
`Button`'s line, a block of the accent at its start, and a slide toward the end that fills
the whole box with the accent once it counts.

It is the confirmation for an action that must not happen by accident: `onConfirm` fires
once, when the thumb is let go past `threshold`.

## Import

```tsx
import { SlideButton } from '@xaui/tram/slide-button'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<SlideButton>
  <SlideButton.Fill />
  <SlideButton.Label />
  <SlideButton.Thumb>
    <SlideButton.Icon />
  </SlideButton.Thumb>
</SlideButton>
```

- **`SlideButton`** — the box. It measures itself and owns the drag and the confirmed
  state. A bare string composes the fill, the label and the thumb for you.
- **`SlideButton.Fill`** — the trail behind the thumb, the accent's soft slice up to the
  middle of the thumb. Leave it out for a bare box.
- **`SlideButton.Label`** — the instruction, centred across the box and kept clear of the
  thumb.
- **`SlideButton.Thumb`** — the block of the accent the finger drags. It draws a chevron
  pointing to the end, then a check once confirmed; children replace both.
- **`SlideButton.Icon`** — a mark in the thumb. `size` and `color` default to the thumb's.
  It takes `Icon`'s forms (`as`, a raw SVG child, or `source`).

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<SlideButton onConfirm={unlock}>slide to unlock</SlideButton>
```

### Composed

```tsx
<SlideButton onConfirm={lock} accessibilityLabel="slide to lock">
  <SlideButton.Fill />
  <SlideButton.Label>slide to lock</SlideButton.Label>
  <SlideButton.Thumb>
    <SlideButton.Icon as={LockIcon} />
  </SlideButton.Thumb>
</SlideButton>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<SlideButton isConfirmed={isReset} onConfirm={() => setIsReset(true)}>
  {isReset ? 'theme reset' : 'reset the theme'}
</SlideButton>
```

Uncontrolled, a confirmed slide stays confirmed (`defaultConfirmed` sets the start).
Controlled, set `isConfirmed` back to `false` to re-arm it; a caller that refuses the
confirm sends the thumb home.

### Threshold

```tsx
<SlideButton threshold={1}>all the way</SlideButton>
```

How far along the track the thumb has to reach, from 0 to 1 — `0.9` by default. Let go
short of it and the thumb springs home.

### The drag

The drag runs on `react-native-gesture-handler`, an optional peer. It takes only after 6
points sideways, so a vertical swipe stays the page's scroll. While held, the thumb
squashes a little.

## Sizes

```tsx
<SlideButton size="sm">sm</SlideButton>
<SlideButton size="md">md</SlideButton>
<SlideButton size="lg">lg</SlideButton>
```

The box is 48, 56 or 64 tall — a control height and 4 inside on each side — and the thumb
is a control height wide. `size` sets the label's type too (`subtitle` at `lg`), never the
width. `radius` sets the box and the thumb, capped at the Tram corner of 2, `full`
included.

## Colour

The thumb, the trail and the confirmed box are the theme's accent. `accent` picks another
of the twenty named accents; `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins when both are set. The
line at rest stays the page's ink. Once confirmed, the label turns to the ink that reads
on the accent (`onAccent`) and the thumb inverts round a check.

```tsx
<SlideButton color={theme.colors.danger} onConfirm={wipe}>
  slide to erase
</SlideButton>
```

`isDisabled` greys the line, the thumb and the label, and stops the drag.

## Accessibility

- The box is one accessible element with the `button` role and a `disabled` state.
- A screen reader cannot drag: the `activate` action confirms. The box is still not
  confirmed by a plain tap.
- On the web the box is a tab stop, and Enter or Space confirms it.
- The grab is felt as a `press` haptic and the confirmation as a `longPress`, through
  `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`.
- The chevron points to the end, mirrored right to left.
- Under reduced motion the thumb's squash is dropped and the fill-in is a short fade.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`.** One drawing: a line around the box and a block of the accent in it. A
  destructive slide is a raw `color`.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **The handle** is a flat block, not a shadowed pill, and the box is a rectangle under
  the Tram corner, never a pill.
- **A refused confirm**: a controlled caller that does not set `isConfirmed` sends the
  thumb home.
- **The root** is one accessible element, and Enter or Space confirms on the web.

# Slider — @xaui/tram

A value chosen along a line, drawn the Metro way: a line of soft grey, filled with the
accent up to a block thumb of ink — the `Switch`'s thumb, standing across the line.

## Import

```tsx
import { Slider } from '@xaui/tram/slider'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Slider>
  <Slider.Output />
  <Slider.Track>
    <Slider.Fill />
    <Slider.Thumb />
  </Slider.Track>
</Slider>
```

- **`Slider`** — the root. It holds the value, the scale and the motion the fill and the
  thumbs share.
- **`Slider.Output`** — the value as text: the number, or the two ends joined by an en
  dash on a range. A function child formats it.
- **`Slider.Track`** — the box the line is drawn in, and what a touch lands on. It holds
  the fill and the thumbs; it carries no margin.
- **`Slider.Fill`** — the filled part, in the accent: from the start to the thumb, or
  between two thumbs.
- **`Slider.Thumb`** — the block the finger holds. `index` says which: `0` on a plain
  slider, `0` and `1` on a range.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Slider defaultValue={40} onValueCommit={save}>
  <Slider.Output />
  <Slider.Track>
    <Slider.Fill />
    <Slider.Thumb />
  </Slider.Track>
</Slider>
```

A touch on the track brings the nearest thumb there; a drag carries it. `onValueChange`
fires on every step crossed, while dragging included; `onValueCommit` fires once, when the
finger lifts — what a network call belongs on.

### Formatting the output

```tsx
<Slider value={volume} onValueChange={setVolume}>
  <Slider.Output>{value => `volume ${value}`}</Slider.Output>…
</Slider>
```

### A range

```tsx
<Slider defaultValue={[20, 60]}>
  <Slider.Output />
  <Slider.Track>
    <Slider.Fill />
    <Slider.Thumb index={0} accessibilityLabel="minimum" />
    <Slider.Thumb index={1} accessibilityLabel="maximum" />
  </Slider.Track>
</Slider>
```

A pair makes it a range, and it comes back as a pair. The two thumbs do not cross.

### Scale and orientation

```tsx
<Slider defaultValue={40} min={0} max={200} step={10} orientation="vertical">
  <Slider.Track>
    <Slider.Fill />
    <Slider.Thumb />
  </Slider.Track>
</Slider>
```

`min` and `max` default to `0` and `100`, `step` to `1`; `step={0}` makes it continuous.
`vertical` counts from the bottom.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Slider size="sm" defaultValue={30}>…</Slider>
<Slider size="md" defaultValue={55}>…</Slider>
<Slider size="lg" defaultValue={70}>…</Slider>
```

`size` sets the line — 8, 12 or 16 thick — the thumb — as wide as the `Switch`'s, 18, 26
or 36 long — and the output's type. `radius` overrides the corner of the line, the fill
and the thumb; every key stays within 2.

## Colour

The fill is the theme's accent. `accent` picks another of the twenty named accents;
`color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins when both are set. The line stays the soft grey and
the thumb the page's ink.

```tsx
<Slider defaultValue={[20, 60]} step={10} accent="lime">
  …
</Slider>
```

`isDisabled` greys the line, the fill, the thumb and the output, and stops the touch.

## Accessibility

- Each thumb is an `adjustable` element with `{ min, max, now }`, and the `increment` and
  `decrement` actions. On the web it carries the `aria-value*` attributes and
  `aria-orientation`.
- `accessibilityValueText` on a thumb reads a text instead of the raw number; name the two
  thumbs of a range with `accessibilityLabel`.
- Each step is felt as a `selection` haptic through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`; a
  continuous slider has no step to feel.
- The thumb springs to a value through Tram's motion (150 ms under reduced motion). The
  squash of a held thumb is dropped under reduced motion.

## Differences from Native

- **The drawing**: a line of soft grey 8 / 12 / 16 thick and a block thumb of ink, the
  `Switch`'s.
- **`accent`** and **`asChild`** are added.
- **Haptics**: a `selection` per step, through `TramProvider`.
- **The line** is drawn inside the `Slider.Track` box, which carries no margin.
- **`useSlider`** reads Tram's own context. `fromFraction`, `snap` and `toFraction` are
  not exported.

# Spinner — @xaui/tram

The wait, drawn as Metro's progress ring: five round dots of the accent, piled into one,
set off one after the other — slow, fast over the top, slow again into the next meeting
point — where each is caught up by the next until the five are one dot again.

The dots meet at six, then seven, then eight, round the clock in twelve laps, and never go
out.

## Import

```tsx
import { Spinner } from '@xaui/tram/spinner'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Spinner />
```

- **`Spinner`** — one element: the ring and the five dots that run round it, drawn from
  the props. It has no slots and no `asChild` — the five dots are nodes a caller's
  element could not receive.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Spinner accessibilityLabel="loading messages" />
```

### Inline

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
  <Spinner size="sm" accessibilityLabel="syncing" />
  <Typography>syncing…</Typography>
</View>
```

### Standing still

```tsx
<Spinner animation={false} />
```

`animation={false}` stops the run and mounts no worklet: the five stand evenly round the
ring, so a list frozen this way keeps its height.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Spinner size="sm" />
<Spinner size="md" />
<Spinner size="lg" />
```

The ring is 20, 32 or 48 across, and the dots go with it.

## Colour

The dots are the theme's accent, as the `ProgressBar`'s bubbles are. `accent` picks
another of the twenty named accents, in its true colour; `color` takes a raw tint and wins
when both are set. A spinner in the page's ink is `color={theme.colors.foreground}`.

```tsx
<Spinner size="lg" accent="magenta" />
<Spinner color={theme.colors.foreground} />
```

## Accessibility

- The root has the `progressbar` role and announces as busy.
- There is no default label: only the caller knows what is loading, so give it an
  `accessibilityLabel`.
- Under reduced motion the five stand evenly round the ring and the ring turns slowly — a
  spinner that stopped would no longer say that something is on its way. Under an
  ancestor's `disable-all`, or with `animation={false}`, they stand still.

## Differences from Native

- **The drawing**: five dots running round a ring, where Native turns an arc.
- **No `variant`.** The dots are the accent; Native's seven variants are inks for the arc.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **The slots** are `root` and `dot`, for Native's `root` and `arc`.
- **Reduced motion** turns the five evenly round the ring; `animation={false}` stands them
  still.

# Stepper — @xaui/tram

Where you are in a sequence of steps, drawn from what Metro has — bars and type: no
circle, no check, no connector line. Each step is a bar at its start edge, a Light
numeral and its words; the bars stand 2 apart and read as one line cut into steps.

## Import

```tsx
import { Stepper } from '@xaui/tram/stepper'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Stepper>
  <Stepper.Item>
    <Stepper.Indicator />
    <Stepper.Content>
      <Stepper.Title />
      <Stepper.Description />
    </Stepper.Content>
  </Stepper.Item>
</Stepper>
```

- **`Stepper`** — the root. It numbers its items and hands each its status.
- **`Stepper.Item`** — one step: a row in a vertical stepper, so the bar runs the full
  height of its words; an equal share of the row in a horizontal one. Not pressable unless
  `asChild` merges it into a pressable child. A function child receives the step's
  `{ index, status, isFirst, isLast }`.
- **`Stepper.Indicator`** — the step's bar and its numeral. Children replace the numeral —
  an `Icon`, a letter — and the bar stays. In a horizontal stepper the bar is all there
  is.
- **`Stepper.Content`** — the step's words.
- **`Stepper.Title`** — the step's name. In progress it is a role larger, in the ink;
  ahead it is grey; done it keeps the ink.
- **`Stepper.Description`** — a grey line under the title.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Stepper value={2}>
  <Stepper.Item>
    <Stepper.Indicator />
    <Stepper.Content>
      <Stepper.Title>dates</Stepper.Title>
      <Stepper.Description>24 to 28 november</Stepper.Description>
    </Stepper.Content>
  </Stepper.Item>
  <Stepper.Item>
    <Stepper.Indicator />
    <Stepper.Content>
      <Stepper.Title>travellers</Stepper.Title>
    </Stepper.Content>
  </Stepper.Item>
</Stepper>
```

`value` is the step in progress, counted from one, and it is always the caller's: the
steps before it are `completed`, the ones after `upcoming`. Nothing moves on its own — a
stepper is a report.

### Horizontal

```tsx
<Stepper value={step} orientation="horizontal">
  {steps}
</Stepper>
```

The same bars lie end to end with a name under each; only the step in progress is in the
ink.

### Without the bars

```tsx
<Stepper hasConnector={false} value={2}>
  {steps}
</Stepper>
```

A step is then its numeral and its words.

### A step that takes you back

```tsx
<Stepper.Item asChild>
  <Pressable onPress={() => setStep(1)}>
    <Stepper.Indicator />
    <Stepper.Content>
      <Stepper.Title>dates</Stepper.Title>
    </Stepper.Content>
  </Pressable>
</Stepper.Item>
```

## Sizes

```tsx
<Stepper size="sm" value={2}>{steps}</Stepper>
<Stepper size="md" value={2}>{steps}</Stepper>
<Stepper size="lg" value={2}>{steps}</Stepper>
```

`size` sets the numeral — 24, 28 or 34 — and the title of the step in progress.

## Colour

The bars of the steps done are the theme's accent; the step in progress is the ink, and
the steps ahead the faint grey, their words grey too. `accent` picks another of the
twenty named accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins when both are set.

```tsx
<Stepper accent="orange" value={3}>
  {steps}
</Stepper>
```

## Accessibility

- The root has the `progressbar` role, with `{ min: 1, max, now: value }` — the number of
  steps and the step in progress.
- Steps are not pressable by default; one made pressable through `asChild` takes the role
  and label of its child.
- Nothing animates, so there is nothing for reduced motion to change.

## Differences from Native

- **The drawing**: bars and a Light numeral, where Native draws a circle, a check and a
  connector line.
- **`Stepper.Indicator`** draws the bar and the numeral.
- **`hasConnector={false}`** leaves the bars undrawn.
- **`accent`** is added. **No `xs`** and **no `asChild` on the root**; `Stepper.Item`
  keeps its `asChild`.
- The value and the statuses are Native's (`stepStatus`).

# Surface — @xaui/tram

A ground for other things to sit on, drawn flat: the discreet grey of the Tram design, or
the page inside a thin grey line — never a shadow.

One node and no slots: a fill, a corner and some padding. What goes on it is yours. Metro
laid its content on the ground, so a surface is the exception, not the frame.

## Import

```tsx
import { Surface } from '@xaui/tram/surface'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Surface />
```

- **`Surface`** — the root and its only node. It resolves the recipe and draws the ground;
  its children are laid in a column with the size's gap.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Surface>
  <Typography variant="body">on the discreet surface</Typography>
</Surface>
```

### Nested

A `secondary` inside a `primary` is drawn by its line, since there is no second grey.

```tsx
<Surface>
  <Typography variant="body">primary</Typography>
  <Surface variant="secondary" size="sm">
    <Typography variant="caption">secondary</Typography>
  </Surface>
</Surface>
```

### As child

`asChild` draws the ground on the element you pass instead of a `View`.

## Variants

Two grounds, under Native's first two names:

| Variant     | Drawn as                                  |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `primary`   | the discreet surface, a grey off the page |
| `secondary` | the page itself, inside a thin grey line  |

```tsx
<Surface variant="primary">…</Surface>
<Surface variant="secondary">…</Surface>
```

The line of `secondary` is 2 points in `muted`: an outline rather than a frame, softer than
the page's ink so it does not read as a control.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Surface size="sm">…</Surface>
<Surface size="md">…</Surface>
<Surface size="lg">…</Surface>
```

`size` moves the padding (12, 16, 20) and the gap — never a height. A surface is as tall as
what it holds. `radius` overrides the corner, within the Tram ceiling of 2.

## Colour

`accent` picks one of the twenty named accents. It fills a `primary` with its true colour,
and draws the line of a `secondary` as the mode's ink, so a yellow line still reads on a
white page. `color` takes a raw value, lands where `accent` does, wins over it and is
never corrected.

```tsx
<Surface accent="cobalt">
  <Typography variant="body" color="#FFFFFF">
    cobalt
  </Typography>
</Surface>
<Surface variant="secondary" color="#7c3aed">…</Surface>
```

The text on a filled surface is yours to colour: the surface does not pick an ink for it.

## Accessibility

- A surface is a plain `View` with no role. It reports nothing; give it a role or a label
  yourself when the group it draws means something to a screen reader.

## Differences from Native

- **`variant`** is `primary` or `secondary`. Native's grey `secondary` and its `tertiary`
  are dropped: one grey is all the design has, and the outlined ground takes the second
  name.
- **`isElevated`** is dropped: a Tram surface is never lifted off the page, and no variant
  has a shadow.
- **`accent`** is added: a fill in its true colour, or a line as the mode's ink.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg` and moves the padding and gap only; Native also has `xs`
  and its size moves the corner too.
- **The corner** stays within 2, the Tram radius scale.

# Switch — @xaui/tram

A setting that is on or off, drawn the Metro way: a rectangular track inside a line,
filled with the accent up to the middle of a block thumb that stands above and below it.

The root is the whole row, so a tap on the label flips the switch too. The thumb can also
be dragged: let go past the half, it turns on.

## Import

```tsx
import { Switch } from '@xaui/tram/switch'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Switch>
  <Switch.Label />
  <Switch.State />
  <Switch.Track>
    <Switch.Thumb />
  </Switch.Track>
</Switch>
```

- **`Switch`** — the root: the pressable row. It owns the state, resolves the recipe and
  hands the styles to its slots. A string child becomes a `Switch.Label` written before a
  default track and thumb.
- **`Switch.Label`** — the setting's name, in the size's type.
- **`Switch.State`** — the state written out, Metro's large `on` / `off` at the start of
  the row. It takes the two texts as `on` and `off` rather than children.
- **`Switch.Track`** — the rectangle the thumb slides on, with the accent filled from its
  start. The drag is caught here.
- **`Switch.Thumb`** — the block. Children are a glyph that travels with it.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Switch isSelected={isOn} onSelectedChange={setIsOn}>
  dark mode
</Switch>
```

### Uncontrolled

```tsx
<Switch defaultSelected>sync</Switch>
```

### Composed

JSX order is screen order: the Metro row reads from its start and ends on the switch.

```tsx
<Switch size="lg" accent="lime" defaultSelected>
  <Switch.Label>wi-fi</Switch.Label>
  <Switch.Track>
    <Switch.Thumb />
  </Switch.Track>
</Switch>
```

### State written out

A row whose only text is its state has no name to announce: give it an
`accessibilityLabel`.

```tsx
<Switch accessibilityLabel="wi-fi" justifyContent="space-between">
  <Switch.State on="on" off="off" />
  <Switch.Track>
    <Switch.Thumb />
  </Switch.Track>
</Switch>
```

Tram ships no language: the two words are the app's.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Switch size="sm">sm</Switch>
<Switch size="md">md</Switch>
<Switch size="lg">lg</Switch>
```

`size` drives the track, the thumb, the gap and the label's type; `lg` is Windows Phone's.
`sm` and `md` are drawn under 48 points, and a hit slop makes up the touch target.
`radius` overrides the corner of the track and thumb, within 2.

## Colour

The track fills with the theme's accent. `accent` picks one of the twenty named accents;
`color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` and wins when both are set. The fill is flat, so a named
accent is its true colour. The line and the thumb stay the page's ink.

```tsx
<Switch accent="magenta">notifications</Switch>
```

## Accessibility

- The root has the `switch` role, with `checked` and `disabled` in its state and
  `aria-checked` on the web. A caller's `accessibilityState` is merged, not replaced.
- A flip is felt through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`, as a `selection`.
- Under the finger the thumb squashes; with motion reduced it keeps its full size.
  `animation="disable-all"` also places the thumb with no slide.
- A disabled switch greys the track, the thumb and the label, and stops the press and the
  drag.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`**: Native's `primary` and `secondary` are two shapes of one control, and
  the Metro switch has one.
- **`accent`** is added: one of the twenty named accents.
- **`Switch.State`** is added: the state written out at the start of the row.
- **The label** is written before the track, not after it.
- **The thumb** is a block over a lined track, tapped or dragged. The drag uses
  `react-native-gesture-handler`, an optional peer.
- **The corner** stays within 2, the Tram radius scale.

# Table — @xaui/tram

Rows and columns drawn as the Metro settings page: no shell — no fill, line, corner or
shadow — just rows on the ground, with the column names in a grey `caption` and the sorted
one in the ink with a small chevron.

The rows are the `ListBox`'s settings rows: at least a control tall, with no separator
anywhere. A chosen row takes the accent's soft band under its ticked box.

## Import

```tsx
import { Table } from '@xaui/tram/table'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Table>
  <Table.ScrollContainer>
    <Table.Content>
      <Table.Header>
        <Table.SelectAllCell />
        <Table.Column />
      </Table.Header>
      <Table.Body>
        <Table.Row>
          <Table.SelectionCell />
          <Table.Cell />
        </Table.Row>
      </Table.Body>
    </Table.Content>
  </Table.ScrollContainer>
  <Table.Footer />
</Table>
```

- **`Table`** — the root. It clips, does not move, and holds the selection and the sort.
- **`Table.ScrollContainer`** — a horizontal `ScrollView` with no bar. The header scrolls
  with the body.
- **`Table.Content`** — the header and the body, one above the other. It may be wider than
  the root: give it a `minWidth`.
- **`Table.Header`** — the row of column names.
- **`Table.Column`** — one column's name, and the press that sorts on it. It declares the
  width (`width`, or an equal share) that the cells below read by position.
- **`Table.Body`** — the rows. It takes `asChild`, so a long table can be a `FlatList`.
- **`Table.Row`** — one row. With a `selectionMode` and an `id`, pressing it chooses it.
- **`Table.Cell`** — one value. A text child is set in `body` on one line; anything else
  is rendered as it is.
- **`Table.SelectAllCell`** — the header's box, the Tram `Checkbox`: nothing, some or all.
  It renders nothing outside `selectionMode="multiple"`.
- **`Table.SelectionCell`** — the row's box. It reads its row, so it can be written
  anywhere in it.
- **`Table.Footer`** — a count, an action, a pager. Outside the scroller, so a wide table
  never carries it off.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Table>
  <Table.ScrollContainer>
    <Table.Content>
      <Table.Header>
        <Table.Column>device</Table.Column>
        <Table.Column width={72}>MB</Table.Column>
      </Table.Header>
      <Table.Body>
        {devices.map(device => (
          <Table.Row key={device.id}>
            <Table.Cell>{device.name}</Table.Cell>
            <Table.Cell>{device.size}</Table.Cell>
          </Table.Row>
        ))}
      </Table.Body>
    </Table.Content>
  </Table.ScrollContainer>
</Table>
```

### Selection

`selectionMode` is `none`, `single` or `multiple`; rows are named by their `id`. `single`
replaces and a second press clears; `multiple` toggles. `disabledKeys` lists rows that
cannot be chosen, and the header's box does not count them.

```tsx
<Table selectionMode="multiple" selectedKeys={keys} onSelectionChange={setKeys}>
  …
  <Table.Row id={device.id}>
    <Table.SelectionCell />
    <Table.Cell>{device.name}</Table.Cell>
  </Table.Row>
</Table>
```

### Sorting

**The table never reorders anything.** A sortable column (`allowsSorting`, with an `id`)
reports the press through `onSortChange`, and the caller sorts. A new column starts
ascending, the same column turns round, and a third press clears the sort.

```tsx
<Table sortDescriptor={sort} onSortChange={setSort}>
  …
  <Table.Column id="name" allowsSorting>
    device
  </Table.Column>
</Table>
```

### Many rows

```tsx
<Table.Body asChild>
  <FlatList
    data={devices}
    keyExtractor={device => device.id}
    renderItem={({ item }) => <Table.Row id={item.id}>…</Table.Row>}
  />
</Table.Body>
```

## Sizes

```tsx
<Table size="sm">…</Table>
<Table size="md">…</Table>
<Table size="lg">…</Table>
```

`size` sets the rows' least height (40, 48, 56), the header's, the type and the boxes.

## Colour

The chosen rows' soft band and the marks of their boxes are the theme's accent. `accent`
picks one of the twenty named accents; `color` takes a raw tint and wins when both are
set. The sort mark stays the ink.

## Accessibility

- `Table.Header` has the `header` role.
- A sortable column is a `button`, `selected` while the data is sorted on it; its press
  reaches 48 points tall.
- A pressable row is a `button` with `selected` and `disabled` in its state. A plain row
  announces itself as nothing.
- A choice or a sort is felt through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`, as a `selection`.
- A pressable row leans toward the finger, its colours unchanged; with motion reduced, or
  under `disable-all`, it does not lean.
- `isDisabled` dims the whole table once and stops every press.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`**: Native's two are shell fills, and a Metro table has no shell.
- **No `radius`**: with no shell there is no corner to round.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **`accent`** is added: one of the twenty named accents.
- **No rules** under the header or between rows.
- **A chosen row** is the accent's soft slice rather than `defaultSoft`; the sort mark
  stays the ink.

# Tabs — @xaui/tram

The tabs of Metro: a row of titles with no ground, no box and no rule — the chosen one in
the page's ink, the others in grey, fading from one to the other.

When the titles are wider than the page the row scrolls sideways, with no bar, and brings
the chosen tab into view. The panel leaving fades out, and the next comes in from its
tab's side.

## Import

```tsx
import { Tabs } from '@xaui/tram/tabs'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Tabs>
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Trigger>
      <Tabs.Label />
    </Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Indicator />
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Content />
</Tabs>
```

- **`Tabs`** — the root. It holds the value and the row's record: the order of the tabs,
  and where each one lies.
- **`Tabs.List`** — the row of titles, a `ScrollView`. `style` is the row's frame;
  `contentContainerStyle` is where the titles are padded.
- **`Tabs.Trigger`** — one tab, named by `value`. `children` may be a function of
  `isSelected`, `isPressed` and `isDisabled`.
- **`Tabs.Label`** — the title, on `subtitle`, `title` or `section` by size. Its colour is
  the whole of the chosen state on screen. The case is the app's.
- **`Tabs.Indicator`** — an extra: a rule under the chosen title. Nothing is drawn unless
  it is written inside `Tabs.List`.
- **`Tabs.Content`** — the panel for one `value`. Only the chosen tab's panel is rendered.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="all">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="all">all</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="unread">unread</Tabs.Trigger>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Content value="all">…</Tabs.Content>
  <Tabs.Content value="unread">…</Tabs.Content>
</Tabs>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<Tabs value={tab} onValueChange={setTab}>
  …
</Tabs>
```

### With a rule

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="day" accent="cobalt">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="day">day</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="week">week</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Indicator />
  </Tabs.List>
</Tabs>
```

The rule is a line of the theme's border width, as wide as the title, and moves from one
tab to the next on the `navigation` spring.

### Disabled tab

```tsx
<Tabs.Trigger value="archive" isDisabled>
  archive
</Tabs.Trigger>
```

A disabled tab is grey, dimmed, and cannot be chosen. `isDisabled` on the root greys the
whole row and stops every press.

### Cascading content

A panel's content is not moved by the tabs. One that wants its rows in cascade reads
`travel` and `towardEnd` from `useTabs()` and moves them itself.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Tabs size="sm">…</Tabs>
<Tabs size="md">…</Tabs>
<Tabs size="lg">…</Tabs>
```

`size` sets the titles' type — `subtitle`, `title`, `section` — and a tab's height: 40,
48, 56. Every tab is pressed like a control of 48.

## Colour

Without `Tabs.Indicator`, no accent shows anywhere in the tabs. With one, `accent` (one of
the twenty named accents) is the rule's colour, read as ink; `color` takes a raw tint,
wins over it and is never corrected. `radius` sets the rule's corner, within 2.

## Accessibility

- `Tabs.List` is a `tablist`, each trigger a `tab` with `selected` in its state and
  `aria-selected` and `aria-controls` on the web.
- `Tabs.Content` is a `tabpanel`, named by its tab through `aria-labelledby`.
- On the web the arrow keys go from tab to tab, past a disabled one, with one tab stop for
  the row.
- A press shrinks the title and leaves its colour alone. With motion reduced the title's
  fade and the panel swap are short; under `disable-all` everything is set, nothing moves.
- The indicator is hidden from screen readers.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`**: Native's three are three grounds for the row.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **No rule without `Tabs.Indicator`**. Written, it is under the chosen title, as wide as
  its label, in the accent read as ink; `accent`, `color` and `radius` touch nothing else.
- **`Tabs.List`** is a `ScrollView` (its ref and its props) where Native's is a `View`.
- **`Tabs.Content`** is a `tabpanel` named by its tab, and a trigger carries
  `aria-controls`.
- **A disabled tab** is grey and dimmed.
- **`useTabs`** exposes `travel` and `towardEnd` for a content that cascades by hand.
- Tabs are ordered as they mount: one added later in the middle counts as last.

# TextArea — @xaui/tram

A field of several lines with its label, its hint and its error: the Tram `TextField` on
several lines, the ground inside a 2-point line of ink, its text starting at the top.

It is a `TextField`. The root is the Tram `TextField`'s, unchanged — the same `size`,
`radius`, `accent`, `color`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isRequired` and `asChild` — and
`Label`, `Description` and `Error` are its slots. Only the field differs, by being
multiline and by taking its height in lines.

## Import

```tsx
import { TextArea } from '@xaui/tram/text-area'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<TextArea>
  <TextArea.Label />
  <TextArea.Field />
  <TextArea.Description />
  <TextArea.Error />
</TextArea>
```

- **`TextArea`** — the root: the column. It takes `rows` and `maxRows`, where the field's
  shape is decided.
- **`TextArea.Label`** — the `TextField`'s label. A touch on it gives the field the focus.
- **`TextArea.Field`** — the multiline `TextInput`. It takes everything
  `TextField.Field` takes except `multiline`, which it sets.
- **`TextArea.Description`** — the `TextField`'s hint, in the muted ink.
- **`TextArea.Error`** — the `TextField`'s error, in `danger` read as ink. Mounting it is
  the caller's condition.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<TextArea>
  <TextArea.Label>message</TextArea.Label>
  <TextArea.Field value={message} onChangeText={setMessage} />
  <TextArea.Description>three lines are enough.</TextArea.Description>
</TextArea>
```

### Rows

`rows` is how many lines tall the field starts (3 by default). The field grows with what
is typed up to `maxRows`, then scrolls; without `maxRows` it grows for as long as the text
goes on. A `height` in the field's `style` is the height it keeps.

```tsx
<TextArea rows={2} maxRows={5}>
  <TextArea.Label>comment</TextArea.Label>
  <TextArea.Field />
</TextArea>
```

### Invalid

```tsx
<TextArea isInvalid={isTooShort} isRequired>
  <TextArea.Label>reason</TextArea.Label>
  <TextArea.Field value={reason} onChangeText={setReason} />
  {isTooShort ? (
    <TextArea.Error>write at least ten characters.</TextArea.Error>
  ) : null}
</TextArea>
```

The border and the error are `danger`; the label and the description keep their ink.

### Disabled

```tsx
<TextArea isDisabled>…</TextArea>
```

The border, the text and the label turn grey, and the field takes no focus.

## Sizes

```tsx
<TextArea size="sm">…</TextArea>
<TextArea size="md">…</TextArea>
<TextArea size="lg">…</TextArea>
```

`size` sets the type and the padding, with lines 22, 26 and 32 tall. `rows` counts the
box's line and padding as well as its lines.

## Colour

As on the `TextField`: the focused border is the theme's accent read as ink, `accent`
picks one of the twenty named accents, and `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` that wins when
both are set. Neither applies while `isInvalid`.

## Accessibility

- The field is named by the label and described by the description and the error, as on
  the `TextField`; `isInvalid`, `isDisabled` and `isRequired` reach the input.
- The focus is the border alone, on a spring; with motion reduced it is a short fade.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`**: the Metro box has one fill — the ground, inside a line.
- **No `labelPlacement`**: the label stands above its box.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **`accent`** and **`isRequired`** are added.
- **`rows`** counts the box's line as well as its padding.

# TextField — @xaui/tram

A text field with its label, its hint and its error, drawn the Metro way: the ground inside
a 2-point line of ink, and the line in the accent once the field has the focus.

The root is the column, not the field: `TextField.Field` is the `TextInput` and takes its
props. A touch on the label gives the field the focus.

## Import

```tsx
import { TextField } from '@xaui/tram/text-field'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<TextField>
  <TextField.Label />
  <TextField.Field />
  <TextField.Description />
  <TextField.Error />
</TextField>
```

- **`TextField`** — the root: the column. It resolves the recipe and holds the state the
  slots read — invalid, disabled, required — and the ids that tie them together.
- **`TextField.Label`** — what the field is for, in the page's ink, above the box.
- **`TextField.Field`** — the `TextInput` itself. It takes everything `TextInput` takes
  except `editable`, which is `isDisabled` on the root.
- **`TextField.Description`** — the hint under the field, in the muted ink.
- **`TextField.Error`** — what is wrong with the value, in `danger` read as ink. It always
  renders what it is given: mounting it is the caller's condition.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<TextField>
  <TextField.Label>email</TextField.Label>
  <TextField.Field
    value={email}
    onChangeText={setEmail}
    keyboardType="email-address"
  />
  <TextField.Description>we never share it.</TextField.Description>
</TextField>
```

### Invalid

`isInvalid` draws the border in `danger`, focused or not. The label and the description
keep their ink.

```tsx
<TextField isInvalid={Boolean(error)}>
  <TextField.Label>password</TextField.Label>
  <TextField.Field secureTextEntry />
  {error ? <TextField.Error>{error}</TextField.Error> : null}
</TextField>
```

### Disabled and read-only

```tsx
<TextField isDisabled>…</TextField>

<TextField>
  <TextField.Label>account</TextField.Label>
  <TextField.Field readOnly value={account} />
</TextField>
```

A disabled field greys the border, the text and the label, and cannot be edited. A
`readOnly` field greys nothing and keeps its selection: its text can be copied.

### Several lines

A field on several lines is its own component: `TextArea`, from `@xaui/tram/text-area`.

## Sizes

```tsx
<TextField size="sm">…</TextField>
<TextField size="md">…</TextField>
<TextField size="lg">…</TextField>
```

`size` drives the field's height (40, 48, 56), its padding, the gaps and the type — never
the width. A box drawn under 48 gets a hit slop that makes up the touch target. `radius`
overrides the corner, within 2.

## Colour

The focused border is the theme's accent, read as ink: a line has to stand out on the
ground. `accent` picks one of the twenty named accents; `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB`,
used as written, and wins when both are set. Neither applies while `isInvalid`.

```tsx
<TextField accent="lime">…</TextField>
```

A `borderColor` written on `TextField.Field` replaces the line, focused or not.

## Accessibility

- The field is named by the label (`aria-labelledby`) and described by the description
  and the error (`aria-describedby`), each slot carrying its own id.
- `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isRequired` and `readOnly` reach the input as
  `aria-invalid`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-required` and `aria-readonly`. `isRequired` draws
  nothing.
- The focus is the border alone, moving on a spring; with motion reduced it is a short
  fade.

## Differences from Native

- **No `variant`**: Native's four are four fills of the box, and the Metro box has one —
  the ground, inside a line.
- **No `labelPlacement`**: a Metro label stands above its box.
- **`size`** is `sm`, `md` or `lg`; Native also has `xs`.
- **`accent`** and **`isRequired`** are added.
- **The line** is 2 points of ink, the `Button`'s, not the theme's 3.
- **A touch on the label** gives the field the focus.
- **`isInvalid`** leaves the label and the description their ink.
- **Disabled** is grey, not dimmed.
- **No `TextField.TextArea`** slot: several lines are the `TextArea` component.
- **`TextField.Error`** carries an id the field is described by.

# Tile — @xaui/tram

The live tile of the Metro start screen — icon, shortcut and widget in one square: a flat
fill of the accent that can carry a count, a name, a picture, and turn over to a second
face.

The tile is Tram's own: it has no Native equivalent. `Tile.Grid` lays tiles out as the
start screen did, each in the first hole it fits.

## Import

```tsx
import { Tile, useTileFace } from '@xaui/tram/tile'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Tile.Grid>
  <Tile>
    <Tile.Image />
    <Tile.Front>
      <Tile.Icon />
      <Tile.Count />
      <Tile.Label />
    </Tile.Front>
    <Tile.Back />
  </Tile>
</Tile.Grid>
```

- **`Tile`** — the root: a pressable square. A text child is the tile's name, written as a
  `Tile.Label`.
- **`Tile.Front`**, **`Tile.Back`** — the two faces, for a tile that turns over. Only the
  face that shows is read by a screen reader.
- **`Tile.Label`** — the tile's name, in the caption role, on one line, truncated.
- **`Tile.Count`** — what a small tile has to say (unread mail, missed calls), in the title
  role, with digits of one width.
- **`Tile.Icon`** — a glyph at the tile's size, in the colour that reads on its fill. An
  explicit `size` or `color` wins.
- **`Tile.Image`** — a picture in place of the fill, on the tile or on one face, cropped
  to it.
- **`Tile.Grid`** — the start screen: square cells, as wide as its parent.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Tile size="small" onPress={openMail}>
  <Tile.Icon as={MailIcon} />
  <Tile.Count>7</Tile.Count>
</Tile>
```

### Two faces

The tile never turns on its own: the app holds `face`. `useTileFace(interval, isPaused)`
gives a cadence; give each tile its own interval, and pause it when the screen is out of
sight.

```tsx
const face = useTileFace(4000, !isFocused)

<Tile size="medium" face={face} onPress={openWeather}>
  <Tile.Front>
    <Tile.Count>29°</Tile.Count>
    <Tile.Label>weather</Tile.Label>
  </Tile.Front>
  <Tile.Back>
    <Tile.Label>storms near 5 pm</Tile.Label>
  </Tile.Back>
</Tile>
```

`transition="flip"` (the default) turns the tile over on the `tile` spring;
`transition="slide"` slides one face out as the other follows it in.

### Picture

What is written over a picture is set in white on a black band across the foot of the
square. `hasBand={false}` leaves the band out, for a photo already dark where the text
goes.

```tsx
<Tile size="wide">
  <Tile.Image source={cover} />
  <Tile.Label>music</Tile.Label>
</Tile>
```

### Grid

```tsx
<Tile.Grid columns={tramTileColumns.phone}>
  <Tile size="medium">…</Tile>
  <Tile size="small">…</Tile>
  <Tile size="wide">…</Tile>
</Tile.Grid>
```

`columns` is 4 by default — `tramTileColumns` (from `@xaui/tram/theme`) gives 4, 6 and 8
for a phone, a tablet and an open foldable. `gap` is in points. Each child's `size` is
read to place it, so a component wrapping a `Tile` has to take `size` and hand it down.
`placeTiles` exposes the placement on its own.

### The app's own text

`useTile()` returns `foreground`, the colour that reads on the tile, for text that is not
a `Tile.Label` or a `Tile.Count`.

## Variants

| Variant     | Drawn as                                       |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `contained` | filled with the true colour                    |
| `flat`      | filled with its soft slice, the accent as ink  |
| `surface`   | the discreet surface — `accent` paints nothing |

Metro filled every tile with the accent; Tram spends it on a few and lets the rest sit
back.

## Sizes

| Size     | Cells     |
| -------- | --------- |
| `small`  | 1         |
| `medium` | 4 (2 × 2) |
| `wide`   | 8 (4 × 2) |

Not `sm` / `md` / `lg`: a wide tile is not a large one, it is a medium one twice as long.
Outside a grid a tile is as wide as it is told to be.

## Colour

The fill is the theme's accent. `accent` picks one of the twenty named accents; `color`
takes a raw `#RRGGBB` — the fill of a `contained`, the slice of a `flat` — and wins when
both are set. A `surface` tile has no accent to repaint.

## Accessibility

- The root has the `button` role; a disabled tile announces its state.
- Only the face that shows is exposed to a screen reader; the other is hidden.
- A picture says nothing to a screen reader: the tile is the button, its label the name.
- A press leans the tile toward the finger and is felt through `TramProvider`'s
  `onHaptic`. With motion reduced, nothing turns or travels: one face fades into the
  other.

# TimePicker — @xaui/tram

A field that opens a page of wheels, drawn as the Metro time picker: the `TextField`'s box
with the time in it, and a page that swivels in on its top edge with a column of hours,
one of minutes and, on a twelve-hour clock, the half of the day.

**Nothing is chosen while the wheels turn.** The wheels stand on a draft: ✓ makes it the
value and fires `onValueChange`; ✕ and the system's back leave the value as it was.

## Import

```tsx
import { TimePicker } from '@xaui/tram/time-picker'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<TimePicker>
  <TimePicker.Label />
  <TimePicker.Field />
  <TimePicker.Overlay />
  <TimePicker.Content>
    <TimePicker.Wheel />
  </TimePicker.Content>
  <TimePicker.Description />
  <TimePicker.Error />
</TimePicker>
```

- **`TimePicker`** — the root: the column holding the label, the field and the help lines.
- **`TimePicker.Label`** — what the time is for. It also titles the page.
- **`TimePicker.Field`** — the trigger and its value in one tag. `placeholder` is shown
  while nothing is chosen.
- **`TimePicker.Trigger`**, **`TimePicker.Value`**, **`TimePicker.Indicator`** — the
  field taken apart, for a field composed by hand. `Indicator` draws nothing unless given
  a glyph through `as`.
- **`TimePicker.Overlay`** — draws nothing; `isDismissable={false}` keeps the system's
  back from closing the page.
- **`TimePicker.Content`** — the page: the label as its title, the wheels, and the App
  Bar's ✓ and ✕ along the bottom, named by `confirmLabel` and `cancelLabel`.
- **`TimePicker.Wheel`** — the columns, a Tram `WheelPicker`. It is what the page holds
  when `Content` is given no children.
- **`TimePicker.Description`**, **`TimePicker.Error`** — the hint and the error under the
  field.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<TimePicker value={time} onValueChange={setTime}>
  <TimePicker.Label>alarm</TimePicker.Label>
  <TimePicker.Field placeholder="choose a time" />
  <TimePicker.Content confirmLabel="ok" cancelLabel="cancel" />
</TimePicker>
```

`value` keeps its day: the wheels change its hours and minutes, and drop its seconds.

### Clock and locale

The clock is the locale's unless `hourCycle` (`12` or `24`) says otherwise, and so is the
order of the columns — the half of the day comes first in Korean. The field reads the
time through `Intl`; `formatOptions` changes how.

```tsx
<TimePicker locale="fr-FR" hourCycle={12} defaultValue={noon}>
  <TimePicker.Label>start</TimePicker.Label>
  <TimePicker.Field />
  <TimePicker.Content />
</TimePicker>
```

The hours and minutes loop: 12 · 1 … 11 on a twelve-hour clock, 00 … 23 on a 24-hour one.

### Minute step

```tsx
<TimePicker minuteStep={5}>…</TimePicker>
```

A step that does not divide the hour is fitted to the nearest one under it that does
(7 → 6, 45 → 30). A time between two squares stands on the one under it.

### Wheel

`TimePicker.Wheel` takes the `WheelPicker`'s own props — `variant`, `size`,
`visibleCount`, `isAwake`, the style props — but not its colour or disabled state, which
are the picker's.

```tsx
<TimePicker.Content>
  <TimePicker.Wheel variant="light" />
</TimePicker.Content>
```

### Open state

`isOpen`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange` control the page.

## Sizes

```tsx
<TimePicker size="sm">…</TimePicker>
<TimePicker size="md">…</TimePicker>
<TimePicker size="lg">…</TimePicker>
```

`size` sets the field's height and type, and the side of the squares on the page.
`radius` overrides the field's corner, within 2.

## Colour

`accent` picks one of the twenty named accents: the field's line while the page is open,
read as ink, and the current squares' fill. `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` for the same two
places and wins when both are set.

## Accessibility

- The field is a `button` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, named by the label and
  described by the description and the error.
- The page is a modal `dialog` titled by the label; ✓ and ✕ are `button`s named by
  `confirmLabel` and `cancelLabel` (`done` and `cancel` by default).
- `isDisabled` greys the line, the value and the label, and the picker does not open.
  `isInvalid` draws the line in `danger`; the label keeps its ink.

## Differences from Native

- **The root is the column**, not a node-less provider, and adds `Label`, `Field`,
  `Description` and `Error`: the label titles the page, as the Metro "choose time" did.
- **`Sheet`** is replaced by `Content`, a page rather than a bottom sheet.
- **`Display` and `Clock`** are replaced by `Wheel`: the squares are the display.
- **`Overlay`** is added, carrying `isDismissable`.
- **No `variant`** and **no `closeOnSelect`**: one box, and nothing is chosen until ✓.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **`Indicator`** draws nothing unless given a glyph; Native's is a clock.

# Timeline — @xaui/tram

What happened, in order, drawn as the Windows Phone timeline: each entry opens on a flat
tile of its date, and a line drops from one tile to the next, with the title and the
description beside it.

The tile is painted by the entry's `status`. The root counts its children so the line
