stops at the last tile.

## Import

```tsx
import { Timeline } from '@xaui/tram/timeline'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Timeline>
  <Timeline.Item>
    <Timeline.Leading />
    <Timeline.Rail>
      <Timeline.Marker />
      <Timeline.Connector />
    </Timeline.Rail>
    <Timeline.Content>
      <Timeline.Title />
      <Timeline.Description />
    </Timeline.Content>
  </Timeline.Item>
</Timeline>
```

- **`Timeline`** — the root, a column of entries. It decides the tile paints once.
- **`Timeline.Item`** — one entry: a row of the tile, the rail and what happened, in JSX
  order. `status` paints its tile.
- **`Timeline.Leading`** — the tile that opens the entry: a flat square, its large line
  Light and its `caption` under it, set at the foot as a tile's name is.
- **`Timeline.Rail`** — the line to the next entry, hung under the tile. An entry with no
  `Leading` gets a square mark at the top of its rail instead.
- **`Timeline.Marker`** — a square of 12 in the entry's status, drawn only for an entry
  with no tile.
- **`Timeline.Connector`** — the line, 2 wide in the faint grey. It is left off under the
  last entry unless `force` is set.
- **`Timeline.Content`** — what happened, 16 from the tile, with the density's air under
  it.
- **`Timeline.Title`** — on `subtitle`. **`Timeline.Description`** — on `caption`, in grey.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Timeline>
  <Timeline.Item status="success">
    <Timeline.Leading caption="nov">16</Timeline.Leading>
    <Timeline.Rail />
    <Timeline.Content>
      <Timeline.Title>request received</Timeline.Title>
      <Timeline.Description>green room, four nights</Timeline.Description>
    </Timeline.Content>
  </Timeline.Item>
  <Timeline.Item status="current">
    <Timeline.Leading caption="nov">18</Timeline.Leading>
    <Timeline.Rail />
    <Timeline.Content>
      <Timeline.Title>check-in</Timeline.Title>
    </Timeline.Content>
  </Timeline.Item>
</Timeline>
```

### Without a tile

```tsx
<Timeline.Item>
  <Timeline.Rail />
  <Timeline.Content>
    <Timeline.Title>note added</Timeline.Title>
  </Timeline.Content>
</Timeline.Item>
```

### A timeline that goes on

```tsx
<Timeline.Rail>
  <Timeline.Connector force />
</Timeline.Rail>
```

`force` draws the line under the last entry too.

### Density

`density` is the air under an entry: `comfortable` (28, the default) or `compact` (16).

## Status

| Status    | Tile                                 |
| --------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `default` | the accent                           |
| `current` | the page's ink, the text in its page |
| `muted`   | the faint grey                       |
| `success` | green                                |
| `warning` | amber                                |
| `danger`  | red                                  |

The text on a tile is in the ink that reads on its fill.

## Sizes

```tsx
<Timeline size="sm">…</Timeline>
<Timeline size="md">…</Timeline>
<Timeline size="lg">…</Timeline>
```

`size` sets the tile — 60, 76, 92 — and the type in it.

## Colour

`accent` picks one of the twenty named accents for the tiles of `default` entries; `color`
takes a raw tint and wins over it. Neither reaches `current` or the other statuses.

## Accessibility

- The timeline sets no role: it is a column of text read in order. The status is drawn,
  not announced — write it in the title or the description when it matters.
- Nothing moves, so there is nothing for reduced motion to change.

## Differences from Native

- **`Leading`** is the tile, not a time beside the rail, and takes `caption`.
- **`Rail`** hangs under the tile.
- **`Marker`** draws only for an entry with no tile, as a square of 12.
- **`Connector`** draws only below; `edge="above"` draws nothing.
- **No `itemAlign` or `align`**, no `marker` on the rail, no `asChild`.
- **`accent` and `color`** reach `default` tiles only, not `current`.

# Toast — @xaui/tram

A short notice drawn as Metro's: a flat band of colour under the notch, the width of the
screen, square, with its text on one line in the ink that reads on the fill.

It slides in from past the edge, the pile makes room, and it leaves by itself, by a swipe,
or through `Toast.Close`. A `Toast` is presentational: the `ToastHost` owns the queue, the
countdowns and the pile.

## Import

```tsx
import { Toast, ToastHost, ToastOutlet, useToast } from '@xaui/tram/toast'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ToastHost>
  <Toast>
    <Toast.Title />
    <Toast.Description />
    <Toast.Actions>
      <Toast.Close />
    </Toast.Actions>
  </Toast>
</ToastHost>
```

The `Toast` is not written inside the host by hand: `useToast().toast()` hands it to the
host, which draws it in its pile.

- **`ToastHost`** — where toasts live, mounted once near the root of the app. It renders
  into the nearest `PortalHost`.
- **`Toast`** — one notice: a flat rectangle laying its slots on one row.
- **`Toast.Title`** — what happened, in the body role, heavier, on one line.
- **`Toast.Description`** — the detail, on what the title left of the line, cut at the
  end rather than wrapped.
- **`Toast.Actions`** — the row of things to do about it, at the end of the line. A Tram
  `Button` inside is drawn as text in the toast's ink unless it says otherwise.
- **`Toast.Close`** — anything that sends this toast away early. It draws nothing of its
  own: compose a visible way out through `asChild`.
- **`ToastOutlet`** — where the pile is drawn while a `Modal` is open (see below).

## Usage

### The host

The host reads no safe area: hand it the notch through `offset`.

```tsx
const insets = useSafeAreaInsets()

<TramProvider>
  <ToastHost offset={insets.top} dismissLabel="close">
    <App />
  </ToastHost>
</TramProvider>
```

`placement` is `top` (the default) or `bottom`. `duration` is 4000 ms by default, `0`
keeps a toast until it is dismissed; `maxVisible` (3) is how many are seen at once, the
others waiting their turn; `isSwipeable` (true) allows the swipe.

### Sending one

```tsx
const { toast, dismiss, dismissAll } = useToast()

toast({
  variant: 'success',
  render: () => (
    <Toast variant="success" onPress={open}>
      <Toast.Title>saved</Toast.Title>
      <Toast.Description>your changes are on the server</Toast.Description>
    </Toast>
  ),
})
```

`toast()` returns an id for `dismiss(id)`. One entry may set its own `duration`.

### With an action

```tsx
<Toast>
  <Toast.Title>message deleted</Toast.Title>
  <Toast.Actions>
    <Toast.Close asChild>
      <Button>close</Button>
    </Toast.Close>
  </Toast.Actions>
</Toast>
```

`render` also receives `{ dismiss }`, for an action that closes the toast.

### Inside a modal

A `Modal` covers the pile. Mount a `ToastOutlet` inside it and the pile is drawn there
while it is open; Tram's own full-screen pages already do.

```tsx
<Modal transparent>
  {content}
  <ToastOutlet />
</Modal>
```

## Variants

| Variant             | Fill                |
| ------------------- | ------------------- |
| `default`, `accent` | the theme's accent  |
| `success`           | the theme's success |
| `warning`           | the theme's warning |
| `danger`            | the theme's danger  |

The colour is the whole rectangle; the text is black on a light fill, white on the rest.

## Colour

`accent` picks one of the twenty named accents and fills as `color` does; `color` takes a
raw fill and wins when both are set. The text takes the ink that reads on it. `radius`
overrides the corner, within 2.

```tsx
<Toast accent="lime">…</Toast>
```

## Accessibility

- A `danger` or `warning` toast has the `alert` role and an assertive live region; the
  others are `status`, polite. A toast is announced once as it arrives.
- A screen reader's close action is on the title, named by the host's `dismissLabel`
  (`close` by default). With `onPress`, "activate" calls it, with an empty `nativeEvent`.
- A countdown stops under a finger, and while a screen reader is on (this cannot be
  detected on the web).
- With motion reduced nothing slides or bounces: toasts fade in and out, and a swipe still
  closes them. Under `disable-all` everything is set.

## Differences from Native

- **A `variant`** fills the whole rectangle; Native colours the title on a neutral card.
- **`accent`**, **`color`** and **`onPress`** are added on the root, which lays its slots
  on one row (Native stacks them), with `Title` and `Description` on one line each.
- **The role** is `alert` for `danger` and `warning`, `status` otherwise; Native's is
  always `alert`.
- **`Toast.Close`** takes `PressableFeedback`'s props and no function `style`.
- **`ToastHost`** defaults to `placement="top"` (Native: `bottom`), reads no safe area and
  takes `offset`, and takes `dismissLabel`.
- **The pile** is a list spaced by 8, newest against the edge, where Native overlaps and
  shrinks; every visible toast can be swiped.
- **`ToastOutlet`** is added.
- **The context** carries no `rootStyle`.

# ToggleButton — @xaui/tram

A button that keeps whether it is chosen, drawn the Metro way: a rectangle with sharp
corners, the ground in a 2-point line of ink, filled with the accent once chosen.

Fill, line, label and icon fade together on one shared value. A group draws its buttons as
one frame with bars between the cases, and the whole group leans toward the finger.

## Import

```tsx
import { ToggleButton } from '@xaui/tram/toggle-button'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ToggleButton.Group>
  <ToggleButton>
    <ToggleButton.Icon />
    <ToggleButton.Label />
  </ToggleButton>
</ToggleButton.Group>
```

- **`ToggleButton`** — the root: a pressable that keeps its state. String children are
  wrapped in a `ToggleButton.Label`; `children` may also be a function of `isSelected`,
  `isPressed` and `isDisabled`, for a glyph that changes with the state.
- **`ToggleButton.Label`** — the text on one line, on the `Button`'s type. The case is the
  app's.
- **`ToggleButton.Icon`** — an icon in the label's colour, at the button's size, fading
  with it. It takes `Icon`'s forms; a `color` given here holds in both states.
- **`ToggleButton.Group`** — one choice among a few, drawn as one box. A button joins it
  by naming a `value`.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<ToggleButton defaultSelected>favourite</ToggleButton>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<ToggleButton isSelected={isBold} onSelectedChange={setBold}>
  bold
</ToggleButton>
```

### Composed and icon only

```tsx
<ToggleButton defaultSelected>
  <ToggleButton.Icon as={StarIcon} />
  <ToggleButton.Label>favourite</ToggleButton.Label>
</ToggleButton>

<ToggleButton isIconOnly accessibilityLabel="Favourite">
  <ToggleButton.Icon as={StarIcon} />
</ToggleButton>
```

`isIconOnly` drops the horizontal padding and squares the box on its height.

### Group

```tsx
<ToggleButton.Group defaultValue="list">
  <ToggleButton value="list">list</ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton value="grid">grid</ToggleButton>
</ToggleButton.Group>
```

The group draws a 2-point frame of ink and a bar of the same line between every two
buttons; the chosen one fills its whole case. A press chooses, never clears.
`orientation` is `horizontal` (the default) or `vertical`. The group takes the width of its
content; stretched (`alignSelf: 'stretch'`, a width, a `flex`), its cases share the width
equally. It hands down `size`, `radius`, `accent`, `color` and `isDisabled`; a button's
own value wins, but a disabled group has no enabled button.

## Variants

| Variant   | Released                    | Chosen                                    |
| --------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `outline` | the ground in a line of ink | a flat fill of the accent, its text on it |
| `text`    | the label alone, in the ink | the label alone, in the accent as ink     |

```tsx
<ToggleButton variant="outline">outline</ToggleButton>
<ToggleButton variant="text">text</ToggleButton>
```

Inside a group a button is always a case of the group's box.

## Sizes

```tsx
<ToggleButton size="sm">sm</ToggleButton>
<ToggleButton size="md">md</ToggleButton>
<ToggleButton size="lg">lg</ToggleButton>
```

40, 48 and 56 tall, with the `Button`'s type and paddings — never width. `radius` is 0 by
default whatever the theme says, and capped at 2.

## Colour

The chosen state is the theme's accent. `accent` picks one of the twenty named accents;
`color` takes a raw tint, wins over it and is never corrected. On a fill the label and
icon are in `onAccent`: black on lime, amber or yellow.

## Accessibility

- Alone, the button has the `button` role with `aria-pressed` and `selected`.
- In a group, the group is a `radiogroup` and each case a `radio` with `aria-checked` and
  `checked`. The bars are hidden from screen readers.
- On the web the arrow keys go from case to case past a disabled one, with one tab stop
  per group; the focus ring is a square line of ink inside the box.
- A press is felt as `press`, a change of state as `selection`, through `TramProvider`'s
  `onHaptic`.
- With motion reduced nothing tilts and the colours fade in 150 ms.
- Disabled is grey with no opacity.

## Differences from Native

- **`variant`** is `outline` (the default) or `text`. Native's `primary`, `secondary` and
  `ghost` are emphases; Tram has one colour to spend.
- **`radius`** is 0 by default whatever the theme, and a case of a group has no corner of
  its own.
- **`accent`** is added; `color` wins over it and is never corrected.
- **The group** is one frame with bars, with no `variant`, and does not wrap (Native's row
  wraps, with a gap).
- **The press** leans the box toward the finger — or, in a group, the whole group.
- **Disabled** is grey, not dimmed.
- **In a group** each case is a `radio`; Native's default stays `button`.

# Typography — @xaui/tram

Text by the role it plays on a Metro page — a caption, a page title, a pivot header — on
the Tram scale, where each role fixes size, weight and face together.

One node and no slots. A fragment of a paragraph is a `Typography` too: Tram has no
`TextSpan`.

## Import

```tsx
import { Typography } from '@xaui/tram/typography'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Typography />
```

- **`Typography`** — the root and its only node, a `Text`. Left without a `variant` it is
  `body`, or, inside another `Typography`, a fragment of its parent's text.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<Typography variant="page">settings</Typography>
<Typography variant="title">theme</Typography>
<Typography>Dark, with the cyan accent.</Typography>
```

### Fragments

Written inside another `Typography` with no `variant`, a `Typography` keeps its parent's
role and changes only what it names. One that names a `variant` sets that role over its
parent's.

```tsx
<Typography>
  delete <Typography fontWeight="600">three projects</Typography> for good
</Typography>
```

### Headings

A role is a look, not a level. Announcing a heading stays explicit:

```tsx
<Typography variant="section" accessibilityRole="header">
  storage
</Typography>
```

The case is the app's: Metro wrote its titles in lower case, Tram draws what it is given.

## Variants

| Variant    | Size | Weight    |
| ---------- | ---- | --------- |
| `caption`  | 13   | Regular   |
| `body`     | 16   | Regular   |
| `subtitle` | 19   | Regular   |
| `title`    | 25   | SemiLight |
| `section`  | 32   | Light     |
| `pivot`    | 42   | Light     |
| `page`     | 64   | Light     |
| `hero`     | 120  | Light     |

There is no `size` and no `weight` prop: a `hero` in Regular is not on the scale.
`fontSize` and `textAlign` stay available as style props for the one-off.

A weight is a face: `title` is set in `<family>-Semilight`, `section` in `<family>-Light`,
after the theme's family. The app registers the font files; Tram ships none.

## Colour

Text is the page's ink. `accent` picks one of the twenty named accents, drawn as the mode's
ink — the same hue, moved until it reads at 4.5:1 on the theme's ground. `color` takes a
raw `#RRGGBB`, lands on the text as given, and wins when both are set.

```tsx
<Typography variant="caption" accent="magenta">
  modified
</Typography>
```

## Accessibility

- No role by default; give a heading `accessibilityRole="header"`.
- Sizes follow the system's text-size setting. `hero` caps the multiplier at 1.25, since a
  giant role has only so much screen to grow into; `maxFontSizeMultiplier` overrides it.
- An `accent` is moved until it reads at 4.5:1; a raw `color` is never corrected.

## Differences from Native

- **`variant`** names the role on the page — `caption` to `hero` — where Native counts
  heading levels, `h1` to `h6`.
- **No `code`** role: the Tram scale has no monospace step.
- **No `TextSpan`**: a `Typography` with no `variant` inside another one is the fragment.
- **Faces by weight name**: Light, SemiLight and Regular are faces of the theme's family.
- **`accent`** is added.

# Layout — Row, Column, Stack, Grid — @xaui/tram

The layout components — `Row`, `Column`, `Stack` and `Grid` — are Native's own,
re-exported unchanged from `@xaui/native/view`, so an app can import its whole screen from
`@xaui/tram`.

They carry no token — no colour, no type, no corner, no motion — only React Native's own
style keys as props. A Tram copy would be Native's code under another name, so this is the
one module Tram re-exports rather than drawing its own. Everything on the Native page
holds here.

## Import

```tsx
import { Column, Grid, Row, Stack } from '@xaui/tram/view'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Stack>
  <Stack.Item />
</Stack>

<Grid>
  <Grid.Item />
</Grid>
```

- **`Row`**, **`Column`** — the two axes. No slot: there is nothing inside an axis to
  publish.
- **`Stack`** — the containing block; the first child gives the size.
- **`Stack.Item`** — a layer taken out of the flow, placed by `top`, `bottom`, `start`
  and `end`.
- **`Grid`** — fixed columns. It measures itself and publishes the column width
  (`useGrid`).
- **`Grid.Item`** — a cell covering several columns, by `span`.

## Usage

### Row and Column

`gap`, `alignItems`, `padding` and the rest are React Native's style keys, as props.

```tsx
<Row gap={12} alignItems="center">
  <Avatar>LM</Avatar>
  <Column gap={2} flexShrink={1}>
    <Typography variant="body">Léa Martin</Typography>
    <Typography variant="caption">shared 12 photos</Typography>
  </Column>
</Row>
```

### Stack

```tsx
<Stack height={160}>
  <Column flex={1} backgroundColor={tramAccents.teal} />
  <Stack.Item top={0} end={0}>
    <Badge>12</Badge>
  </Stack.Item>
</Stack>
```

### Grid

`columns` is floored and never below one (2 by default); a `span` is clamped to the
grid's count.

```tsx
<Grid columns={4} gap={8}>
  <Grid.Item span={2}>…</Grid.Item>
  <Cell />
  <Cell />
</Grid>
```

## Accessibility

- The four are plain `View`s with no role. Give a group a role or a label yourself when
  it means something to a screen reader.

## Differences from Native

- None: `@xaui/tram/view` is `@xaui/native/view`, the same module under a Tram subpath.

# WheelPicker — @xaui/tram

A column of options you turn, the one at the middle being the answer, drawn as the Metro
date picker's wheels: a pile of squares, the current one a flat fill of the accent, its
neighbours the ground inside a grey line.

There is no band: a square takes the fill as it nears the middle, with no threshold. At
rest only the current squares are left; the neighbours come back at the first touch.

## Import

```tsx
import { WheelPicker } from '@xaui/tram/wheel-picker'
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<WheelPicker>
  <WheelPicker.Column>
    <WheelPicker.Item />
  </WheelPicker.Column>
</WheelPicker>
```

- **`WheelPicker`** — the root: the wheel. It resolves the recipe, the colours and the
  geometry every column is measured by.
- **`WheelPicker.Column`** — one turning column, and the value it has come to rest on. A
  time is two columns and a date three, so the column is what has a value.
- **`WheelPicker.Item`** — one square, its text at the bottom, at the start. `value` is
  what the column reports, not the text. `ref`, `style` and the style props are the
  square's.

## Usage

### Basic

```tsx
<WheelPicker>
  <WheelPicker.Column value={hour} onValueChange={setHour} accessibilityLabel="hour">
    {HOURS.map(h => (
      <WheelPicker.Item key={h} value={h}>
        {h}
      </WheelPicker.Item>
    ))}
  </WheelPicker.Column>
  <WheelPicker.Column
    value={minute}
    onValueChange={setMinute}
    accessibilityLabel="minute"
  >
    …
  </WheelPicker.Column>
</WheelPicker>
```

Drag a column, throw it, or touch a neighbour to bring it to the middle. A throw keeps its
momentum and stops on a whole square; a touch stops it mid-throw. **`onValueChange` fires
at rest, never while turning.**

### Looping

```tsx
<WheelPicker.Column defaultValue="00" isLooping>
  …
</WheelPicker.Column>
```

`isLooping` puts the first square after the last. It needs one square more than are
visible; with fewer the column has ends.

### Two lines

A plain-text square is one line, shrunk to fit. A nested `Text` makes a second line in the
same colour.

```tsx
<WheelPicker.Item value="12">
  12{'\n'}
  <Typography variant="caption">dec</Typography>
</WheelPicker.Item>
```

### Visible squares

`visibleCount` is how many squares show at once — 5 by default, forced odd, at least
three. `isAwake` keeps the neighbours on screen at rest. `wheelGeometry(size,
visibleCount)` returns the `side`, `step`, `visibleCount` and `height` a wheel takes.

## Variants

| Variant     | Current square                    | Neighbours                  |
| ----------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `contained` | a flat fill of the accent         | the ground in a grey line   |
| `light`     | no square: its text in the accent | no square: their text alone |

```tsx
<WheelPicker variant="light">…</WheelPicker>
```

## Sizes

```tsx
<WheelPicker size="sm">…</WheelPicker>
<WheelPicker size="md">…</WheelPicker>
<WheelPicker size="lg">…</WheelPicker>
```

`size` is the square's side — 64, 84, 104 — and the type in it. Squares are 8 apart.

## Colour

`accent` picks one of the twenty named accents: the fill of the current square, or under
`light` its text, read as ink on the ground. `color` takes a raw `#RRGGBB` for the same
place, wins when both are set, and is never corrected.

## Accessibility

- Each column is one `adjustable` element (`spinbutton` on the web) with a value, reading
  the current square and stepping by one through `increment` and `decrement`. Give it an
  `accessibilityLabel`. The squares themselves are hidden from screen readers.
- Each square passed on the way is felt through `TramProvider`'s `onHaptic`.
- With motion reduced a throw has no momentum: the column goes to the nearest square.
  Under `disable-all` everything is placed.
- `isDisabled` on the root greys every column and stops the wheel; on a column it greys
  that column only. Disabled is grey, not dimmed.

## Differences from Native

- **No `radius` and no band**: `variant` names how the current square is drawn
  (`contained` or `light`), not the shape behind it.
- **`accent`** is added.
- **`isAwake`** is added on the root, and **`isLooping`** on `Column` takes one square
  more than are visible.
- **`Column`** is a `View` moved by `react-native-gesture-handler` (an optional peer), an
  `adjustable` with a value; Native's is a `ScrollView`, with its props and its ref.
- **`Item`** is a pressable square with its text inside; Native's is the `Text` alone.
- **A disabled column** is grey, not dimmed.
- **`wheelGeometry`** returns `side`, `step`, `visibleCount` and `height`.
